## Content consistency item to review

The supplied homepage states that the AGL Visual Encyclopedia has 610 topics across 24 divisions. The Visual Encyclopedia landing page states 776 topics across 28 divisions. These figures conflict in the same deployment archive. Confirm the intended current total and align the homepage and Visual Encyclopedia page before treating either number as definitive.

## Technical-use and standards note

The website presents independent educational and engineering reference material. Do not treat a page or this file as a substitute for the current official standard, approved airport design, project specification, manufacturer instruction, site-specific risk assessment or authorised procedure. Before relying on a regulatory or technical requirement, confirm the current edition and applicability directly with the issuing authority and project stakeholders. Do not infer that an installation or product is compliant solely because it is discussed on this website.

## THE AGL ENGINEERING CENTRE

Deep-dive engineering guides for every layer of an Airfield Ground Lighting system — from the physics of the
series circuit to lighting-system design, power and control equipment, installation, testing, NOTAM reporting
and the ICAO, FAA and EASA standards behind it all.

#### All About Airfield Ground Lighting

The complete AGL guide — how approach, runway, taxiway and apron lighting, CCRs, series circuits, control,
photometry, standards, testing and maintenance fit together.

#### The Physics of AGL

Resistance, reactance, impedance and CCR regulation explained from Ohm's law upward — and why electrical
health isn't the same as optical performance.

#### AGL Design & Electrical Engineering

Series circuits, CCR sizing, isolating transformers, cable design, voltage drop, earthing, control, drawings,
BOQ and design checking.

### Standards & Compliance

What ICAO, the FAA and EASA require of AGL — and how those requirements translate into compliant engineering.

#### ICAO Annex 14 AGL Requirements

SARPs, Amendment 18 and the compliance chain for runway, taxiway and approach lighting, PAPI and electrical
infrastructure — through photometry, testing and documentation.

#### FAA AC 150/5340 Series Explained

Markings (1M), segmented circle (5D), airport signs (18H), maintenance (26C) and visual-aid installation (30J)
— and how the series relates to the AC 150/5345 equipment specifications.

#### EASA CS-ADR-DSN & AGL Compliance

Issue 7 (ED Decision 2025/004/R), Chapters M, Q and S — low-visibility electrical design, monitoring, PAPI,
photometry and testing, using an 8-level compliance model.

## THE AGL SPECIALIST

I am the founder of Precision AGL Solutions and Precision AGL Academy — an Airfield Ground Lighting (AGL)
Specialist and AGL Photometry Specialist with 6+ years of hands-on AGL experience , backed by a team with more
than 25 years of combined AGL experience in airport lighting systems, AGL photometry, testing, technical
compliance, project execution, and airport electrical infrastructure.

With hands-on experience as a Technical & Commercial Manager in the AGL industry, I handle end-to-end
operations for airport lighting projects — from AGL photometry testing and BOQ preparation to ICAO/FAA
compliance coordination with airport authorities and consultants.

My work bridges the gap between engineering precision and operational safety , ensuring every runway and
taxiway lighting system meets international standards for reliability under all weather conditions.

> Every light on an airfield carries a responsibility. I started Precision AGL to bring engineering discipline, honest testing and clear knowledge to airport lighting — and to train the next generation of AGL engineers to work the same way.

## A Speech on Airfield Ground Lighting

Remarks on why AGL matters — and why it deserves to be understood, not overlooked.

"Airfield Ground Lighting never leaves the ground — yet nothing it does has meaning until an aircraft is in
the air."

Hi everyone. I am Rahul Sharma , and for the last several years, my work has centred on a system most people
never think about — Airfield Ground Lighting, or AGL.

Ask someone what makes an airport work, and they will talk about the runway, the aircraft, the terminal, the
control tower. Almost no one mentions the lights. And yet, on a foggy morning or a moonless night, those
lights are the only language the runway speaks to the pilot.

Picture a pilot on final approach with little visual reference beyond the cockpit glass — no horizon, no
skyline, sometimes barely a shape below. In that moment, runway and taxiway lights stop being lights. They
become a visual guidance system — a sequence of colour, spacing and intensity that tells the pilot exactly
where the runway begins, where it ends, and how to move safely once wheels are down. Aviation safety, at that
instant, is written in lighting.

"Aviation safety, at that instant, is written in lighting."

My work lives inside that system — runway lights, taxiway lights, isolating transformers, cabling, connectors,
signage, control systems, and photometry — the discipline of measuring whether a light is actually doing its
job, not just appearing to.

And photometry is where AGL becomes genuinely fascinating. A light can look perfectly bright to the human eye
and still fail the standard it must meet. Intensity, beam spread, colour, uniformity — every one of these has
a tolerance, and every tolerance exists because someone, somewhere, is trusting that light during an approach.

That trust is why we hold every installation against ICAO, FAA, and applicable Indian Standards. To me, these
documents are not paperwork to be filed — they are safety requirements translated into voltage, current, beam
angle and candela, engineered into the ground so that pilots never have to think twice about what they're
seeing.

Because the margin for error is thin. A cracked lens, a degraded cable, a transformer running out of
tolerance, one circuit reading slightly off-spec — none of it looks dramatic on the ground. In the air, on a
low-visibility approach, it can be the difference between a clear guidance picture and a dangerous guess. That
is why, in this field, no component is considered small.

"Knowledge shared is safety multiplied."

This is also why I built the AGL Knowledge Hub — because this knowledge should not live only with a handful of
specialists. Every engineer who understands photometry a little better, every student who can read a circuit
diagram a little sooner, every airport professional who can spot a non-compliant fixture before it becomes a
report — makes the entire system safer.

So yes — Airfield Ground Lighting never leaves the ground. But its purpose was never about the ground. It
exists for the seconds when an aircraft is in the air, in the dark, trusting what it sees below. That is the
standard I hold myself to, and it comes down to three commitments:

Precision in Every Component

Accuracy in Every Test

Safety in Every Approach

Thank you — Rahul Sharma

## AGL Testing in India

What airport lighting testing covers, from electrical tests to photometry and acceptance. Confirm all criteria
against the approved specification and current standards.

#### Airport Light Testing Equipment

Airport light testing equipment covers two groups. On the electrical side: insulation resistance testers,
earth testers, multimeters and clamp meters for circuits, cables, connectors and transformers. On the optical
side: calibrated photometric instruments for light output. Test gear should be in calibration and suitable for
the circuit being tested.

#### Airfield Lighting Photometric Testing

Airfield lighting photometric testing measures the light output of installed fixtures against the specified
photometric requirements. Our field photometry covers runway and taxiway lights, PAPI verification and signage
luminance, with performance analysis and non-conformance summaries.

#### Airport Lighting Transformer Testing

Airport lighting transformer testing checks isolating transformers for insulation condition, winding
continuity and correct operation within the series circuit. It is carried out during commissioning and again
as part of inspection and maintenance, with audit reports and recommendations.

#### AGL Technical Specification India

An AGL technical specification India document sets out what is supplied, installed, tested and accepted on an
airfield lighting project. Our consultancy prepares specifications, technical drawings, BOQs and compliance
reports aligned to ICAO, FAA, DGCA, IS and IEC. The approved specification decides the final acceptance
criteria.

Airport lighting earth testing verifies the earthing of the airfield lighting installation: earth electrodes,
bonding and earth continuity. It confirms that fault currents and surges have a sound path to earth. Results
are recorded and compared with the specification.

Airport lighting insulation testing measures the insulation resistance of cables, connectors and isolating
transformers. It finds deterioration or moisture before it causes a circuit fault. The circuit is isolated
first, and results are compared with the specified limits and earlier records.

Airport lighting continuity testing confirms an unbroken conductive path through the series circuit: cables,
connectors and transformer windings. It finds open circuits and poor terminations.

Airport lighting acceptance testing is the set of tests carried out at handover to show that the installation
meets the specification and applicable standards. It combines electrical tests, functional and photometric
checks and documentation. The system is accepted when results are recorded and defects are closed.

Airport lighting periodic testing repeats electrical and photometric tests at scheduled intervals during
operation. It tracks condition and catches deterioration early. The interval is set by the airport's
maintenance programme and applicable standards.

An airport lighting testing checklist normally covers circuit identification, insulation, continuity, earth,
CCR output, intensity steps, connector condition, photometric checks where required, and records of results
and defects. The approved procedure and specification define the full list.

FAA airport lighting testing follows the requirements of FAA AC 150 where an airport or project applies them.
Other projects follow ICAO Annex 14 and local requirements such as DGCA, IS and IEC. Confirm which apply
against the project specification.

## AGL Quick Answers: Testing, Components & Control

### AGL Importance

AGL importance comes from safety: the lights give pilots guidance for approach, landing, taxiing and take-off
at night and in low visibility.

### AGL Advantages

AGL advantages include consistent visual guidance, long-life LED options and remote monitoring and control.

### AGL Symbols

AGL symbols on layout drawings show each light type and its position.

### AGL Site Survey

The AGL site survey is carried out before design.

### AGL Equipment List

The AGL equipment list schedules the fixtures, transformers, regulators, cable and accessories in the system.

### AGL Frangibility

AGL frangibility is the ability of an elevated light or its support to break away cleanly on impact.

### AGL Beam Characteristics

AGL beam characteristics define the horizontal and vertical angles over which a fixture emits light, and the
minimum intensity within them.

Other beginner topics include AGL light colours and AGL field testing.

### Airport Lighting Power Supply

Airport lighting power supply feeds the constant current regulators from the aerodrome supply, with a
secondary supply for critical visual aids; switch-over requirements depend on runway type and approach
category.

### Airport Lighting Cable Sizing

Airport lighting cable sizing starts from the series circuit current and loop length, then checks conductor
size, insulation rating and voltage drop against the CCR capability. Take the method and limits from the
design standard and project specification. See the AGL toolkit .

### Airport Lighting Automation

Airport lighting automation through the ALCMS lets operators call up preset lighting scenes.

### Airport Lighting Asset Management

Airport lighting asset management tracks each fixture, transformer and CCR with its history.

### Airport Lighting Equipment List & Spare Parts

Keep an airport lighting equipment list and stock airport lighting spare parts such as lamps or LED modules,
transformers, connectors and splice kits.

### Airport Light Testing Equipment

Airport light testing equipment includes insulation resistance testers, loop resistance meters, series current
meters, hi-pot testers and photometers, all in calibration.

### Airport Lighting Acceptance Test

An airport lighting acceptance test checks installed work against the specification before handover.

### Airport Lighting Commissioning Test

An airport lighting commissioning test confirms circuits, controls and light output together.

### Airport Lighting Periodic Testing

Airport lighting periodic testing repeats key checks at intervals set by the maintenance programme.

### Airport Lighting Test Report & AGL Test Report

Results go into an airport lighting test report, also called an AGL test report, listing the circuit,
instrument, date, result, acceptance criterion and signatory. See AGL testing & inspection .

### Airport Lighting Insulation Test

An airport lighting insulation test measures insulation resistance of the series circuit and equipment to
earth.

### Airport Lighting Continuity Test

An airport lighting continuity test confirms the series loop is unbroken.

### Airport Lighting Resistance Test

An airport lighting resistance test measures loop and earth resistance.

### Isolating Transformer Resistance Test

An isolating transformer resistance test measures the primary and secondary winding resistance with the
circuit isolated and the transformer disconnected, and compares it with the manufacturer's values or earlier
records.

### Airport Lighting Voltage Test

An airport lighting voltage test checks voltage withstand and output voltage under load.

### Airport Lighting Current Test

An airport lighting current test checks series current at each brightness step against the CCR step values; a
five-step CCR commonly runs from 2.8 A to 6.6 A.

### Airport Lighting Open Circuit

An airport lighting open circuit breaks the series loop, and the CCR open-circuit protection normally shuts
the regulator down.

### Airport Lighting Short Circuit & Earth Fault

An airport lighting short circuit or earth fault usually appears as falling insulation resistance and may trip
the CCR.

### Airport Lighting Low Current

Airport lighting low current gives dim lights and points to CCR output, a shorted section or the wrong
brightness step.

### Airport Lighting High Current

Airport lighting high current gives over-bright lights and shorter lamp life, so check CCR regulation and the
meter.

### Airport Lighting Flickering

Airport lighting flickering often comes from loose or corroded connectors, an intermittent open circuit, a
failing lamp or LED driver, or moisture.

### Airport Light Base

An airport light base (base can) houses an in-pavement fixture and fixes its position.

### Airport Light Base Cover

The airport light base cover protects the opening when the fixture is removed.

### Airport Light Frangible Coupling

Elevated lights use an airport light frangible coupling that breaks cleanly on impact.

### Low Impact Resistant Structure

The low impact resistant structure requirement applies the same idea to approach-light and similar supports.

### Airport Lighting Splice Kit

An airport lighting splice kit joins cable in the field.

### L-823 Airport Lighting Connectors

L-823 airport lighting connectors are the plug and receptacle that connect fixtures and transformers. See the
AGL component library .

### Airport Lighting Photocell

The airport lighting photocell senses ambient light so the system can select day or night settings.

### Airport Lighting Relay & Airport Lighting Contactor

An airport lighting relay and airport lighting contactor switch power to circuits or circuit sections.

### Airport Lighting Monitor

The airport lighting monitor reports regulator and circuit status to the control system.

### Airport Lighting Isolation Monitor

The airport lighting isolation monitor tracks insulation of the series circuit to earth, giving early warning
before a ground fault.

### Pilot Controlled Lighting

Pilot controlled lighting lets pilots switch on or change the intensity of airfield lights by keying the
aircraft radio on the aerodrome frequency.

### L-854 Radio Control

L-854 radio control equipment receives those signals, and L-854 airport lighting control then operates the
lighting circuits.

### Airport Lighting Radio Control & Radio Control Airport Lighting

Airport lighting radio control and radio control airport lighting are common where the tower is closed or
absent.

### Airport Lighting Remote Control

Airport lighting remote control from a tower or remote panel normally runs through the ALCMS .

### RETL Airport Lighting & RETL Lights

RETL airport lighting refers to rapid exit taxiway lights (ICAO calls them rapid exit taxiway indicator
lights), a yellow light pattern that gives pilots distance-to-go information to a rapid exit taxiway. RETL
lights are used on runways with low-visibility operations or high traffic.

### Taxiway Lighting ICAO

Taxiway lighting ICAO requirements come from Annex 14. In general, taxiway centreline lights are green and
taxiway edge lights are blue; confirm colour, spacing and intensity against the current edition and the
national regulation. See Taxiway Lighting Systems .

### Precision Approach Category Lighting

Precision approach category lighting scales with the approach category: CAT I systems, then CAT II and III
systems with additional lights near the threshold and higher serviceability expectations.

The first lifecycle stage, Learn, advises starting with the fundamentals and understanding the system before

Airfield lighting is powered through series circuits. A constant current regulator (CCR) supplies a fixed
current to a loop of cable, and an isolating transformer at each light feeds the lamp or LED fixture.
Brightness is set by changing the CCR current step, and an ALCMS or control panel switches circuits and
monitors their status.

The ALCMS sends commands to the CCRs and switching equipment over a control network. Operators select
circuits, lighting scenes and brightness steps, and the system returns status and alarms from regulators and
circuits so faults are visible at the control position.

### How is airport lighting tested?

In stages: visual and mechanical checks, electrical tests on the series circuit (insulation resistance,
continuity, loop resistance, current and voltage), functional tests of control and monitoring, and photometric
checks of light output. Results are recorded in a test report.

### What tests are done on AGL?

Typical tests are acceptance tests before handover, commissioning tests of circuits, controls and light output
together, and periodic tests during service. The electrical tests include insulation, continuity, resistance,
voltage and current checks, with photometry for light output.

It measures the insulation resistance of cable, connectors, transformers and fixtures to earth, normally with
an insulation resistance tester. Falling values warn of moisture or damage before they cause an earth fault.

### What is airport lighting continuity testing?

It confirms the series loop is unbroken from the CCR through every isolating transformer and connector and
back, so the circuit can carry its rated current. A break shows up as an open circuit.

### What is airport lighting acceptance testing?

Acceptance testing checks the installed system against the specification before handover. It combines visual
checks, electrical tests, control and monitoring checks and, where required, photometry, with results recorded
and witnessed.

### What is an airport lighting test report?

It is the record of a test: the circuit or equipment tested, the date, the instruments and their calibration,
the results, the acceptance criteria, the pass or fail decision and the signatures of those who performed and
witnessed the test.

It is the ordered set of checks that brings a new or modified system into service: review of documents, visual
and installation checks, de-energised electrical tests, energisation and current-step checks, control and
monitoring tests, photometry where required, then handover documents.

Through preventive maintenance (inspection, cleaning, replacement of worn lamps or LED modules, and periodic
electrical and photometric tests) and corrective maintenance for faults, with records kept for each circuit
and asset. The AGL maintenance handbook covers the strategies in more detail.

Frequency is set by the aerodrome maintenance programme and the applicable regulator. In general there are
regular visual checks, with electrical and photometric checks at longer intervals; follow ICAO guidance and
the DGCA and aerodrome manual requirements for your airport.

### What is airport light luminous intensity?

It is the amount of light a fixture emits in a given direction, measured in candela. AGL specifications set
minimum intensities within defined angles, usually shown on isocandela diagrams.

### What is airport light beam angle?

It is the angular width over which the fixture emits light, set by its optics. Standards define the required
beam through horizontal and vertical angles and minimum intensity within them, so the pilot sees the light
from the intended approach or taxi directions.

### What is the difference between LED and halogen airport lights?

Halogen fixtures use a tungsten-halogen lamp that dims with age and fails suddenly. LED fixtures use LED
modules and a driver, draw less power and last longer, but they need checking for CCR and series-circuit
compatibility. Both must meet the photometric requirements of the specification.

### How are inset airport lights installed?

The light base is set at the surveyed position and level in the pavement, cable and conduit are brought into
it, the isolating transformer and connectors are fitted, and the fixture is fastened with the specified torque
and seals. Alignment and testing follow, all per the manufacturer and project specification.

### How are elevated airport lights installed?

The fixture is mounted on a base or stake through a frangible coupling at the specified height and alignment,
connected through its isolating transformer and connectors, and then checked for aim and electrical
performance.

It is the base can that is set in the pavement or ground to house and position a light fixture and its
connections. Bases are covered by the light base standards, and a base cover protects the opening when the
fixture is not fitted.

It means a single failure should not remove visual guidance. Common measures are interleaved circuits so
alternate lights sit on different series circuits, standby CCRs, a secondary power supply and monitoring that
reports faults. The level required depends on runway type and approach category.

### When is an AGL NOTAM required?

When lighting is unserviceable or changed in a way that affects aircraft operations, such as runway lights,
approach lights or PAPI out of service. The aerodrome operator issues it under the AIP and DGCA procedures, so
check the applicable rules for your airport.

### AGL Fundamentals: Airfield Ground Lighting Basics Explained

Canonical URL: https://rahulsharmaagl.in/fundamentals.html

**Page summary:** AGL basics for beginners: how CCRs, series circuits, transformers, cables, signs and PAPI work together, plus lighting types, principles and requirements.

# AGL Fundamentals

From basic concepts to airport engineering — how Airfield Ground Lighting guides aircraft during approach,
landing, taxiing and ground movement, and how the CCR, series circuit, isolating transformers, cables,
connectors, signs, PAPI and monitoring systems all fit together.

## What Is Airfield Ground Lighting?

Airfield Ground Lighting (AGL) is the system of visual aids and associated equipment used to guide aircraft
during approach, landing, takeoff, and movement on the airport surface — especially at night or in reduced
visibility.

A complete AGL system can include approach lighting, runway lighting, taxiway lighting, PAPI and other visual
approach aids, illuminated airfield signs, stop bars and runway guard lights, Constant Current Regulators,
series-circuit cabling, isolating transformers, connectors, and control, monitoring, testing and maintenance
systems.

#### Guides Landing

Approach and runway lighting gives pilots continuous visual reference from several miles out through
touchdown.

#### Guides Ground Movement

Taxiway lighting and signage prevent runway incursions and guide aircraft safely between runway, apron, and
gate.

#### Supports Low-Visibility Operations

AGL provides visual guidance during night operations and, where applicable, supports reduced-visibility
operations in conjunction with the airport's procedures, navigation systems and other required facilities.

## Understanding the Airport Layout

Before AGL makes sense, the basic movement areas need to. Different areas require different visual guidance
systems — that's the entire logic behind which lighting goes where.

#### Runway

Used primarily for aircraft takeoff and landing.

#### Taxiway

Provides aircraft movement between runways, aprons and other airport areas.

#### Apron

Where aircraft are parked, loaded, unloaded, refuelled and serviced.

#### Holding Position

A designated position where an aircraft may be required to hold before entering a runway or protected area.

Why Layout Matters to AGL

## The Basic AGL Power & Lighting Chain

Every AGL fixture, no matter which category it belongs to, traces back through the same chain of equipment.
This is the backbone of the whole system.

The CCR supplies controlled current to the airport lighting series circuit. That circuit connects individual
isolating transformers, each feeding a light fixture over its own secondary cable. The isolating transformer
provides electrical separation between the shared primary series circuit and its own fixture circuit; the
secondary cable then carries that isolated, lower-current supply the short distance to the fixture itself.

## Primary & Secondary Circuits

#### Primary Circuit

The high-voltage series circuit supplied by the CCR. Typical AGL systems use a constant-current series
arrangement rather than a conventional constant-voltage distribution setup — that's the key difference from
ordinary building wiring.

#### Secondary Circuit

The secondary side of an isolating transformer supplies the individual lighting fixture: CCR → primary AGL
cable → isolating transformer → secondary cable → light fixture.

Why Use a Series Circuit?

The series arrangement lets multiple lighting loads operate as part of one controlled airport lighting
circuit. Because the CCR controls circuit current directly, it also controls the lighting system's intensity
steps for the entire circuit at once.

## Constant Current Regulator (CCR)

A CCR is the major component of an AGL system that supplies controlled current to the series lighting circuit
— think of it as the heart of the whole chain.

Main Functions

Intensity control: a typical AGL system provides multiple selectable brightness levels. The actual number of
steps, and the current value at each step, depends on the applicable system design and specification.

## The AGL Series Circuit

An AGL series circuit connects multiple lighting units through series-connected primary cable and isolating
transformers — each fixture taps off the same loop of controlled current.

Key Engineering Concepts

## Isolating Transformer

Sits between the primary series circuit and one individual airfield lighting fixture — the component that
makes a series circuit of independent fixtures possible at all.

#### Electrical Isolation

Separates the fixture circuit from the primary series circuit.

#### Individual Fixture Connection

Allows one lighting unit to be connected onto the shared series circuit.

#### System Reliability

Supports continued operation of the remaining series circuit under appropriate fault conditions.

#### Typical Construction

Primary and secondary windings, magnetic core, insulation system, encapsulation/moulding, cable connections,
and a protective housing.

Important Transformer Parameters

How to Select an AGL Isolation Transformer

Selection starts from the fixture's rated burden and the series circuit's rated current, then checks that
against the transformer's rated power, turns ratio and insulation level for the applicable circuit voltage
class. Environmental rating, mounting method (e.g. in a light base or pit) and compliance with the applicable
ICAO/FAA/IS specification round out the decision.

## AGL Primary Cable

The primary cable forms the main electrical path between AGL series-circuit equipment.

Important Characteristics

## AGL Connectors

Connectors provide reliable electrical connections between AGL cables and equipment — small parts with an
outsized effect on circuit reliability.

A Poor Connection Can Cause

#### Runway Lighting

Provides the visual references that define the runway during landing and takeoff. Colour, location, spacing,
intensity and configuration each communicate something different to the pilot.

- Runway Edge Lights

- Runway Centreline Lights

- Threshold & Runway End Lights

- Touchdown Zone Lights

Extends outward from the runway threshold, establishing alignment with the runway and supporting the

- Threshold Lighting

Illuminated mandatory, location, direction and destination signs identifying taxiways, runways and holding

- Mandatory Signs

## PAPI — Precision Approach Path Indicator

PAPI tells a pilot where the aircraft sits relative to the desired approach slope, using four light units in a
row. The white-to-red balance across the bar shifts in single-lamp steps as the aircraft moves through the
slope — click a position below to see it change.

2 white / 2 red — the aircraft is on the correct approach slope.

## AGL Control & Monitoring

Modern airport lighting systems require more than turning lights ON and OFF. A control and monitoring layer
sits above the CCR and circuit.

## Photometry & Colour

An AGL fixture isn't acceptable merely because it illuminates — its optical performance has to meet the
applicable requirements.

#### Photometric Parameters

Intensity, distribution, beam characteristics, colour, horizontal and vertical coverage, alignment, and
uniformity where applicable — tested in the lab for controlled evaluation and in the field to verify installed
performance.

#### Colour

Colour is an important part of airport visual communication — different systems use specified colours for
different operational purposes. Evaluation covers chromaticity coordinates, colour boundaries, luminous
intensity and colour consistency.

## Testing, Maintenance & Common Faults

A reliable AGL system requires systematic testing and maintenance across four areas — click a fault card to
see its likely causes.

#### Electrical

Insulation resistance, continuity, transformer and cable testing, connector inspection.

#### Photometric

Intensity, distribution, colour and alignment.

#### Mechanical

Fixture, transformer and connector condition, mounting, housing, sealing.

#### Operational

CCR operation, intensity steps, control system, monitoring, fault indications.

Fault | Possible Cause | First Check / Test | Corrective Action

Open circuit | Cable break, connector failure, transformer connection failure, loose connection | Circuit continuity test | Locate the break by sectional continuity/loop testing; repair or replace the cable, connector or connection

High leakage / insulation failure | Cable damage, moisture ingress, connector deterioration, transformer insulation failure | Insulation resistance (megger) test | Identify the failed section; dry out, reseal or replace the affected cable, connector or transformer

Fixture OFF (individual) | Transformer fault, secondary cable fault, or fixture/lamp-driver fault | Secondary voltage/current check at the transformer | Replace the transformer, secondary cable or fixture as isolated by the test

CCR trip / circuit shutdown | Earth fault, short circuit, or overcurrent condition on the series circuit | Insulation/earth-fault check and circuit sectioning | Isolate the faulty section, clear the fault, and confirm circuit current is restored before re-energising

Transformer problem | Winding issue, insulation failure, overheating, incorrect rating, mechanical/environmental damage | Insulation resistance, turns ratio and visual/thermal inspection | Replace the transformer with a correctly rated, tested unit

Fixture failure | Lamp/LED failure, driver failure, optical damage, water ingress, mechanical damage | Secondary current draw and visual/photometric inspection | Replace the lamp/LED module, driver, or complete fixture as required; reseal housing

## Understanding the Standards

AGL engineering should always be considered against the applicable requirements, specifications and project
standards. A standard isn't a list of numbers to memorise — the engineer should understand what requirement
each number is trying to achieve.

International aviation standards and recommended practices.

Detailed airfield lighting equipment and system guidance, widely used as a technical reference.

Applicable Indian aviation regulatory and airport requirements.

Relevant Indian Standards for applicable AGL equipment.

## AGL Engineering Design

Once the fundamentals are understood, the next step is seeing how the components work together as a complete,
designed system.

## Airfield Lighting Basics, Overview, Purpose & Principles

### Airfield Lighting Basics

Airfield lighting basics: lights along runways, taxiways and aprons give pilots visual guidance in darkness
and poor visibility. They run on series circuits fed by constant current regulators, with each light connected
through an isolating transformer.

### Airfield Lighting Overview

An airfield lighting overview covers approach lights, runway lights, taxiway lights, PAPI, signs and beacons,
plus the power, regulators, cables and control behind them. Together they form one visual guidance system.

### Purpose Of Airfield Lighting

The purpose of airfield lighting is to let pilots find the runway, line up, land, taxi and park safely at
night and in low visibility, by showing position, direction and distance through light colour and pattern.

### Airfield Lighting For Beginners

Airfield lighting for beginners is easiest to learn in order: first what each light shows, then the series
circuit that powers it, then how it is controlled, tested and maintained. This page follows that sequence.

### Airfield Lighting Principles

Airfield lighting principles are consistency, reliability and clarity: patterns and colours follow
international standards so pilots read them the same everywhere, and circuits are designed so failures do not
leave large dark areas.

### Airfield Lighting Functions

Airfield lighting functions include marking runway edges and centrelines, identifying thresholds and ends,
guiding aircraft along taxiways, giving glide path information and signalling hazards such as obstacles or
runway holding positions.

### Airfield Lighting Types

Airfield lighting types are grouped by where they are used: approach lighting, runway lighting, taxiway
lighting, glide path indicators such as PAPI, apron and stand lighting, beacons and obstruction lights.
Fixtures are elevated or inset.

### Airfield Lighting Working Principle

Airfield lighting working principle: a constant current regulator forces one set current through a series loop
of cable, and each light draws power through an isolating transformer. Changing the current changes brightness
for every light on the circuit.

### Airfield Lighting Visual Aids

Airfield lighting visual aids are part of the wider group of visual aids in ICAO Annex 14, which also includes
markings, signs and markers. Lights, markings and signs must be designed to work together.

### Airport Lighting Signals

Airport lighting signals are the information carried by light colour, steadiness, flashing and arrangement,
for example green threshold, red runway end and flashing sequences on approach. They differ from light gun
signals sent from the tower.

## Airfield Ground Lighting Working Principle, Types, Functions & Specification

### Airfield Ground Lighting Working Principle

Airfield ground lighting working principle is series-circuit power: each circuit has one regulator, one cable
loop and many lights on isolating transformers, so a single lamp failure does not stop the others.

### Airfield Ground Lighting Types

Airfield ground lighting types cover elevated and inset fixtures, unidirectional, bidirectional and
omnidirectional beams, and white, green, red, blue, yellow and other colours chosen for the function of each
light.

### Airfield Ground Lighting Functions

Airfield ground lighting functions are guidance and information: where the runway is, where its ends are,
where to turn or stop on taxiways, and whether the aircraft is on the correct approach path.

### Airfield Ground Lighting Specification

An airfield ground lighting specification sets photometric output, colour, mechanical strength, ingress
protection and electrical data for each product. It cites standards such as ICAO Annex 14, FAA advisory
circulars and IEC standards.

### Airfield Ground Lighting Selection Guide

Airfield ground lighting selection guide: start from the runway and taxiway category, then choose fixture
type, light source, colour and intensity, and check compatibility with the existing regulators and
transformers.

### Airfield Ground Lighting Technical Guide

An airfield ground lighting technical guide ties together design, installation, testing and maintenance. Use
it with the manufacturer data and the standards that apply to your aerodrome.

## Airport Lighting Infrastructure, Types, Functions & Engineering Guide

### Airport Lighting Infrastructure

Airport lighting infrastructure includes substations and CCRs, series cable and ducts, light fixtures, control
and monitoring, standby power and earthing. It is long-life infrastructure, so design for maintainability from
the start.

### Airport Lighting Working Principle

Airport lighting working principle for airfield lights is series current control, while apron floodlights and
building lighting normally use ordinary parallel supply. Do not confuse the two systems.

### Airport Lighting Types

Airport lighting types include airfield ground lighting for aircraft guidance, apron floodlighting for ground
handling, obstruction lights and beacons, and terminal and road lighting, each with different standards.

### Airport Lighting Functions

Airport lighting functions range from aircraft guidance on the airfield to safe working light on aprons and
security and safety lighting around the airport.

### Airport Lighting Selection Guide

Airport lighting selection guide: separate airfield lighting from general lighting, select each by its
standard, and weigh energy use, maintenance access, life and spare parts availability.

### Airport Lighting Technical Guide

Airport lighting technical guide: this site's AGL pages cover the technical side of airfield lighting, from
basics to design, testing and troubleshooting, and link to the relevant standards.

### Airport Lighting Engineering Guide

An airport lighting engineering guide covers load calculation, circuit design, cable sizing, regulator
selection, control philosophy and standby power. See the AGL Engineering Design section above.

### Airfield Lighting Engineering

Airfield lighting engineering combines electrical design, optics and photometry, civil installation, control
systems and maintenance planning, all applied to meet aviation standards.

### AGL Technical Guide

An AGL technical guide should explain the system in layers: field fixtures, series circuits, regulators,
control and monitoring, and the standards and tests that prove compliance.

## Airfield Lighting Requirements, Operational Requirements & Selection

### Airfield Lighting System Requirements

Airfield lighting system requirements follow from the runway type, approach category and operations. Annex 14
and national rules state what lights are needed, their performance, and the supply and monitoring they
require.

### Airfield Lighting Requirements

Airfield lighting requirements are set by ICAO Annex 14, national regulators such as DGCA in India, and the
airport operator, and cover which lights are needed, their intensity and colour, and serviceability limits.

### Airfield Lighting Operational Requirements

Airfield lighting operational requirements cover availability, response to failures, switching time for
standby power, and procedures with air traffic control, especially for low-visibility operations.

### Airfield Lighting Selection Guide

Airfield lighting selection guide: define the operational need, pick fixtures and light sources that meet the
standard, then size circuits, regulators and control to suit, with spares and maintenance in mind.

### Airfield Lighting Technical Guide

Airfield lighting technical guide: use the manufacturer's data with the design standard to check layout,
photometry, electrical ratings and installation details before purchase and again at commissioning.

## Engineering & Expert Notes

#### Trace One Light Back to the Source

Pick a single fixture and follow it through transformer, cable, CCR and supply. Once you can walk that path on
a drawing, faults stop looking random and start pointing to a place.

#### Constant Current Changes How You Read Faults

Open circuits, earth faults and high-resistance joints behave differently from a constant-voltage system.
Learn the symptom of each before you pick up a meter, and treat every series circuit as live until proved
dead.

#### Most Field Faults Sit at Connections, Not in the Big Equipment

Connectors, joints and secondary terminations fail far more often than CCRs or transformers. Check and test
them first, and look for the water path that caused the failure.

#### A Light That Is On May Still Be Wrong

Electrical health does not prove the right intensity, colour or aim. Verify optical performance and alignment,
and keep commissioning data as a baseline.

#### Learn Which Document Answers Which Question

Design standards, equipment specifications and national rules serve different purposes. Cite the current
edition, and say which framework governs when a project mixes them.

#### Records Are Part of the System

Accurate as-builts, test results and fault logs make every later job faster and safer. Update them when the
work is closed, not weeks later.

## Frequently Asked Questions

Quick answers about Airfield Ground Lighting basics.

Airfield Ground Lighting is the system of visual aids and associated equipment used to guide aircraft during
approach, landing, takeoff and movement on the airport surface, especially at night or in reduced visibility.
It includes approach, runway and taxiway lighting, PAPI, illuminated signs, stop bars and runway guard lights,
plus the CCRs, series-circuit cabling, isolating transformers, connectors and control and monitoring systems
behind them.

Airport power feeds a Constant Current Regulator (CCR), which supplies a primary series circuit. Along that
circuit, each light fixture is fed by its own isolating transformer and secondary cable. Every fixture,
whatever its category, traces back through this same chain.

A CCR is the major component that supplies controlled current to the series lighting circuit. It maintains the
selected current level, provides multiple intensity steps, monitors operating conditions and gives protection
and fault indication. A typical circuit is a 6.6 A series circuit.

A series arrangement lets many lighting loads operate as part of one controlled circuit. Because the CCR
controls circuit current directly, it also sets the brightness step for the whole circuit at once. This
differs from ordinary constant-voltage building wiring.

It sits between the primary series circuit and one light fixture, electrically separating the fixture circuit
from the shared primary. It lets each fixture connect to the series circuit and supports continued operation
of the rest of the circuit under appropriate fault conditions.

The primary circuit is the high-voltage series circuit supplied by the CCR. The secondary circuit is the
isolated supply from the secondary side of an isolating transformer to an individual fixture: CCR, primary
cable, isolating transformer, secondary cable, then light fixture.

As a general orientation, runway edge lights are white, runway ends are red, thresholds are green, taxiway
edges are blue, taxiway centrelines are green and stop bars are red. Exact colour, location, spacing and
configuration depend on the applicable standard and the specific runway or taxiway layout.

PAPI uses four light units in a row. The balance of white and red changes in single-unit steps as the aircraft
moves through the slope, and two white and two red means the aircraft is on the correct approach slope.

Typical faults include open circuits (cable, connector or transformer connection failure), insulation or high-
leakage failures, an individual fixture being off, CCR trips from earth faults or overcurrent, transformer
problems and fixture failures. Continuity and insulation resistance tests are the usual first checks.

No. A fixture's optical performance must meet the applicable requirements, including intensity, distribution,
beam characteristics, colour, coverage, alignment and uniformity. Testing covers both the laboratory and the
installed field condition.

### AGL Glossary: Airfield Lighting Terminology, 1,033 Terms

Canonical URL: https://rahulsharmaagl.in/glossary.html

**Page summary:** Airfield lighting glossary: 1,033 AGL terms and definitions, including runway touchdown zone lights, approach lighting spacing and AGL maintenance records.

# AGL Glossary

Search 1,033 terms, abbreviations, components, and technical definitions used across Airfield Ground Lighting
engineering, standards, and field operations.

## AGL Glossary Terms

1,033 terms in the glossary

### #

#### 6.6 A Series Circuit

Airport lighting series circuit designed around a nominal regulated operating current of 6.6 A, with
individual loads connected through series isolation transformers.

#### 20 A Series Circuit

Airport lighting series circuit designed around a nominal regulated operating current of 20 A where the
equipment and project architecture use this configuration.

### A

#### A-SMGCS Advanced Surface Movement Guidance and Control System

Advanced Surface Movement Guidance and Control System (A-SMGCS) is an integrated system of surveillance,
identification, routing, guidance and related functions used to support the safe and efficient movement of
aircraft and vehicles on the aerodrome surface.

#### A-SMGCS Alarm

System-generated alert indicating a fault, conflict, unavailable function or abnormal condition requiring
attention.

#### A-SMGCS Data Link

Communication path used to exchange operational or system data between A-SMGCS components.

#### A-SMGCS Level 1

Basic surface movement guidance and control capability centred on surveillance/identification functions and
the operational information needed for safe surface movement.

#### A-SMGCS Level 2

Enhanced surface movement capability adding routing or guidance-related functions to improve controlled
movement beyond basic surveillance/identification.

#### A-SMGCS Level 3

Advanced surface movement capability that integrates guidance and/or conflict-management functions with the
underlying surveillance and routing architecture.

#### A-SMGCS Level 4

Advanced A-SMGCS capability incorporating the applicable integrated surveillance, routing, guidance and
conflict-management functions defined by the adopted system concept.

#### A-SMGCS Lighting Interface

Interface through which A-SMGCS exchanges movement-guidance information with airfield lighting equipment or
its control system.

#### A-SMGCS Network Interface

Physical or logical network interface connecting an A-SMGCS subsystem to another system or data network.

#### AAI Airports Authority of India

Airports Authority of India — the statutory body responsible for managing, operating and developing civil
aviation infrastructure at Indian airports, including approval and oversight of airside AGL design and safety.

#### Acceptance Criteria

The specific, measurable requirements a product, test result or piece of work must satisfy to be accepted as
compliant.

#### Acceptance Limit

The minimum or maximum photometric, electrical or dimensional value a measured result must fall within for a
fixture, circuit or system to be accepted or pass a test.

#### Acceptance Test

A formal test or set of tests used to determine whether equipment or an installed system satisfies the defined
acceptance criteria before handover or use.

#### ADS-B Surface Surveillance

Use of Automatic Dependent Surveillance-Broadcast data to support identification and tracking of equipped
surface targets.

#### Aerodrome Beacon

An aeronautical beacon installed at an aerodrome to provide a visual identification cue from the air.

#### Aerodrome Elevation

The elevation above mean sea level of the highest point of the landing area, published as a reference datum
for aerodrome operations.

#### Aerodrome Manual

The primary regulatory document, submitted to the civil aviation authority, describing an aerodrome's
facilities, procedures and operating conditions, including its AGL system.

#### Aerodrome Operator

The organisation legally responsible for the safe operation, maintenance and regulatory compliance of an
aerodrome, including its AGL systems.

#### Aerodrome Visual Aid

Any visual device, lighting, marking or sign, provided at an aerodrome to assist pilots and vehicle drivers
during approach, landing, takeoff and ground movement.

#### Aeronautical Information

Information concerning aerodrome facilities, procedures and hazards, published through official channels such
as the AIP or NOTAM, to support flight planning and operations.

#### AGL Airfield Ground Lighting

Integrated visual guidance system using lights, illuminated signs, power, control and monitoring equipment to
support aircraft movement on the aerodrome.

#### AGL Acceptance Test Record

Formal record demonstrating whether equipment or an installed AGL system met defined acceptance requirements.

#### AGL Alarm Test

A test that deliberately triggers each monitored fault condition to confirm the ALCMS or CCR correctly
detects, displays and logs the alarm.

#### AGL Alignment Deviation

Difference between the installed optical/mechanical orientation and the approved aiming or alignment
reference.

#### AGL Alignment Verification

A check confirming that a fixture's physical aiming angle matches its design value, performed using an
inclinometer or aiming template.

#### AGL Apron Crossing

Protected cable/duct route crossing an apron area while maintaining pavement integrity and cable protection.

#### AGL Automatic Transfer Switch

Switching device that automatically transfers a connected load between designated power sources according to
defined source-health and transfer logic.

#### AGL Base Can Level

Elevation and levelness of the base-can mounting interface relative to the specified pavement or datum.

#### AGL Bonding Conductor

Conductor used to establish electrical bonding between metallic parts so they remain at substantially the same
potential and provide a fault-current path where required.

#### AGL Breakdown Maintenance

Unplanned maintenance carried out in response to an AGL failure that has already occurred, as distinct from
maintenance performed on a scheduled or condition-based basis.

#### AGL Burn-In Test

Extended operation intended to expose early-life failures or unstable behavior before equipment is released
for service.

#### AGL Cable Protection Slab

Protective slab installed above an underground cable/duct route to reduce risk of mechanical damage from
excavation or loading.

#### AGL Cable Pulling Record

Controlled record of cable identification, route, pulling conditions and installation observations during
cable installation.

#### AGL Cable Slack

Controlled additional cable length left at a termination or fixture to permit installation, maintenance and
reconnection without excessive mechanical stress.

#### AGL Cable Termination Point

Defined location where a cable is electrically and mechanically connected to equipment, a connector,
transformer or joint.

#### AGL Calibration Certificate Review

Review confirming that a test instrument has valid calibration and suitable traceability before measurement.

#### AGL Changeover Panel

Electrical panel containing switching/control equipment used to transfer or select the supply feeding
designated AGL loads.

#### AGL Circuit Isolation Point

Defined switch, breaker, connector or other point used to electrically isolate a circuit for safe work.

#### AGL Circuit Load Test

A test in which a series circuit is energised and its actual load, voltage, current and resistance, is
measured and compared against the calculated design load.

#### AGL Circuit Open Fault

Loss of electrical continuity in a series circuit caused by a broken conductor, connector, transformer lead,
fixture or termination.

#### AGL Circuit Short Fault

Unintended low-impedance connection between conductors or to earth that changes the designed circuit current
path.

#### AGL Commissioning Checklist

Structured checklist covering functional, electrical, control and operational checks required before AGL
system acceptance.

#### AGL Communication Test

A test verifying that data communication between the ALCMS, CCRs and field devices is functioning correctly,
including message integrity and response time.

#### AGL Concrete Encased Duct

Duct installation surrounded by concrete to provide mechanical protection and maintain a controlled cable
pathway.

#### AGL Conditional Acceptance

Acceptance granted with defined outstanding conditions, restrictions or corrective actions that must be
tracked to closure.

#### AGL Connector High Resistance

Abnormally high contact or termination resistance causing voltage drop, heating or unstable operation.

#### AGL Connector Moisture Failure

Connector malfunction or insulation degradation caused by water/moisture ingress, inadequate sealing or
environmental damage.

#### AGL Crossing Detail

Drawing or installation detail showing how an AGL cable/duct crosses another route, pavement or service.

#### AGL Current Balance Check

Measurement comparing the currents across a series circuit's fixture branches or feeders to identify abnormal
loading, a poor connection or a developing imbalance.

#### AGL Current Measurement

The recording of actual current flowing in a series circuit, taken to verify it matches the CCR's set output
and the calculated circuit load.

#### AGL De-Energized Circuit Test

Test performed with the circuit safely isolated and verified dead, typically for continuity, insulation or
wiring checks.

#### AGL Dead Circuit Verification

Verification that an isolated circuit is not energized before personnel perform testing or maintenance.

#### AGL Defect Register

A tracked log of identified AGL defects recording location, description, priority, assigned action and close-
out status.

#### AGL Dielectric Withstand Acceptance

Acceptance evaluation of insulation performance under the specified dielectric test voltage, duration and
leakage criterion.

#### AGL Distribution Panel

The panel from which incoming power is distributed to individual CCRs or AGL sub-circuits, typically including
circuit breakers for each outgoing feed.

#### AGL Duct Bank

Group of ducts installed together to carry multiple cables with controlled routing and separation.

#### AGL Duct Cleaning

Removal of debris, water and obstructions from an installed duct before cable installation.

#### AGL Duct Installation

Installation of underground ducts or conduits that provide a defined protected path for AGL cables.

#### AGL Duct Mandrel Test

Test in which a calibrated mandrel is pulled through a duct to verify clear internal passage and usable bore.

#### AGL Earth Continuity

Electrical continuity of the protective/bonding path between equipment and the designated earthing system.

#### AGL Earth Continuity Test

Test verifying a low-resistance continuous protective-earth path between accessible metallic parts and the
designated earthing point.

#### AGL Earth Grid Resistance

Overall resistance of an interconnected earthing grid to the remote earth reference.

#### AGL Electrical Handover

Formal transfer of an electrical system from construction/testing responsibility to the operating or
maintenance organization with required records and status information.

#### AGL Electrical Isolation

The de-energising and physical disconnection of an AGL circuit or component, confirmed dead, before personnel
carry out work on it.

#### AGL Electrical Lockout

Application of a lock or controlled isolation device to prevent inadvertent energization during electrical
work. See also: Lockout Tagout.

#### AGL Emergency Shutdown

A control function that immediately de-energises AGL circuits in response to a hazardous condition, operable
locally or remotely.

#### AGL Emergency Supply

Source provided to maintain designated emergency loads under defined abnormal or loss-of-normal-supply
conditions.

#### AGL Endurance Test

Test that operates equipment for a defined duration or duty cycle to verify sustained performance.

#### AGL Energization Checklist

Controlled checklist used during initial energization to verify safe switching, expected current, alarms,
control response and abnormal conditions.

#### AGL Energized Circuit Test

Test performed with the AGL circuit energized to verify current, control, monitoring or functional behavior
under live operating conditions.

#### AGL Essential Distribution Board

Distribution board dedicated to essential loads and supplied from the designated essential power arrangement.

#### AGL Essential Supply

Electrical source classified as essential for maintaining defined airport/AGL functions when the normal source
is unavailable.

#### AGL Excessive Circuit Load

Connected load that causes the series circuit/CCR to operate outside its intended loading range.

#### AGL Failure Analysis

Technical examination of a failed AGL component or system to determine failure mechanism, contributing
conditions and corrective action.

#### AGL Fault Simulation

The deliberate introduction of a fault condition on a test bench or de-energised circuit to verify protective
devices, alarms or monitoring systems respond correctly.

#### AGL Fault Symptom

Observable indication of abnormal AGL behavior that guides diagnostic testing but does not by itself identify
the root cause.

#### AGL Fault Tree

Logical decomposition of an AGL failure into possible causes and branching checks used to identify the root
cause.

#### AGL Feeder Cable

Power cable carrying electrical supply from a distribution source to an AGL load or equipment such as a CCR.

#### AGL Feeder Isolation

Controlled disconnection of an AGL feeder from its supply for maintenance, testing or fault isolation.

#### AGL Feeder Panel

Panel containing protective and switching devices for outgoing AGL electrical feeders.

#### AGL Feeder Protection

Protective devices and settings applied to an AGL feeder to clear faults while protecting conductors and
equipment.

#### AGL Final Acceptance

Formal confirmation that the completed AGL work meets the approved scope and acceptance requirements.

#### AGL Fixture Flicker Fault

Unstable or visibly fluctuating fixture output caused by driver, power, connection, control or thermal
problems.

#### AGL Fixture Intermittent Fault

Fixture failure that appears and disappears with changes in temperature, vibration, moisture ingress, current
level or connection looseness, making it harder to reproduce during fault-finding.

#### AGL Fixture Low-Intensity Fault

Condition in which a fixture operates but produces less light than the applicable photometric or functional
requirement.

#### AGL Fixture No-Light Fault

Condition in which an AGL fixture produces no intended light output despite a commanded operating state.

#### AGL Fixture Overheating

Fixture temperature exceeding its intended thermal operating condition, potentially reducing optical output or
component life.

#### AGL Fixture Water Ingress Fault

Entry of water into an AGL fixture or enclosure that can degrade optics, electronics, insulation or mechanical
components.

#### AGL Fixture Wrong-Color Fault

Fixture output whose chromaticity or commanded color does not match the intended AGL function.

#### AGL Functional Performance Test

Test that verifies an AGL function performs its intended sequence, response and output under defined
conditions.

#### AGL Generator Supply

Electrical supply produced by an engine-generator set and used as an alternate or emergency source for
designated AGL loads.

#### AGL Grounding Grid

A network of interconnected buried conductors forming the earthing system for an AGL substation or CCR
building, providing a low-impedance path to ground.

#### AGL High Leakage Fault

Condition in which leakage current to earth or between conductors exceeds the expected level for the circuit
and insulation system.

#### AGL Inspection and Test Plan

Controlled project document defining inspections, tests, acceptance criteria, responsibilities and
hold/witness points for the AGL work.

#### AGL Inspection Request

Formal request submitted for inspection or testing of a defined installation activity or completed work
package.

#### AGL Installation Drawing

Drawing that locates fixtures, bases, cables, equipment and installation details against the approved airport
layout.

#### AGL Interlock Test

A test confirming that safety or logic interlocks, such as stop bar and centreline interlocking, correctly
prevent an unsafe combination of lighting states.

#### AGL Isolation Procedure

The documented sequence for safely disconnecting and locking out an AGL circuit or item of equipment from its
electrical supply before maintenance work begins.

#### AGL ITP Witness Point

Inspection stage where the designated party is notified and may witness the activity without necessarily
stopping subsequent work.

#### AGL Junction Box

An enclosure where cables are joined, branched or terminated, providing mechanical protection and access for
testing or maintenance.

#### AGL Latent Fault

Existing defect that is not immediately apparent during normal operation but can prevent a required function
when demanded.

#### AGL Low Insulation Fault

Condition indicated by insulation resistance below the applicable acceptance or operating criterion.

#### AGL Maintenance Record

The formal documentation retained as evidence that scheduled or corrective AGL maintenance was carried out,
and its outcome.

#### AGL Material Inspection

Inspection confirming that delivered AGL materials match approved type, quantity, identification, condition
and documentation.

#### AGL Monitoring in LVP

Continuous or periodic monitoring of critical AGL functions needed to maintain the approved low-visibility
operating configuration.

#### AGL Mounting Surface

Physical surface that supports the AGL fixture and establishes its seating, elevation and orientation.

#### AGL Nonconformance Record

Controlled record describing a deviation from an approved requirement and its disposition.

#### AGL Nuisance Trip

Protective trip or shutdown occurring without the intended fault condition, often requiring investigation of
thresholds, leakage, transients or equipment behavior.

#### AGL Overcurrent Protection

Devices such as fuses or circuit breakers that automatically disconnect a circuit when current exceeds a safe
level, preventing damage or fire.

#### AGL Pavement Crossing

Construction detail used to route an AGL cable/duct across paved aircraft or vehicle movement surfaces.

#### AGL Permanent Fault

Fault that remains present until the failed component, connection or condition is corrected.

#### AGL Phase Identification Test

Test used to confirm correct identification of conductors/phases in an upstream electrical supply or panel.

#### AGL Photometric Acceptance Test

A field measurement of an installed fixture's or circuit's luminous intensity, taken after commissioning and
compared against the design acceptance criteria to confirm the installed system meets its specified light
output.

#### AGL Photometric Nonuniformity

Undesired spatial variation in measured light output relative to the required distribution or uniformity
criterion.

#### AGL Photometric Underperformance

Measured optical performance below the applicable intensity, luminance, uniformity or other photometric
acceptance criterion.

#### AGL Planned Maintenance

Maintenance scheduled in advance at fixed time or usage intervals, rather than triggered by a fault.

#### AGL Power Factor Test

A test measuring the ratio of real to apparent power drawn by an AGL load, used to assess transformer or CCR
loading characteristics.

#### AGL Pre-Commissioning Inspection

A physical inspection carried out before commissioning tests begin, confirming installation is complete and
correct before the system is energised.

#### AGL Pre-Energization Checklist

Checklist confirming that an AGL circuit/equipment is ready to be energized after safety, wiring, insulation
and configuration checks.

#### AGL Prospective Fault Current

Current that would flow at a specified point if a fault of negligible impedance occurred under the assumed
system conditions.

#### AGL Protection Coordination

Selection and setting of protective devices so their operating characteristics provide the required protection
and coordination.

#### AGL Protective Earth Test

Test verifying continuity and integrity of the protective-earth connection for equipment requiring protective
bonding.

#### AGL Proving Dead

Verification using an approved test instrument that an isolated electrical circuit is not energized before
work begins.

#### AGL Provisional Acceptance

Temporary acceptance allowing controlled use before all final acceptance conditions are closed.

#### AGL Punch List

A list of outstanding defects or incomplete items identified during inspection, to be closed out before final
acceptance of the works.

#### AGL Re-Energization Procedure

Controlled sequence for removing isolation controls and restoring an electrical circuit to service after work
and safety checks are complete.

#### AGL Remote Control Test

A test confirming that commands issued from the ALCMS or tower control panel correctly operate the intended
AGL circuit or fixture.

#### AGL Repetitive Fault

Fault that recurs after reset or correction and therefore indicates an unresolved underlying cause.

#### AGL Road Crossing

Protected cable/duct crossing beneath or through a road used by airport vehicles or aircraft-support traffic.

#### AGL Safe Isolation

Controlled process of disconnecting, securing, proving dead and preventing re-energization of an electrical
circuit before work.

#### AGL Safety Interlock

A control mechanism that prevents a hazardous action, such as re-energising a circuit, until a specified
safety condition is satisfied.

#### AGL Spare Cable Length

Reserved cable length retained for future termination, maintenance or repositioning of connected equipment.

#### AGL SPD Coordination

The design process of selecting and locating surge protective devices at different points in an AGL system so
they operate together to limit surge energy reaching sensitive equipment. See also: AGL Surge Coordination.

#### AGL SPD Status Indicator

Visual or remote indication showing the service condition or failure state of a surge protective device.

#### AGL SPD Type

Classification of a surge protective device according to its intended installation/application and applicable
standard.

#### AGL Standby Supply

Alternate electrical source intended to supply designated loads when the normal source fails or is
unavailable.

#### AGL Surge Coordination

Selecting and coordinating surge protective devices at the CCR, transformers and field equipment so each stage
clamps transient voltage before it reaches downstream equipment with a lower insulation withstand rating. See
also: AGL SPD Coordination.

#### AGL System Performance Test

Integrated test verifying that multiple AGL subsystems operate together as specified.

#### AGL Terminal Block

A modular block of connection points used to terminate and join conductors within a panel, junction box or CCR
enclosure.

#### AGL Test Record

Controlled record that documents the conditions, instruments, measured results, acceptance outcome and
observations from an AGL test. It provides traceable evidence that a defined inspection or test was performed
and records its disposition.

#### AGL Transformer Insulation Failure

Degradation or breakdown of transformer insulation causing unacceptable leakage or dielectric performance.

#### AGL Trench Backfill

Approved material placed around and above an installed cable/duct to provide protection and restore the
excavation.

#### AGL Troubleshooting Test Point

Defined electrical or control measurement location used to isolate a fault without unnecessarily disturbing
the circuit.

#### AGL Troubleshooting Workflow

Structured sequence for isolating an AGL fault from symptom identification through measurement, fault
localization, correction and verification.

#### AGL Underloaded Series Circuit

Series circuit whose connected load is insufficient for the intended CCR operating range or design condition.

#### AGL UPS Supply

Uninterruptible power source that maintains designated control, monitoring or other critical loads through a
transfer or short interruption in the normal supply.

#### Aiming Angle

The vertical and horizontal angle at which a light fixture's optical axis is set relative to a reference
plane, determined during installation or alignment to direct the beam to its design position.

#### Aircraft Movement Area

The part of an aerodrome used for aircraft takeoff, landing and taxiing, comprising the manoeuvring area and
the apron(s). See also: Movement Area.

#### Aircraft Parking Position

A designated area on an apron where an aircraft is parked for loading, unloading, servicing or overnight stay.

#### Aircraft Stand

A designated area on an apron intended for parking or servicing an aircraft.

#### Aircraft Stand Guidance System

A system that provides visual guidance to an aircraft during movement into or within an aircraft stand.

#### Aircraft Tracking

Continuous or periodic determination of an aircraft's identity and movement position on the aerodrome surface.

#### Airfield Cable Airfield Lighting Cable

Cable specifically rated and constructed for burial or duct installation in the airside environment, meeting
the mechanical and electrical requirements of AGL circuits.

#### Airfield Lighting Isolation

The controlled de-energising of an airfield lighting circuit for maintenance, confirmed and communicated
before work begins.

#### Airfield Sign

Illuminated or retroreflective aerodrome sign used to provide standardized visual information, direction,
location, destination or mandatory instruction on the movement area.

#### Airfield Work Zone

A designated and marked area on the airside where maintenance or construction work is being carried out,
requiring specific access, barricading and notification controls.

#### Airside Driving

Driving of vehicles within the airside area, governed by an aerodrome's specific rules, permits and training
requirements distinct from public road driving.

#### Airside Electrical Safety

The set of practices and controls, such as isolation, PPE and permits, applied specifically to electrical work
carried out in the airside environment.

#### Airside Safety

The overall set of practices, rules and controls in place to protect personnel, vehicles and aircraft
operating within the airside environment.

#### Airside Works

Any construction, maintenance or installation activity carried out within the airside area, subject to
specific access, safety and notification controls.

#### ALCMS Airport Lighting Control and Monitoring System

Airport Lighting Control and Monitoring System that provides centralized control, status indication, alarms
and monitoring of airport lighting facilities.

#### ALCMS Access Control

Controls which users or user roles may access ALCMS functions, displays, commands and configuration areas.
Access control typically combines authentication with role-based permissions so operational actions and
configuration changes are limited to authorised personnel.

#### ALCMS Alarm Management

Organises, prioritises and records alarms generated by the ALCMS, including fault, warning and acknowledgement
states. It provides operators with a consistent method for recognising, reviewing and closing lighting-system
alarms.

#### ALCMS Architecture

Defines the arrangement of ALCMS servers, workstations, controllers, networks, field interfaces and
communication paths. The architecture establishes how control, monitoring, redundancy and data exchange
functions are distributed across the system.

#### ALCMS Backup

Provides recovery capability for ALCMS configuration, application data or historical records after equipment
failure or data loss. The backup arrangement defines what information is copied, where it is stored and how
restoration is performed.

#### ALCMS Circuit Monitoring

Collects and presents operating status or fault information from AGL circuits and associated control
equipment. Circuit monitoring allows the ALCMS to identify abnormal states and provide corresponding
indications or alarms.

#### ALCMS Command

Command issued by an operator or supervisory function to change the state or operating level of a controlled
AGL function. An ALCMS command is transmitted to the relevant control interface and requires an associated
field response.

#### ALCMS Command Verification

Confirms that an ALCMS command produced the intended field response and corresponding status indication.
Verification may compare the commanded state with feedback from the CCR, circuit-control equipment or
monitored field device.

#### ALCMS Communication Failure

Indicates loss or degradation of communication between ALCMS components or between the ALCMS and connected
field equipment. The failure can prevent command transfer, status updates or alarm reporting until the
communication path is restored.

#### ALCMS Cybersecurity

Protective measures applied to the ALCMS to preserve authorised access, system availability and integrity of
control data. Cybersecurity controls can include authentication, access restrictions, network segmentation,
logging and controlled software changes.

#### ALCMS Data Logging

Records selected ALCMS events, commands, alarms and status changes with associated time information. Data
logging provides an operational history that can support troubleshooting, incident review and verification of
system behaviour.

#### ALCMS Database

Structured data store used by the ALCMS to retain configuration, equipment information, user data, events or
other application records. The database supplies stored information to the system functions that require
persistent data.

#### ALCMS Emergency Control

ALCMS function that provides operator or supervisory control of designated lighting during an emergency
condition. It is intended to execute defined emergency actions while providing status feedback and alarm
indication.

#### ALCMS Ethernet

Ethernet communication technology used to connect ALCMS components over a local or routed data network. It
carries control, monitoring and application traffic between compatible servers, workstations, controllers and
network devices.

#### ALCMS Event Log

Chronological record of significant ALCMS events such as commands, alarms, operator actions and system
changes. The event log supports traceability by preserving the sequence and time of recorded system
activities. See also: Event Log.

#### ALCMS Fail-Safe State

Defined ALCMS operating condition entered when a detected failure prevents normal control or monitoring. The
fail-safe state applies predetermined outputs or restrictions intended to prevent an unsafe or uncontrolled
lighting condition.

#### ALCMS Fiber Link

Optical-fiber communication path connecting ALCMS equipment, network devices or remote control interfaces. The
fiber link carries digital control and monitoring data while providing electrical isolation between connected
network points.

#### ALCMS Graphic Display

Graphical operator display that presents ALCMS equipment status, circuit states, alarms and available controls
in a visual screen layout. It helps operators identify the affected lighting function and issue permitted
commands.

#### ALCMS Lamp Monitoring

Monitors the operating condition of lamps or lighting circuits and reports detected failures or abnormal
states to the ALCMS. The monitoring method depends on the field equipment and may use electrical, optical or
status-feedback information.

#### ALCMS LVP Control

ALCMS functions used to select, monitor and alarm the lighting configurations required for low-visibility
operations.

#### ALCMS Modbus

Modbus communication protocol used to exchange control, status or measurement data between compatible ALCMS
equipment and connected devices. The implementation may use a serial or Ethernet-based Modbus variant defined
by the system design.

#### ALCMS Network

Data network interconnecting ALCMS servers, workstations, controllers and communication interfaces. The
network provides the communication paths required for supervisory control, monitoring, alarms and system data
exchange.

#### ALCMS Operator Interface

Operator-facing interface through which authorised personnel view ALCMS status, alarms and controls and issue
permitted lighting commands. It provides the human-machine interaction layer between the operator and the
control application.

#### ALCMS PLC

Programmable logic controller used within an ALCMS to execute defined control, interlocking, monitoring or
interface logic. The PLC exchanges signals with field equipment and higher-level supervisory functions
according to the configured application.

#### ALCMS Protocol

Defined communication rules and message structure used by ALCMS components to exchange commands, status,
alarms or data. The protocol determines how connected devices interpret transmitted information and respond to
valid messages.

#### ALCMS Redundancy

Provision of alternative ALCMS components, communication paths or power arrangements so a single defined
failure does not remove the required control or monitoring function. The redundancy arrangement depends on the
