system architecture and availability requirements.

#### ALCMS Remote I/O

Remote input/output interface that exchanges field signals with an ALCMS controller over a communication
network. Remote I/O reduces the need to route every field signal directly to the central control panel or PLC.

#### ALCMS Server

Computer system that hosts ALCMS applications, databases or services required for supervisory control and
monitoring. The server provides shared processing or data functions to connected operator workstations and
system clients.

#### ALCMS Status Monitoring

Continuous or periodic presentation of ALCMS equipment and circuit status to identify normal, abnormal or
unavailable conditions. Status monitoring supplies operators and supervisory functions with the information
needed for operational control.

#### ALCMS User Authentication

Process that verifies the identity of an ALCMS user before permitting access to protected functions. User
authentication can use credentials or another approved identity mechanism defined by the system security
design.

#### ALCMS Workstation

Computer terminal used by an operator to access ALCMS applications, displays, alarms and authorised control
functions. A workstation provides the local human-machine interface to the supervisory lighting-control
system.

#### ALCMS-A-SMGCS Interface

Data/control interface exchanging lighting commands, status or alarms between the ALCMS and an A-SMGCS
environment.

#### Alignment Check

A measurement or verification that the installed equipment orientation or position agrees with the approved
reference geometry.

#### ALS Approach Lighting System

Approach Lighting System providing a visual reference during the approach and transition toward the runway
threshold.

#### APAPI Abbreviated Precision Approach Path Indicator

Abbreviated Precision Approach Path Indicator (APAPI) system using two optical light units to provide visual
approach-slope guidance. The optical units produce the required white/red visual indications used to determine
whether the aircraft is above, on or below the intended approach path.

#### APAPI Photometric Verification

Field verification of APAPI optical performance against the approved alignment and photometric requirements.
The verification uses measured or observed light output to confirm that the installed two-unit system provides
the intended approach-slope indications.

#### APAPI Unit Alignment

Mechanical and optical adjustment of an APAPI unit so its aiming direction and elevation correspond to the
approved installation geometry. Alignment is normally checked against the specified approach-slope reference
before photometric verification.

#### Approach Light Base

Physical support or mounting structure used to install an approach-lighting fixture at the specified position
and elevation. The base transfers fixture loads to the supporting surface while maintaining the required
installation geometry.

#### Approach Light Circuit

Electrical circuit supplying one or more approach-lighting fixtures or units. The circuit provides the
required power path from the lighting control or distribution equipment to the field fixtures and associated
connections.

#### Approach Light Failure

Loss or unacceptable degradation of an approach-lighting fixture's intended light output or operation. The
failure may result from lamp or LED failure, wiring, connector, power-supply, optical or mechanical problems.

#### Approach Light Fixture

Lighting unit installed as part of an approach lighting system to provide a specified visual reference during
approach. Its optical assembly, mounting arrangement and light source are selected to produce the required
distribution and colour.

#### Approach Light Maintenance

Inspection, cleaning, adjustment and repair activities performed to keep approach-lighting equipment
operational and correctly aligned. Maintenance addresses fixture condition, supports, electrical connections
and optical performance as applicable to the installed system.

#### Approach Lighting Alignment

Geometric adjustment and verification of approach-lighting units relative to the approved runway centreline,
elevation and aiming references. Correct alignment ensures the light distribution is directed toward the
intended approach sector.

#### Approach Lighting Barrette

Three or more closely spaced lights arranged in a short transverse line so that, from a distance, they appear
as a single short bar of light. Barrettes repeated along the centreline form the main axis of precision
approach lighting systems.

#### Approach Lighting Centerline

Longitudinal reference line formed by the central axis of an approach lighting system. The centreline
establishes the primary geometric reference for positioning and alignment of approach-lighting elements.

#### Approach Lighting Crossbar

Transverse row or assembly of approach-lighting elements extending across the system centreline. The crossbar
provides a lateral visual reference whose location and dimensions are defined by the applicable approach-
lighting arrangement.

#### Approach Lighting in LVP

Operation of the approach lighting system during low-visibility procedures, including the required control,
monitoring and operational checks for the installed lighting configuration.

#### Approach Lighting Intensity Control

Control function that changes the commanded intensity of an approach lighting system to provide the required
visual brightness for the operating condition. The control acts through the applicable lighting power or
control equipment.

#### Approach Lighting Sequenced Flashing Light

Approach-lighting unit that produces a brief high-intensity flash as part of a timed sequence with other
flashing units. The sequence creates a moving visual effect that helps indicate the approach direction toward
the runway.

#### Approach Lighting Spacing

Specified distance between adjacent approach-lighting elements or assemblies along or across the approach
system. Spacing establishes the intended visual geometry and must be maintained during installation and
inspection.

#### Approach Lighting Threshold Transition

Defined changeover region where approach-lighting visual guidance transitions to the runway threshold lighting
environment. The transition is coordinated with the applicable approach and threshold geometry so pilots
receive continuous visual guidance.

#### Approach Lighting Tower

Elevated support structure on which approach-lighting fixtures are mounted where terrain or obstacles require
lights above ground level. Under ICAO Annex 14 approach-light structures must be as low as practicable and
frangible, with limited allowances for tall structures, so towers use frangible sections or couplings that
break away on impact. Maintenance at height needs approved access and fall-protection practice.

#### Approach Slope

The descent path an aircraft follows on final approach, indicated visually by systems such as PAPI or defined
by instrument procedures.

#### Apron

A defined area of an aerodrome intended to accommodate aircraft for purposes such as loading, unloading,
passenger embarkation, servicing, parking or maintenance.

#### Apron Floodlight

A lighting fixture used to illuminate aircraft parking and servicing areas on an apron while providing the
required visual environment for ground operations.

#### Apron Management Service

An air traffic or ground service function responsible for managing aircraft and vehicle movement on the apron.

#### Apron Sign

Sign used to identify or direct movement toward an apron or apron-related destination.

#### Apron Taxiway

A taxiway located on or bordering an apron, intended to provide a taxi route across the apron rather than
serve as a stand-alone taxiway.

#### Arc Flash

A dangerous release of energy from an electrical fault, capable of causing burns and injury, guarded against
through safe work procedures, PPE and equipment design.

#### As-Built Drawing

A drawing updated after construction to show the AGL system exactly as installed, including any deviations
from the original design.

#### Asset Register

A structured record listing every AGL asset such as fixtures, cable, CCRs and transformers, with
identification, location, installation date and status, used for maintenance and lifecycle tracking.

#### Average Intensity Average Luminous Intensity

The mean luminous intensity calculated from multiple measurement points across a photometric distribution,
used to characterize overall fixture output against a specification.

### B

#### Barricading

The use of physical barriers, cones or tape to mark off a work area or hazard on the airside, preventing
unauthorised entry by vehicles, personnel or aircraft.

#### Base Can

The below-ground metal or composite housing into which a light fixture is mounted, providing a fixed
connection point for the fixture and cable.

#### Beam Axis

The reference line through the beam centre along which a light is aimed. For a symmetrical beam it coincides
with the direction of maximum intensity. Used as the reference for aiming and alignment checks.

#### Beam Center

The centre of the main beam, normally the geometric centre of the specified isocandela area, used as the
aiming reference. It does not always coincide with the single point of peak intensity (see Peak Intensity), so
a test report should state which convention it uses.

#### Beam Spread

The angular width of a light beam, usually measured between the points where intensity falls to a defined
fraction of peak, used to characterize how tightly or broadly a fixture distributes light.

#### Bias Correction

Correction applied to compensate for a known or estimated systematic measurement bias.

#### BIS Bureau of Indian Standards

Bureau of Indian Standards — India's national standards body, publishing Indian Standards (IS) referenced for
cables, transformers, enclosures and other electrical components used in AGL installations.

#### Black-on-Yellow Sign

Airfield sign with a black legend on a yellow background, used for direction, destination and similar
information signs. Location signs use the reverse (yellow on black) and mandatory instruction signs use white
on red.

#### BOM Bill of Materials

An itemised list of every component, quantity and part number required to construct or install an AGL system
or subsystem.

#### BOQ Bill of Quantities

A priced schedule listing the quantities of materials, labour and works items for an AGL project, used for
tendering and contract valuation.

#### Brightness Control

A control function used to adjust or select the perceived/photometric light output of a lighting system within
its designed operating range.

### C

#### Cable Bend Radius

Cable Bend Radius is the minimum permissible radius to which an AGL cable may be bent without exceeding the
mechanical limits of its construction.

#### Cable Conductor

Cable Conductor is the metallic conductive element within an AGL cable that carries the electrical current or
signal required by the circuit.

#### Cable Continuity Test

Cable Continuity Test is an electrical test used to verify that the intended conductive path exists between
defined ends of an AGL cable or conductor.

#### Cable Duct

Cable Duct is a conduit, duct or enclosed passage used to route and protect AGL cables through pavement,
structures or other installation zones.

#### Cable Fault

Cable Fault is an abnormal electrical or physical condition in an AGL cable or associated connection that
interrupts, degrades or changes intended circuit performance.

#### Cable Fault Distance

Cable Fault Distance is the estimated distance from a defined cable test point to the location of a detected
cable fault or impedance discontinuity.

#### Cable Gland

A fitting used to terminate a cable at the point it enters an enclosure, providing a sealed, strain-relieved
connection.

#### Cable Insulation

The dielectric material surrounding a conductor that provides electrical separation from other conductors and
grounded structures.

#### Cable Joint

A permanent connection made between two cable ends or a cable and a fixture, insulated and sealed to restore
the cable's original electrical and mechanical properties.

#### Cable Locator

Cable Locator is an instrument used to detect and trace the route of buried or concealed cables by sensing an
applied or induced electrical signal.

#### Cable Marker

A tag or sign, placed along a cable route or at access points, identifying the cable's route, type or
ownership for future reference.

#### Cable Megger Test

Cable Megger Test is an insulation-resistance test performed with a megohmmeter to assess cable insulation
between specified conductors and/or between a conductor and earth.

#### Cable Phase Identification

Cable Phase Identification is the process of positively identifying the corresponding conductor or cable phase
at different points in an AGL electrical circuit before connection, testing or maintenance.

#### Cable Protection

Cable Protection is the set of mechanical, environmental and electrical measures used to protect AGL cables
from damage, excessive stress, moisture and other installation hazards.

#### Cable Pulling Tension

Cable Pulling Tension is the tensile force applied to an AGL cable during installation and pulling through a
route, duct or conduit.

#### Cable Repair

The process of restoring a damaged section of cable to a serviceable condition, typically by cutting out the
fault and installing a jointed splice or replacement length.

#### Cable Resistance

The electrical resistance of a cable/conductor path, influenced by conductor material, length, cross-sectional
area and temperature.

#### Cable Route

The physical path a cable follows from source to destination, recorded on drawings to guide installation and
later locate the cable for maintenance or fault-finding.

#### Cable Route Marker

Cable Route Marker is a physical marker or sign used to identify the approximate route or location of a buried
or concealed AGL cable or associated underground service.

#### Cable Schedule

A tabulated record listing every cable in a project by identification number, origin, destination, type,
length and circuit, used for installation and testing reference.

#### Cable Screen

Cable Screen is a conductive shielding layer around one or more cable conductors used to control
electromagnetic coupling and, where designed, provide a defined shielding or bonding path.

#### Cable Separation

Cable Separation is the physical or designed separation maintained between AGL cables, circuits and other
services to reduce interference, fault propagation, mechanical damage and maintenance risk.

#### Cable Sheath

Cable Sheath is the protective outer layer of a cable that provides mechanical and environmental protection to
the insulated conductors and internal construction.

#### Cable Splice

Cable Splice is an approved connection joining two cable sections while restoring electrical continuity,
insulation and environmental protection.

#### Cable Termination

Cable Termination is the prepared end connection of a cable to a connector, terminal, transformer, fixture or
other equipment interface.

#### Cable Trench

An excavated, typically backfilled or covered channel used to route and protect buried AGL cables along a
defined path, sized to maintain separation between primary, secondary and other services.

#### Calibration Certificate

Documented record showing that an instrument or reference standard was calibrated against specified references
under defined conditions.

#### Calibration Factor

A correction value applied to raw instrument readings, derived by comparing the instrument's output against a
certified reference standard, to bring measurements into agreement with true values.

#### Candela

SI unit of luminous intensity in a given direction; symbol cd.

#### CAPA Corrective and Preventive Action

A structured process for investigating a nonconformance, correcting it, and implementing changes to prevent
recurrence.

#### CAT I Category I Precision Approach

Precision approach and landing with a decision height not lower than 60 m (200 ft) and either visibility not
less than 800 m or runway visual range (RVR) not less than 550 m (ICAO Annex 14 definition of a Category I
precision approach runway). Operator and State minima may differ.

#### CAT II Category II Precision Approach

Precision approach and landing with a decision height lower than 60 m (200 ft) but not lower than 30 m (100
ft), and RVR not less than 300 m (ICAO). Needs Category II/III-standard approach, runway centreline and
touchdown zone lighting with higher availability and monitoring requirements.

#### CAT II AGL

AGL configuration supporting operations under Category II approach/landing criteria, with the required visual
aids, control, monitoring and reliability provisions defined by the applicable aerodrome design.

#### CAT II/III Lighting System

Integrated AGL arrangement designed to support Category II/III operations, including the specified runway,
approach, taxiway, stop-bar and control/monitoring functions.

#### CAT III Category III Precision Approach

Precision approach and landing in very low visibility. ICAO sub-categories: IIIA (decision height below 30 m /
100 ft or none, RVR not less than 175 m), IIIB (decision height below 15 m / 50 ft or none, RVR below 175 m
but not less than 50 m) and IIIC (no decision height and no RVR limit). Lighting reliability, monitoring and
maintenance requirements are the most demanding.

#### CAT III AGL

AGL configuration supporting Category III low-visibility operations, where lighting availability, redundancy,
monitoring, alignment and maintenance controls are critical to continued operational capability.

#### CAT III Alignment Verification

Survey/inspection confirming that critical fixtures remain within the approved aiming and positioning
tolerances for Category III operation.

#### CAT III Backup Power

Alternate electrical source or power path provided to maintain required critical lighting functions after loss
of the normal source.

#### CAT III Circuit Integrity

Verified electrical continuity, insulation and functional integrity of a critical lighting circuit.

#### CAT III Maintenance Requirement

Maintenance control needed to preserve the availability, alignment, monitoring and redundancy of lighting used
for Category III operations.

#### CAT III Operational Readiness

Verified state in which the required CAT III lighting, power, control, monitoring, maintenance and operational
conditions are satisfied.

#### CAT III Photometric Verification

Measurement of specified critical lighting photometry to demonstrate compliance with the applicable Category
III criteria.

#### CAT III Stop Bar Interlock

Control logic preventing an unsafe combination of stop-bar status and movement authorization in a protected
low-visibility operation.

#### CCR Constant Current Regulator

Constant Current Regulator that maintains controlled current in an airport series circuit despite changes in
circuit impedance and load.

#### CCR Alarm Reset

Action that acknowledges or clears a CCR alarm indication according to the monitor/control design.

#### CCR Auxiliary Supply

Internal or external low-power supply used for CCR control, monitoring, relays, communication or auxiliary
functions.

#### CCR Cabinet Temperature

Temperature measured or monitored within the CCR enclosure during operation.

#### CCR Cabinet Ventilation

Controlled airflow through the CCR enclosure used to manage internal temperature.

#### CCR Circuit Insulation

The insulation resistance of a constant-current series circuit's conductors and isolation transformers to
earth, verified with a megohmmeter to confirm there is no unintended leakage or fault path.

#### CCR Circuit Load

The combined impedance presented by the lamps and isolation transformer primaries wired in series on a
circuit, which the CCR's regulator must drive at the selected current step; used to size and verify CCR output
capacity.

#### CCR Closed-Loop Control

Control method in which measured output current is compared with the reference and corrected to maintain the
required regulated value.

#### CCR Communication Interface

The data connection (serial, Ethernet, or discrete I/O) between a CCR and an Airfield Lighting Control and
Monitoring System (ALCMS) used for remote step selection and status/fault reporting.

#### CCR Control Interface

The local or remote control inputs, such as a panel-mounted selector or an ALCMS command, used to choose a
CCR's brightness step and on/off state.

#### CCR Control Transformer

Transformer supplying an isolated control voltage for CCR control circuitry.

#### CCR Cooling Fan

Forced-air cooling component used to remove heat from a CCR cabinet or power electronics.

#### CCR Cooling System

The method, such as natural convection, forced-air, or oil-filled construction, used to dissipate heat
generated in a CCR's regulating transformer and electronics, sized to the unit's rated output.

#### CCR Current Feedback

Signal representing measured output current and returned to the CCR control loop or monitor.

#### CCR Current Sensing

Measurement of CCR output current used by the regulator or monitor for control and protection.

#### CCR Current Setpoint

The target series-circuit output current commanded for a brightness step. On a 6.6 A (Class 1) circuit a
5-step (Style 2) regulator uses nominal steps of 2.8, 3.4, 4.1, 5.2 and 6.6 A; a 3-step (Style 1) regulator
uses 4.8, 5.5 and 6.6 A. On a 20 A (Class 2) circuit the steps are scaled up to 20 A.

#### CCR Current Stability

The degree to which a CCR holds its selected output current constant despite input voltage fluctuation or
changes in series-circuit load, specified as a tolerance band under AC 150/5345-10.

#### CCR Current Transformer

A current transformer used within or alongside a CCR to sense actual output current for feedback regulation
and for monitoring and fault-alarm reporting.

#### CCR Door Interlock

Interlock that changes or inhibits CCR operation when the cabinet door is opened, where required by the
equipment design.

#### CCR Electromagnetic Compatibility

Ability of the CCR to operate correctly in its electromagnetic environment without causing or suffering
unacceptable interference.

#### CCR Emergency Stop

Safety function that rapidly removes or inhibits CCR operation when an emergency stop command is applied.

#### CCR Fault Alarm

An indication raised by a regulator monitor, either a standalone L-827 monitor or the monitoring built into an
L-829 regulator, when a defined fault such as an open circuit, overcurrent or out-of-tolerance output current
is detected in the series circuit.

#### CCR Fault Monitoring

The function of detecting, acquiring and reporting CCR abnormal conditions such as protection trips, current
deviation, control faults or other defined alarms.

#### CCR Fault Reset

Controlled action that clears a latched CCR fault after the underlying cause has been removed or assessed.

#### CCR Harmonic Content

Frequency components of CCR input/output waveforms other than the fundamental that contribute to power-quality
distortion.

#### CCR Heat Sink

Thermal component that transfers heat from power semiconductor devices to the surrounding cooling medium.

#### CCR Input Current

Current drawn by the CCR from its electrical supply under the defined operating condition.

#### CCR Input Supply

The primary AC power feed, defined by voltage, phase and frequency, delivered to a CCR, as distinct from the
regulated constant-current output it produces for the series circuit.

#### CCR Intensity Step

One of a CCR's selectable output-current levels; FAA Style 1 regulators provide three brightness steps and
Style 2 regulators provide five, each step commanding a defined series-circuit current.

#### CCR Local Control

Operation of a CCR from controls mounted at the regulator or vault panel rather than from a remote source,
typically used for maintenance or when the communication link to the ALCMS is unavailable.

#### CCR Local Remote Selector

Selector determining whether CCR commands are accepted from the local control interface or remote system.

#### CCR Maintenance Bypass

Controlled bypass arrangement used to maintain or test a defined function while selected equipment is
isolated, only where the approved design permits it.

#### CCR Monitor Accuracy

The measurement tolerance, usually expressed as a percentage of reading or full scale, with which a CCR's
monitoring circuitry reports output current, voltage and status against a calibrated reference instrument.

#### CCR Open-Circuit Response

The protective action a CCR takes when the series-circuit loop is broken, since circuit resistance rises
sharply and the regulator would otherwise drive output voltage up to maintain current; monitors detect this as
an open-circuit fault and the CCR trips or limits voltage.

#### CCR Output Contactor

The electromechanical switching device within a CCR that connects or disconnects its regulated output to the
series circuit, actuated by control commands or fault logic.

#### CCR Output Current

Measured current delivered by the CCR into the series circuit during operation.

#### CCR Output Current Regulation

The accuracy with which a CCR maintains its rated output current at a selected brightness step, expressed as a
percentage tolerance and verified during commissioning against AC 150/5345-10 limits.

#### CCR Output Isolation

Electrical isolation between CCR output circuitry and other circuits or accessible parts as required by the
equipment design.

#### CCR Output Measurement

A reading of a CCR's actual output current and voltage, taken via a digital meter or the regulator's current
transformer/monitor, and compared against the specified value for the selected step.

#### CCR Output Power

Electrical power delivered by the CCR to the series circuit under the specified load and current step.

#### CCR Output Ripple

Periodic variation superimposed on the nominal CCR output current or voltage.

#### CCR Output Voltage

CCR output voltage is the voltage developed by the constant-current regulator across the connected series
circuit under a defined load and intensity step.

#### CCR Overcurrent Protection

A protective function that trips or limits a CCR when its output current exceeds a set threshold, guarding the
regulator and downstream isolation transformers from damage.

#### CCR Reference Current

Target current value used by the CCR control loop for a selected intensity step.

#### CCR Regulator Characteristic

Relationship between CCR control setting and regulated series-circuit output under defined load conditions.

#### CCR Regulator Monitor

A device that continuously checks regulator output and series-circuit condition and reports faults such as
open circuit, overcurrent or out-of-tolerance current to local or remote control. Under FAA AC 150/5345-10 it
is either a standalone L-827 monitor or the monitoring integral to an L-829 regulator; an L-828 regulator has
no monitoring.

#### CCR Regulator Monitor Interface

Interface through which the CCR regulator and its monitor exchange operating values, alarms and status
information.

#### CCR Remote Command

Control instruction received from an external ALCMS or control system to change CCR state, step or function.

#### CCR Remote Control

A control interface or communication function that allows an authorized command system to select or control
CCR operating states remotely.

#### CCR Remote Status

Status information transmitted from the CCR to a remote monitoring/control system.

#### CCR Short-Circuit Response

The protective action a CCR takes when a low-impedance path bypasses part of the series circuit, since the
reduced circuit resistance would otherwise push output current above the setpoint if the regulator did not
compensate or trip.

#### CCR Soft Start

Controlled rise of CCR output during startup intended to limit transient stress and avoid abrupt current
application.

#### CCR Status Feedback

The signal a CCR returns to the ALCMS or control panel confirming its present operating state, including
on/off, selected brightness step, remote/local mode, and any active fault.

#### CCR Step CCR Intensity Step

One selectable CCR operating level that commands a defined series-circuit current and therefore a
corresponding lighting intensity.

#### CCR Step Accuracy

Closeness of the actual regulated output current to the specified current for a selected CCR step.

#### CCR Step Selector

The control, whether a physical switch, relay logic, or software command, used to choose which of a CCR's
available brightness steps is applied to the series circuit.

#### CCR Step Transition

Change in regulated output current as the CCR moves from one intensity step to another.

#### CCR Surge Protection

Lightning and transient-voltage protection, such as surge arrestors, fitted to a CCR's input and output to
protect the regulator and connected series circuit from induced surges.

#### CCR Thermal Protection

A temperature-sensing protective function that shuts down or derates a CCR if internal components, such as
windings or power semiconductors, exceed a safe operating temperature.

#### CCR Undervoltage Protection

A protective function that trips or alarms a CCR when its input supply voltage falls below a specified
threshold, preventing unstable or out-of-tolerance regulated output.

#### Certificate of Conformity

A document issued by a manufacturer or supplier declaring that a product meets the specified standard or
contract requirements.

#### Changeover Time

Elapsed time required for a power or lighting system to transfer from one source/configuration to another
after a defined failure or command.

#### Chock Aircraft Wheel Chock

A wedge placed against an aircraft's wheels to prevent it moving while parked.

#### Chromaticity

Specification of colour independent of brightness using coordinates derived from a colour space such as CIE
chromaticity diagrams.

#### Chromaticity Coordinates

The x,y values on the CIE chromaticity diagram that define a light's exact colour, used to verify a fixture's
output falls within the colour boundaries specified for its signal type.

#### Circuit Breaker

A resettable protective switching device that interrupts an electrical circuit when specified overcurrent or
fault conditions occur.

#### Circuit Breaker Coordination

Circuit Breaker Coordination is the engineering process of selecting and setting protective devices so a fault
is cleared by the nearest appropriate protective device while maintaining service to unaffected portions of
the electrical system.

#### Circuit Identification

The labelling and record-keeping system used to uniquely identify each AGL circuit, fixture or cable run so it
can be located, tested and maintained without confusion with adjacent circuits.

#### Circuit Load

The electrical demand connected to a circuit, expressed through the current/power characteristics used for
design and equipment selection.

#### Circuit Resistance

The total electrical resistance of a series lighting circuit's conductors, terminations and transformer
primaries; the CCR must develop enough output voltage to force its set current through this resistance, so it
is checked by loop or insulation-resistance testing.

#### Clamp Meter

An electrical measuring instrument that measures current through a conductor using a clamp around the
conductor, reducing the need to open the circuit.

#### Closed Marking (X)

A cross displayed at each end of a closed runway or taxiway, or portion of one, to show the surface is
unusable. ICAO specifies white on a runway and yellow on a taxiway; FAA practice uses yellow crosses. Lighting
on a closed surface should not be operated.

#### Color Rendering Index

A measure of how accurately a light source reveals the true colours of illuminated objects compared with a
reference light source, expressed on a scale up to 100.

#### Colorimetry

The measurement and specification of light colour, typically expressed as chromaticity coordinates or dominant
wavelength, used to verify AGL fixtures emit the correct colour for their function.

#### Combined Standard Uncertainty

The overall standard uncertainty of a measurement result, obtained by combining individual input uncertainty
components in quadrature (root-sum-of-squares) per the GUM uncertainty framework.

#### Commissioning

The structured process of inspecting, testing, adjusting and verifying installed equipment or systems so they
can be placed into intended service.

#### Commissioning Report

A document recording the tests, measurements and checks performed before an AGL system is handed over,
confirming it meets the specified performance criteria.

#### Communication Cable

Cable used to carry data signals, such as between the ALCMS and field CCRs, as distinct from power cable.

#### Compliance Assessment

The process of comparing measured or observed results against a specification, standard or acceptance
criterion to determine whether an item passes or fails.

#### Compliance Matrix

A table cross-referencing project or system requirements against the specific standard clauses or design
features that satisfy them, used to demonstrate compliance.

#### Condition-Based Maintenance

Maintenance triggered by the measured or observed condition of equipment, such as declining photometric output
or rising insulation resistance, rather than by a fixed time interval.

#### Conditional Clearance

Movement clearance containing conditions that must be satisfied before the aircraft or vehicle may proceed.

#### Conduit Cable Conduit

A tube, rigid or flexible, used to enclose and protect a cable during and after installation.

#### Confidence Interval

Statistical interval associated with an estimated parameter and a stated confidence level under the adopted
statistical model.

#### Conflict Alerting

Conflict Alerting is a surface-movement safety function that identifies potentially conflicting aircraft or
vehicle movements from available surveillance and system data and generates an operational alert according to
approved system logic.

#### Connector Kit

A pre-packaged set of components, connector body, seals and boots, used to make a standard field-installed
cable connection, typically an L-823 style connector.

#### Connector Replacement

The removal and replacement of a worn, damaged or corroded cable connector to restore a reliable electrical
connection.

#### Contactor

An electrically controlled switching device used to make or break a power circuit under defined operating
conditions.

#### Continuity Test

A test used to verify that the intended conductive path has sufficiently low resistance and is electrically
continuous.

#### Control Cable

Cable carrying low-voltage control or signalling connections, such as between a CCR and its remote control
panel.

#### Control Panel

An enclosure containing electrical/control components used to distribute, switch, protect, interface or
control the associated AGL equipment.

#### Corrective Action

An action taken to eliminate the root cause of an identified nonconformance, distinct from a quick fix that
addresses only the symptom.

#### Corrective Maintenance

Maintenance carried out in response to an identified fault or failure, to restore equipment to working
condition.

#### Correlated Color Temperature

A single-number description, in kelvins, of the colour appearance of a white light source, used mainly for
apron floodlighting or white LED fixtures rather than coloured aeronautical signal lights.

#### Coverage Factor

Multiplier used to obtain expanded uncertainty from combined standard uncertainty.

#### Critical Area

A protected area around a navigational aid, such as an ILS, within which vehicles, aircraft or structures must
not enter or park when the aid is in use, to avoid signal interference. See also: ILS Critical Area; ILS
Sensitive Area.

#### Critical Lighting Circuit

AGL circuit whose availability is essential to a defined operational function, especially during low-
visibility operations.

#### Critical Lighting Equipment

AGL equipment whose failure can directly affect a required operational lighting function.

#### Current Regulation

A CCR's core function of holding its output current fixed at the selected step regardless of the resistance
the connected series circuit presents, which is what keeps every lamp on the circuit at uniform brightness.

#### Cutoff Angle

The angle above which a fixture is designed to emit no light, used to control glare and stray light outside
the intended beam.

### D

#### Data Validation Photometric Data Validation

The process of checking recorded photometric, electrical or inspection data for errors, out-of-range values or
inconsistencies before it is accepted into a report or record.

#### Deep Base

A base can with a greater burial depth, typically used for elevated fixtures or where ducting requires
additional clearance.

#### Destination Sign

Sign identifying a destination such as an apron, terminal area, cargo area or other operational destination.

#### DGCA Directorate General of Civil Aviation

Directorate General of Civil Aviation — India's civil aviation safety regulator, responsible for aerodrome
licensing and enforcement of Indian requirements for AGL performance and maintenance.

#### Dielectric Test Dielectric Withstand Test

A test in which insulation is subjected to a specified electrical stress to verify dielectric withstand.

#### Dimensional Inspection

Measurement of specified physical dimensions and comparison with the approved drawing, standard or acceptance
criterion.

#### Dimming

Controlled reduction or adjustment of light output by changing the operating condition of the lighting source
or driver.

#### Direction Sign

Sign providing directional information toward one or more taxiways, runways, aprons or other aerodrome
destinations.

#### Discrimination

Ability of protective devices to distinguish fault conditions and isolate the intended section without
unnecessary upstream interruption.

#### Displaced Threshold

A runway threshold located at a point other than the physical start of the runway, reducing the usable landing
distance while the full length remains available for takeoff or roll-out.

#### Document Control

The system of numbering, versioning, approval and distribution used to manage project drawings, reports and
records so the correct revision is always in use.

#### Duct Cable Duct

A pipe or channel, installed underground, through which cables are pulled and protected.

#### Dynamic Taxi Routing

Generation or modification of a taxi route in response to traffic, closures, operational constraints or system
conditions.

### E

#### Earth Electrode

A conductive element installed in contact with soil to provide the connection between an earthing system and
the general mass of earth.

#### Earth Pit Earth Pit / Grounding Pit

An enclosure or accessible point used to house/protect an earth electrode connection and facilitate inspection
or testing of the grounding system.

#### Efficiency Test

A test measuring the ratio of useful output, light or power, to input power for a fixture, transformer or CCR,
to verify it meets its rated efficiency.

#### Electrical Clearance

The minimum required physical distance between an energised conductor or component and another object, person
or structure, maintained to prevent flashover or contact.

#### Electrical Safety

The set of practices, procedures and equipment used to prevent injury from contact with, or proximity to,
energised electrical equipment.

#### Electrical Test

A general term for tests such as insulation resistance, continuity, voltage and current, performed to verify
the electrical integrity of an AGL circuit or component.

#### Elevated Light Fixture

An AGL light fixture mounted above the pavement on an approved support or mounting arrangement to provide the
required visual indication.

#### Emergency Stop

A manually initiated safety function intended to place affected equipment into a defined safe or stopped state
during an emergency.

#### Environmental Test

A controlled test exposing equipment to specified environmental conditions to verify the required performance
or durability.

#### Equipotential Bonding

Electrical bonding that connects conductive parts together so that potential differences between them are
minimized under normal or fault conditions.

#### Ethernet

Ethernet is a family of wired computer-networking technologies used to exchange digital data between networked
devices through defined physical and data-link communication methods.

#### Event Log

A chronological record of alarms, faults, switching operations or other system events captured by the ALCMS or
CCR controller. See also: ALCMS Event Log.

#### Expanded Uncertainty

Measurement uncertainty obtained by multiplying the combined standard uncertainty by a stated coverage factor.

### F

#### FAA Federal Aviation Administration

Federal Aviation Administration — the United States civil aviation authority, whose AC 150 series Advisory
Circulars on airport lighting are widely referenced internationally for AGL equipment and installation
practice.

#### FAA AC 150/5340 Series FAA Advisory Circular 150/5340 Series

FAA Advisory Circular series covering airport visual aids: standards and guidance for the design, installation
and maintenance of airport markings, signs and lighting. Equipment specifications sit in the AC 150/5345
series.

#### FAA AC 150/5345 Series FAA Advisory Circular 150/5345 Series

FAA Advisory Circular series specifying airport lighting equipment such as constant current regulators,
isolation transformers, connectors and lighting control and monitoring systems.

#### FAA AC 150/5345-26E FAA Specification for L-823 Plug and Receptacle, Cable Connectors

FAA specification (edition E, issued December 2021) for L-823 plug and receptacle cable connectors used with
underground power cables, isolation transformer leads and light fixture leads. Confirm the edition in force
before citing.

#### FAA AC 150/5345-47C FAA Specification for Series to Series Isolation Transformers

FAA specification (edition C, July 2011) for series-to-series isolation transformers used in airport lighting
systems, including their L-830 type ratings by wattage and current. Confirm the edition in force before
citing.

#### Factory Acceptance Test

A controlled test performed at the manufacturer or approved facility to verify specified equipment functions
and performance before shipment or site installation. See also: FAT.

#### Factory Inspection

An inspection of equipment or materials carried out at the manufacturer's premises, before shipment, to verify
build quality and specification compliance.

#### Fail-Safe Lighting Arrangement

Lighting/control arrangement designed so that a defined failure drives the system toward a predetermined safe
condition.

#### FAT Factory Acceptance Test

The formal test event, held at the manufacturer's works, where the purchaser or their representative witnesses
equipment performance against the agreed test procedure before shipment. See also: Factory Acceptance Test.

#### Fault Log

A record listing each fault detected on an AGL system, including date, description, affected circuit and
corrective action taken.

#### Fiber Optic Cable

Cable using optical fiber to carry data signals over long distances with immunity to electrical interference,
increasingly used for AGL monitoring and control networks.

#### Field Photometry

Field photometry is the measurement of the photometric performance of installed aerodrome lighting equipment
at the airport using calibrated instruments and defined measurement geometry.

#### Filter Optical Filter

A component fitted to a fixture to alter its transmitted light, most commonly a coloured filter used to
produce a specific aeronautical signal colour from a white light source.

#### Final Inspection

The last inspection performed on completed work or equipment before handover, confirming all outstanding items
from earlier inspections have been closed.

#### Fixture Alignment

The adjustment of a fixture's aiming angle back to its design position, carried out when inspection finds it
has shifted out of tolerance.

#### Fixture Base Installation

The installation of an AGL fixture's mounting base or can, set to the correct depth, level and orientation
before the fixture itself is fitted.

#### Fixture Cable Entry

The point and method by which a supply cable enters a fixture housing, sealed to maintain the enclosure's
ingress protection rating.

#### Fixture Cleaning

The removal of dirt, dust or contamination from a fixture's lens, reflector or prism to restore its rated
light output.

#### Fixture Connector Sealing

The sealing of a fixture's electrical connector, typically an L-823/L-830 style waterproof coupling, to
prevent moisture ingress at the joint.

#### Fixture Drainage

Provision within a fixture base or housing to allow water to drain away rather than collect around cable
entries and connectors.

#### Fixture Elevation

The height of an in-pavement or elevated fixture relative to the surrounding surface, controlled to meet
frangibility and photometric siting requirements.

#### Fixture Fastener

The bolts, screws or clips used to secure a fixture to its base or mounting, tightened to the manufacturer's
specified torque.

#### Fixture Frangible Mounting

A mounting design that allows a fixture to break away cleanly on impact, reducing damage to an aircraft that
strikes it.

#### Fixture Functional Check

A quick verification, usually visual and electrical, that an installed or maintained fixture illuminates and
operates as intended.

#### Fixture Grouting

The filling of the annular gap around an in-pavement fixture base with grout, providing a stable, level
surface and reducing water ingress.

#### Fixture Housing

The outer body of a light fixture, providing structural support, weatherproofing and mounting for the internal
optical and electrical components.

#### Fixture Identification

The unique reference, tag, serial number or location code assigned to each AGL fixture so it can be tracked
through installation, testing, maintenance and replacement.

#### Fixture Leveling

Adjustment of a fixture during installation so its top surface sits flush with, and parallel to, the
surrounding pavement.

#### Fixture Optical Cleaning

Cleaning of a fixture's lens or optical surfaces to remove dirt, rubber deposits or film that would otherwise
reduce light output.

#### Fixture Orientation

The rotational alignment of a fixture's beam relative to the runway or taxiway centreline, set to meet the
required azimuth.

#### Fixture Reinstallation

The refitting of a fixture into its base after removal for maintenance, repair or replacement.

#### Fixture Replacement

The removal of a failed or end-of-life fixture and its substitution with a new or refurbished unit of the
correct type.

#### Fixture Seating

The correct, fully engaged fit of a fixture into its base or mounting, confirmed before final fastening.

#### Fixture Torque

The tightening force applied to a fixture's fasteners, specified by the manufacturer to secure the unit
without damaging the housing or seal.

#### Fixture Visual Inspection

A visual examination of an installed fixture's condition, alignment, cleanliness and physical damage.

#### Fixture Water Ingress

Water entry into a fixture housing or connector, typically through a failed seal, that can damage optics,
electronics or insulation.

#### FOD Foreign Object Debris / Foreign Object Damage

Foreign Object Debris is material or an object in the aviation environment that can create a hazard or cause
damage; Foreign Object Damage is the resulting damage.

#### FOD Control Foreign Object Debris Control

The procedures used to prevent, detect and remove foreign object debris from the movement area.

#### FOD Prevention

Measures taken to prevent foreign object debris, such as loose fasteners, tools or materials, from being left
on or entering the movement area, where it could damage aircraft or engines.

#### Follow-Me Vehicle

A marked airside vehicle used to guide an aircraft, typically on the ground, from the runway to its parking
position or vice versa.

#### Foreign Object Inspection

Foreign Object Inspection is a systematic inspection of the movement area and associated work areas to
identify foreign objects, debris or conditions that could damage aircraft, vehicles, personnel or airport
infrastructure.

#### Frangible Coupling

A mounting designed to break away cleanly under impact, reducing the risk of damage to an aircraft that
strikes an elevated fixture such as an approach light tower.

#### Frequency Variation

Variation of the AC supply frequency from its nominal value. In AGL systems, frequency variation can affect
equipment designed for a specific supply frequency and should be evaluated against the applicable equipment
specification.

#### Functional Test

A test that verifies the intended operation of a system or component through its specified command, response,
indication and protective functions.

#### Fuse

An overcurrent protective device that opens its circuit when the current exceeds its specified operating
characteristic.

### G

#### Gasket

A sealing component fitted between two mating surfaces of a fixture or enclosure to prevent water and dust
ingress.

#### Goniophotometer

Photometric instrument/system that measures light output as a function of direction by controlling or
measuring angular position.

#### GPU Ground Power Unit

A mobile or fixed unit supplying electrical power to a parked aircraft so its engines and APU can remain shut
down. See also: Ground Power Unit.

#### Ground Movement Display

An air traffic control workstation display, typically fed by surface surveillance such as A-SMGCS, showing
aircraft and vehicle positions, taxi routes and lighting or guidance status across the movement area.

#### Ground Power Unit

A mobile or fixed unit supplying electrical power to a parked aircraft so its engines and APU can remain shut
down while systems stay powered. See also: GPU.

#### Grounding

The electrical practice of establishing a conductive reference or fault-current path to ground/earth as
required by the applicable electrical design.

#### Guidance Function

Function that provides route or movement guidance to an aircraft or vehicle using system information and
available visual aids.

#### Guidance Status Feedback

Feedback indicating whether the commanded guidance state has been achieved and is being monitored.

### H

#### Halogen Lamp

An incandescent-type lamp containing halogen gas, which extends filament life and maintains more consistent
light output compared with a standard incandescent lamp, used in some AGL fixtures.

#### Handhole Cable Handhole

A shallow, below-grade access enclosure, smaller than a manhole, installed along an underground duct route to
permit cable jointing, transformer housing, or inspection without excavation.

#### Harmonic Distortion

Distortion of an AC waveform caused by harmonic components relative to the fundamental frequency.

#### Hazard Identification

The process of recognising conditions or activities that could cause harm, carried out before work begins so
risks can be assessed and controlled.

#### Heat Sink

A component, typically finned metal, designed to conduct heat away from an LED module or electronic component
and dissipate it to the surrounding air.

#### HIALS High Intensity Approach Lighting System

High Intensity Approach Lighting System providing high-intensity approach visual guidance to support the
transition from instrument approach to runway visual reference.

#### High Voltage Test

A dielectric withstand test in which a voltage above normal operating level is applied to a cable or component
to confirm its insulation can withstand system voltage without breakdown. See also: HV Test.

#### HIRL High Intensity Runway Lights

High Intensity Runway Lights (HIRL) provide high-intensity runway-edge guidance for operations requiring
enhanced visual conspicuity.

#### HMI Human-Machine Interface

A Human-Machine Interface (HMI) is the operator interface through which users view system status, alarms and
controls and issue commands to an automated system.

#### Holding Bay

A defined area where aircraft can be held, or bypassed, to make surface movement more efficient (ICAO). It is
often a widened area beside a taxiway near a runway entrance.

#### Humidity Test

A controlled environmental test used to assess equipment performance or insulation/sealing behaviour under
specified humidity conditions.

#### HV Test High Voltage Test

A high-voltage electrical test in which a specified test voltage is applied to verify the withstand or
insulation condition of the equipment/circuit under the approved procedure. See also: High Voltage Test.

#### HV Tester High Voltage Tester

A test instrument designed to apply or measure high-voltage test conditions for specified electrical
insulation or dielectric tests.

### I

#### ICAO International Civil Aviation Organization

International Civil Aviation Organization — the UN specialized agency that sets international Standards and
Recommended Practices (SARPs) for aerodrome design and operation, including AGL, chiefly through Annex 14.

#### ICAO Annex 14 ICAO Annex 14 Aerodromes

The ICAO annex governing aerodrome design and operations; Volume I sets the core international standards and
recommended practices for AGL siting, photometric performance and reliability.

#### Identification Beacon

A beacon that provides a coded or distinctive visual signal used to identify the aerodrome or facility.

#### Identification Function

Function that associates a detected surface target with an aircraft, vehicle or other operational identity.

#### IEC International Electrotechnical Commission

International Electrotechnical Commission — publishes international electrical and electronic equipment
standards, several of which underpin AGL power supply, cabling and equipment design.

#### IEC 60364 IEC 60364 series for low-voltage electrical installations

IEC standard series for low-voltage electrical installations, referenced for cabling, protection and earthing
practice on AGL power circuits.

#### IEC 60598 IEC 60598 series for luminaires

IEC 60598 is a family of standards for luminaires and related requirements; its applicability to a particular
airport light depends on the product construction and the governing AGL specification.

#### Illuminance

Photometric quantity equal to luminous flux incident on a surface per unit area.

#### ILS Critical Area Instrument Landing System Critical Area

A protected ground area around an Instrument Landing System antenna, within which vehicle and aircraft
movement is restricted when the ILS is in use by an aircraft on approach, to prevent signal reflection or
blockage. See also: Critical Area; ILS Sensitive Area.

#### ILS Sensitive Area Instrument Landing System Sensitive Area

An area extending beyond the ILS critical area where the parking or movement of aircraft and vehicles is
controlled to prevent unacceptable interference with the ILS signal, particularly during low-visibility
operations.

#### In-Process Inspection

An inspection carried out during manufacture or installation, rather than at the start or end, to catch
defects before further work is built on top of them.

#### Incandescent Lamp

A traditional lamp producing light from a heated filament, still found in some older AGL fixtures ahead of LED
conversion.

#### Incoming Inspection Incoming Material Inspection

An inspection performed on materials or equipment when they arrive on site, checking for transport damage and
confirming they match the order and specification.

#### Indian Standard (IS)

An Indian Standard (IS) is a standard published by the Bureau of Indian Standards for a defined product,
material, process, test method or other subject.

#### Information Sign

Sign providing operational information that does not itself constitute a mandatory instruction or movement
clearance.

#### Inset Cleaning Inset Light Cleaning

Cleaning specifically of inset, flush-mounted fixtures, whose recessed lenses are prone to collecting rubber
deposits, dirt and standing water.

#### Inset Light Fixture

An AGL light fixture designed for installation substantially flush with the pavement surface, with its
optical, mechanical and load characteristics controlled by the applicable fixture design.

#### Inspection Report

A document recording the findings of a physical or functional inspection of AGL equipment against a checklist
or specification.

#### Inspection Test Plan Inspection and Test Plan

A document listing every inspection and test required for a scope of work, in sequence, identifying who
performs each one and which are hold or witness points.

#### Instrument Identification

The recording of the make, model and calibration status of the test instrument used for a given measurement,
so results can be traced to a verified instrument.

#### Instrument Warm-Up

The period a photometric or electrical test instrument is allowed to stabilise after power-up before readings
are taken, required because sensor and electronic drift settle over time.

#### Insulation Breakdown

Loss of dielectric integrity allowing excessive leakage or an unintended conductive path through the
insulation system.

#### Insulation Coordination

The design process of selecting insulation levels and surge protection so that, under overvoltage conditions,
protective devices operate before insulation is damaged.

#### Insulation Monitoring

Monitoring of insulation condition or leakage to detect deterioration that could compromise electrical
isolation or cause an earth fault.

#### Insulation Test

A megohmmeter test measuring the insulation resistance of a cable or winding, used to detect insulation
degradation or moisture ingress before energising.

#### Intensity Step

A defined selectable operating level of an AGL lighting system that corresponds to a controlled light-output
condition, commonly selected through the CCR/control system.

#### Inter-Instrument Comparison

Comparison of measurements from two or more instruments measuring the same reference or test item.

#### Interlock

A control or protection function that prevents or constrains an operation when a specified permissive or safe
condition is not present.

#### Intermediate Holding Position

Intermediate Holding Position is a designated position on a taxiway where an aircraft or vehicle may be
required to hold for traffic sequencing or control, distinct from a runway holding position.

#### Intermittent Fault Intermittent Electrical Fault

A fault that appears and disappears as a function of movement, temperature, moisture, vibration, loading,
switching or another changing condition.

#### IP Rating Ingress Protection Rating

An enclosure protection classification defining the degree of protection against ingress of solids and water
according to the applicable IP classification standard.

#### ISO 9001 Quality Management Systems

International standard for quality management systems, often required of AGL manufacturers and contractors as
evidence of consistent process control and product quality.

#### Isolating Transformer

Series-to-series isolation transformer used to electrically isolate an individual airport-lighting load from
the primary series circuit while transferring power to the secondary load. Called an isolation transformer in
FAA documents. See also: Transformer Primary; Transformer Secondary.

#### Isolation Transformer Connector Lead

The short factory-terminated cable segment, primary or secondary, that extends from the isolation
transformer's potted winding to the L-823 plug or receptacle used to join it into the series or fixture
circuit.

#### Isolation Transformer Continuity Test

A test verifying an unbroken electrical path through the isolation transformer's primary and secondary
windings, typically performed with an ohmmeter before energizing or re-energizing a series circuit.

#### Isolation Transformer Dielectric Test

A hipot (high-potential) test applying an elevated AC or DC voltage between a transformer's primary and
secondary windings, and between windings and ground, to confirm the insulation withstands its specified test
voltage without breakdown.

#### Isolation Transformer Fault

A failure condition in an isolation transformer, such as an open or shorted winding, insulation breakdown, or
moisture ingress, that interrupts or degrades power transfer to the connected fixture.

#### Isolation Transformer Housing

The potted or resin-encapsulated enclosure that protects an isolation transformer's core and windings from
moisture and mechanical damage in its below-grade or in-base installation.

#### Isolation Transformer Impedance

The transformer's internal opposition to current flow, arising from winding resistance and leakage reactance,
which affects voltage regulation and current transfer between the series circuit and the connected fixture.

#### Isolation Transformer Insulation

The dielectric material, potting compound and winding insulation that electrically isolates the primary series
circuit from the secondary fixture circuit and withstands the transformer's rated test voltage.

#### Isolation Transformer Moisture Ingress

Water intrusion into a transformer housing or connector interface, typically through a failed seal, that
degrades insulation resistance and can progress to an insulation or dielectric fault.

#### Isolation Transformer Polarity

The defined orientation relationship between an isolation transformer's primary and secondary windings,
relevant to correct lead connection during installation and replacement.

#### Isolation Transformer Primary

The isolation transformer winding connected directly into the constant-current series circuit; it carries the
regulated series-circuit current, such as 6.6 A or 20 A.

#### Isolation Transformer Secondary

The winding connected to the individual light fixture. It supplies the lamp or LED-driver current at the
voltage that fixture needs, while staying electrically isolated from the series circuit.

#### Isolation Transformer Temperature Rise

The increase in winding temperature above ambient under rated load, measured to confirm the transformer's
thermal design stays within its insulation class limits.

#### Isolation Transformer Turns Ratio

The ratio of primary to secondary winding turns. For a 6.6 A series circuit feeding a 6.6 A lamp the ratio is
typically 1:1 (6.6 A / 6.6 A); other types, such as 20 A / 6.6 A units on 20 A circuits, step the series
current down to the lamp current.

#### Isolation Transformer VA Rating

The transformer's rated apparent power capacity in volt-amperes, sized to match or exceed the connected
fixture's load without exceeding the transformer's thermal limits.

#### ITP Hold Point Inspection Test Plan Hold Point

A stage in an Inspection Test Plan beyond which work may not proceed until a specified party has inspected and
formally released it.

### J

#### Jet Bridge Passenger Boarding Bridge

A movable, enclosed passenger bridge connecting a terminal gate to an aircraft door.

### K

#### kcmil Thousand Circular Mils, MCM

A unit used to specify the cross-sectional area of large power cable conductors, commonly used for primary
feeder cables supplying series airfield lighting circuits.

#### Kelvin K, Colour Temperature

SI base unit of thermodynamic temperature, symbol K. In lighting it is the unit used to state correlated
colour temperature: lower values look warm (yellowish), higher values cool (blue-white).

#### Key-Operated Switch

A control switch requiring a physical key to change state, used at constant current regulators or control
panels to restrict unauthorised operation of airfield lighting circuits.

#### kVA Rating Kilovolt-Ampere Rating

The apparent power rating of a constant current regulator, isolating transformer or other electrical
equipment, expressed in kilovolt-amperes.

### L

#### L-823 Connector FAA L-823 Connector

Standardized plug/receptacle cable connector used to make detachable electrical connections in airport
lighting circuits.

#### L-823 Connector Cable Preparation

The process of stripping, measuring and dressing a cable end to the dimensions specified in AC 150/5345-26,
prior to crimping and assembling an L-823 plug or receptacle onto it.

#### L-823 Connector Contact

The metal pin or socket element inside an L-823 plug or receptacle body that makes the electrical connection
when the two halves are mated.

#### L-823 Connector Contact Resistance

The electrical resistance measured across a mated L-823 connector's contacts; elevated resistance indicates
corrosion, a poor crimp, or contact wear, and can cause localized heating or circuit faults.

#### L-823 Connector Crimp

The mechanical compression joint made between a cable conductor and an L-823 contact using a specified
crimping tool and die, forming the connector's primary electrical and mechanical connection.

#### L-823 Connector Field Installation

The on-site assembly of an L-823 connector kit onto cable ends, including cable preparation, crimping, contact
insertion and boot/seal closure, performed per the manufacturer's instructions and AC 150/5345-26.

#### L-823 Connector Identification

The style, class and type markings molded or stamped onto an L-823 connector body (e.g., "L-823, Style 3")
that identify its configuration for correct mating and replacement.

#### L-823 Connector Insulation

The connector body and boot material, typically an elastomer, providing dielectric separation and
environmental sealing around the mated contacts.

#### L-823 Connector Mating

The act of joining an L-823 plug and receptacle so their internal contacts engage and complete the circuit;
correct mating also compresses the connector's watertight seal.

#### L-823 Connector Moisture Protection

The sealing boot, gel fill or heat-shrink covering applied over a mated L-823 connector to prevent water
ingress into the below-grade splice.

#### L-823 Connector Plug

The male half of an L-823 connector pair, typically terminating the fixture or transformer lead, that inserts
into the corresponding receptacle.

#### L-823 Connector Receptacle

The female half of an L-823 connector pair, typically terminating the circuit cable, into which the
corresponding plug is inserted.

#### L-823 Connector Replacement

The removal and substitution of a damaged, corroded or failed L-823 connector, including cable re-preparation
and re-crimping, to restore a low-resistance, sealed connection.

#### L-823 Connector Sealing

The final step in connector assembly, where a boot, tape, gel or heat-shrink sleeve is applied to exclude
moisture from the mated connector and cable entry points.

#### L-823 Connector Visual Inspection

A physical examination of an L-823 connector for cracking, discoloration, corrosion, seal damage or incomplete
mating, typically performed during scheduled maintenance or fault investigation.

#### L-824 Cable FAA L-824 Cable

Cable manufactured to FAA specification L-824, the standard for airport lighting cable used in series
circuits.

#### Laboratory Photometry

Photometric testing of a fixture performed on a goniophotometer under controlled indoor conditions, as opposed
to field measurements taken on the installed system.

#### Ladder Safety

Practices governing the safe selection, inspection and use of ladders, applicable when accessing elevated AGL
equipment such as approach lighting towers.

#### Lamp Life

The rated operating hours a lamp is expected to provide before failure or before its output falls below a
defined threshold, used to plan replacement intervals.

#### Lamp Replacement

The removal of a failed or degraded incandescent or halogen lamp and its replacement with a new one of the
correct rating.

#### Layout Drawing

A drawing showing the physical arrangement of AGL fixtures, cables and equipment across the aerodrome, used
for installation and reference.

#### Leakage Current

Small current that flows through insulation or to earth under normal operation, monitored because an abnormal
increase indicates insulation degradation.

#### LED Array

A grouping of multiple individual LED emitters mounted together within a fixture's light engine, combining
their output to produce the required total luminous intensity.

#### LED Chromaticity Shift

A change in an LED source's emitted color coordinates over its operating life, usually from phosphor or
semiconductor aging, which can move the fixture's output outside its specified color box.

#### LED Color Stability

The degree to which an LED light source maintains consistent chromaticity and intensity over its service life
and across its operating temperature range.

#### LED Degradation

The gradual reduction in light output of an LED source over its operating life, tracked to predict when a
fixture will fall below its minimum intensity requirement.

#### LED Dimming

The controlled reduction of an LED fixture's output, achieved by lowering drive current or through pulse-width
modulation, used to implement the fixture's brightness steps within a CCR-regulated series circuit.

#### LED Driver

LED Driver is an electronic power-conversion/control component that supplies the LED light source with the
electrical conditions required for stable and controlled operation.

#### LED Driver Current

The regulated current supplied by an LED fixture's internal driver circuit to its LED array, matched to the
LEDs' rated forward current to achieve correct output and lifespan.

#### LED Driver Replacement

The removal and substitution of a failed or degraded LED driver module within a fixture, restoring correct
current regulation to the LED array.

#### LED Environmental Rating

The ingress protection (IP) and temperature or vibration rating of an LED fixture, specifying its suitability
for the below-grade or exposed outdoor conditions found in airfield lighting installations.

#### LED Failure Mode

The characteristic way an LED fixture degrades or fails, such as gradual lumen depreciation, individual
emitter dropout, or driver failure, as distinct from the abrupt filament failure typical of incandescent
lamps.

#### LED Harmonic Distortion

Distortion of the current waveform drawn by an LED driver from the series circuit, which must be kept within
limits so it does not interfere with CCR regulation or other equipment on the circuit.

#### LED Heat Sink

The thermally conductive structure, typically metal, that conducts heat away from an LED array's junction to
the fixture body or ambient air, limiting junction temperature to preserve output and lifespan.

#### LED Inrush Current

The brief current surge drawn by an LED driver at the moment power is applied or a series circuit is
energized, which the CCR and protection equipment must tolerate without nuisance tripping.

#### LED Intensity Control

The mechanism, whether analog current reduction or digital signaling, by which an LED fixture's brightness is
set to match the series circuit's commanded intensity step.

#### LED Junction Temperature

The temperature at the semiconductor junction inside an LED emitter; the key parameter governing its light
output, efficiency and long-term reliability.

#### LED Lens

The optical element, often a precision-molded polymer lens, that shapes an LED fixture's raw emitter output
into the required beam pattern and intensity distribution.

#### LED Lifetime

The rated operating life of an LED light source, typically expressed as hours to a specified lumen-maintenance
threshold such as L70, generally far exceeding that of incandescent lamps.

#### LED Light Engine

The integrated assembly of LED array, driver electronics, heat sink and optics that together produce a
fixture's specified photometric output.

#### LED Light Source

A solid-state light source based on light-emitting diodes used to generate controlled optical output in an AGL
fixture.

#### LED Module

A pre-assembled unit combining LED sources, driver electronics and optics, designed as a replaceable light-
source assembly within a fixture.

#### LED Module Replacement

The removal and substitution of a complete LED light engine or module in a fixture, typically handled as a
single field-replaceable unit rather than individual component repair.

#### LED Optical Efficiency

The proportion of an LED source's generated light that is successfully directed into the fixture's useful beam
by its lens or reflector, after accounting for optical losses.

#### LED Optical Module

The lens, reflector and associated optical housing that shapes an LED light engine's output into the fixture's
required beam pattern.

#### LED Prism

A refractive optical element used in some LED fixture designs to redirect or shape light output where a simple
lens alone cannot achieve the required distribution.

#### LED Redundancy

A fixture design feature in which multiple LED emitters or circuits operate in parallel, so a single emitter's
failure causes only a partial, rather than total, loss of fixture output.

#### LED Reflector

A shaped, reflective optical surface within a fixture that redirects LED emitter output into the required beam
pattern, often used together with, or instead of, a lens.

#### LED Replacement

The removal and replacement of a failed or degraded LED light source or module.

#### LED Retrofit

The replacement of a legacy incandescent or halogen airfield light fixture's lamp and optical assembly with an
LED light engine, while reusing the existing base can and, where compatible, the wiring.

#### LED Temperature Derating

The manufacturer-specified reduction in an LED fixture's drive current or output at elevated ambient
temperature, applied to keep the LED junction temperature within its rated limit.

#### LED Thermal Management

The overall design approach, combining heat sinking, thermal derating and enclosure design, used to keep an
LED fixture's junction temperature within limits across its rated environmental range.

#### Lens Discoloration

Yellowing, clouding or fading of a fixture's optical lens caused by UV exposure, heat or contamination, which
reduces transmitted light and can shift colour.

#### Level Check

A verification of installed elevation, level or slope against the applicable reference datum and tolerance.

#### Light Beam

The directional pattern in which a light fixture emits its luminous intensity, described by its beam axis (the
aiming reference, usually close to the direction of peak intensity) and beam spread (the angular range over
which intensity stays above a stated fraction of the peak). For airfield lights, the required beam shape and
minimum intensities are given by the applicable isocandela diagram.

#### Light Output

The optical output produced by a light source or fixture, which may be characterized by luminous flux,
luminous intensity or another defined photometric quantity.

#### Light Output Degradation

The gradual fall in a fixture’s luminous output over its service life, for example from lamp or LED ageing and
from dirt or discolouration on the optics. It is expressed as a reduction from the initial or rated intensity
and is checked against the minimum intensity required for the light.

#### Lighting Availability in LVP

Availability of required AGL functions during low-visibility operations, considering failed units, circuits,
controls and redundancy.

#### Lighting Guidance Command

Command sent to an AGL control system to establish a defined visual-guidance state.

#### Lighting System Availability

Proportion of required operating time during which the specified lighting function is capable of performing
its intended service.

#### Lighting System Reliability

Probability or demonstrated ability of the lighting system to perform its required function for a specified
operating period under defined conditions.

#### Lightning Protection

A coordinated system of measures intended to intercept, conduct and dissipate lightning current while limiting
damage and hazardous potential differences.

#### LIRL Low Intensity Runway Lights

Low Intensity Runway Lights (LIRL) provide low-intensity runway-edge guidance for runway operations where the
approved lighting system uses the low-intensity class.

#### Load Calculation

The design calculation of a series circuit's total connected load, based on the number and VA rating of lamps
and isolation transformers plus cable impedance, used to size a CCR and confirm it can drive the circuit
within its rated capacity.

#### Load Test

A test performed with a defined electrical or mechanical load to verify equipment performance under
representative operating conditions.

#### Load Verification

Confirmation that the connected AGL load matches the design/CCR capability and expected circuit loading.

#### Location Sign

Sign identifying the taxiway, runway or other movement-area location at which the sign is installed.

#### Lockout Tagout Lockout / Tagout

A safety procedure in which an isolated circuit or piece of equipment is physically locked in the off position
and tagged, preventing it from being re-energised while work is in progress.

#### Low Visibility Approach

Approach conducted under reduced visibility using the applicable approach lighting, runway lighting and
instrument/operational procedures.

#### Low Visibility Inspection

Targeted inspection confirming the serviceability of critical visual aids, controls, power and monitoring
before or during low-visibility operations.

#### Low Visibility Landing

Landing under reduced visibility using the applicable approach/runway visual aids, procedures and landing
minima.

#### Low Visibility Operations

Low Visibility Operations are aerodrome operations conducted under defined reduced-visibility conditions that
require specific procedures, minima, visual aids, surface-movement controls and system readiness measures.

#### Low Visibility Procedures LVP

Operational procedures applied when visibility is reduced below defined conditions and additional controls,
including enhanced visual aids, are required for safe aircraft and vehicle movement.

#### Low Visibility Takeoff

Takeoff operation conducted under reduced visibility with the applicable runway lighting, procedures and
operational minima in force.

#### Low Visibility Taxiing

Taxi operation under reduced visibility requiring enhanced surface guidance, lighting conspicuity and movement
control.

#### Lumen

SI unit of luminous flux; symbol lm.

#### Luminance

Photometric quantity describing luminous intensity per unit projected area in a specified direction; unit
cd/m².

#### Luminous Flux

Photometric quantity representing the total luminous power evaluated according to the spectral luminous-
efficiency function; unit lumen.

#### Luminous Intensity

Photometric quantity describing luminous flux emitted by a source per unit solid angle in a specified
direction.

#### Lux

SI unit of illuminance; symbol lx. One lux equals one lumen per square metre.

#### LVP Lighting Failure Response

Defined operational and maintenance response when a critical lighting function fails during low-visibility
conditions.

#### LVP Lighting Test
