Test confirming that the lighting functions required for an LVP configuration respond correctly to commands
and faults.

#### LVP Maintenance Restriction

Maintenance limitation applied during low-visibility operations to prevent work from reducing required
lighting availability or creating an unsafe condition.

### M

#### Magnetic Heading

The direction in which an aircraft's nose is pointing, measured clockwise from magnetic north. Runway
designators are derived from the runway's magnetic bearing, rounded to the nearest 10 degrees.

#### Main Supply

Normal electrical source feeding the AGL power-distribution system under ordinary operating conditions.

#### Maintenance Log

A chronological record of maintenance activities performed on AGL equipment, including routine, preventive and
corrective work.

#### Maintenance Safety Boundary

A defined physical or procedural boundary around a maintenance work site, restricting aircraft, vehicle or
personnel access while work is in progress.

#### Mandatory Instruction Sign

Sign displaying a mandatory instruction, typically identifying a runway holding position or other location
where a specified movement restriction applies.

#### Manhole Cable Manhole

A below-grade access chamber, sized for personnel entry, installed along an underground duct route to house
cable joints or equipment and to provide access for cable pulling, jointing, inspection and maintenance.

#### Manoeuvring Area

The part of an aerodrome used for takeoff, landing and taxiing, excluding aprons.

#### Marshalling Aircraft Marshalling

The use of visual hand or wand signals by a ground crew member to guide an aircraft during taxi, parking or
pushback.

#### Material Test Certificate

A document issued by a material manufacturer certifying the chemical, mechanical or electrical properties of a
specific batch of material.

#### Maximum Intensity Maximum Luminous Intensity

The highest luminous intensity value recorded within a fixture's photometric distribution, typically at or
near the beam centre.

#### Measurement Error

Difference between a measured quantity value and a reference/true quantity value as defined for the
measurement context.

#### Measurement Geometry

Measurement Geometry is the defined spatial relationship among the measurement instrument, light source or
test object, reference points, angles, distances and measurement surface used to obtain a valid measurement.

#### Measurement Plane

The defined surface or set of points, at a specified distance and orientation from a fixture, at which
photometric readings are taken.

#### Measurement Point

A single defined location within a measurement plane or grid at which a photometric reading is recorded.

#### Measurement Uncertainty

Parameter characterizing the dispersion of values that could reasonably be attributed to the measured
quantity.

#### Megger Test Insulation Resistance Test

A field term commonly used for an insulation-resistance measurement performed with a megohmmeter; the actual
test voltage and method must follow the approved procedure.

#### Megohmmeter Insulation Resistance Tester

An electrical test instrument used to measure high resistance, particularly insulation resistance, by applying
a specified DC test voltage.

#### Method Statement

A document describing the sequence, resources and safety controls for carrying out a specific work activity,
prepared before the work begins.

#### Minimum Intensity Minimum Luminous Intensity

The lowest acceptable luminous intensity value a fixture must produce at specified angles to remain compliant,
below which the fixture is considered failed or due for replacement.

#### MIRL Medium Intensity Runway Lights

Medium Intensity Runway Lights (MIRL) provide medium-intensity runway-edge guidance for the operating
conditions and runway application for which the system is approved.

#### Modbus

Modbus is an industrial communication protocol used for exchanging data and control information between
supervisory systems, controllers, instruments and other field devices using defined request-and-response data
structures.

#### Mounting Stake

A ground anchor used to fix a portable or semi-permanent light fixture, such as a temporary runway or taxiway
light, in position.

#### Movement Area

The part of an aerodrome used for aircraft takeoff, landing and taxiing, comprising the manoeuvring area and
aprons.

#### Movement Area Map

Digital or graphical representation of runways, taxiways, aprons, holding positions and other controlled
movement-area features.

#### Multilateration

Surveillance technique that estimates a transponder-equipped target position from differences in signal
arrival times at multiple receiving stations.

#### Multimeter Digital Multimeter

A portable electrical measuring instrument capable of measuring selected quantities such as voltage, current
and resistance.

### N

#### NCR Nonconformance Report

The abbreviation commonly used on site and in documentation for a Nonconformance Report. See also:
Nonconformance Report.

#### NCR Closure

The formal process of verifying that the corrective action described in a Nonconformance Report has been
completed and is effective, allowing the NCR to be closed.

#### Network Switch

A data-communications switch used within an ALCMS network to connect CCRs, field devices and control
workstations over an Ethernet-based control and monitoring network.

#### Nonconformance Report

A formal document raised when work, material or a test result fails to meet a specified requirement, recording
the deviation and the action taken. See also: NCR.

#### NOTAM Notice to Airmen / Notice to Air Missions as applicable

A notice distributed by telecommunication containing information on the establishment, condition or change of
an aeronautical facility, service, procedure or hazard, timely knowledge of which is essential to personnel
concerned with flight operations (ICAO Annex 15).

### O

#### Observation Angle

The angle, measured from a fixture's optical axis, at which a photometric measurement or visual assessment is
taken.

#### Obstacle

Any fixed or mobile object, or part of one, located in an area intended for aircraft movement or projecting
above a defined surface intended to protect aircraft in flight.

#### Obstacle Limitation Surface

A defined imaginary surface around a runway, establishing the maximum permitted height of objects to protect
the safety of aircraft operations.

#### Obstruction Light

A light installed on an obstacle or structure to provide the required visual warning of the obstacle to
aircraft.

#### Operational Readiness

The state in which an aerodrome facility, including its AGL system, is fully functional and available for use
in operations.

#### Optical Axis

The central reference line of a fixture's optical system, around which the beam pattern is symmetric and from
which aiming angles are measured.

#### Optical Contamination

Dirt, dust, moisture or residue on a lens or reflector that scatters or absorbs light, reducing a fixture's
effective output.

#### Optical Lens

The transparent component of a fixture that shapes, directs or filters the light emitted from the source.

#### Outlier Measurement Outlier

A measured value that falls significantly outside the expected range of a data set, flagged during data
validation for re-measurement or investigation before being accepted or discarded.

### P

#### PAPI Precision Approach Path Indicator

Precision Approach Path Indicator (PAPI) system providing visual approach-slope guidance through the colour
transition of its optical light units.

#### PAPI Aiming

Mechanical and optical adjustment of a PAPI unit to establish its specified vertical beam angle relative to
the reference datum.

#### PAPI Alignment

Verification and adjustment of PAPI unit orientation, elevation, spacing and reference alignment against the
approved siting design.

#### PAPI Approach Angle

The vertical glide-path angle, commonly 3.0 degrees, that a Precision Approach Path Indicator is set to
indicate, matched to the runway's obstacle clearance surfaces and approach procedure design.

#### PAPI Cable Circuit

The electrical circuit, typically series-connected, linking a PAPI installation's individual light units to
their power supply and control equipment.

#### PAPI Control Unit

The equipment that supplies power to and controls the operation of a PAPI installation's light units, and that
can be coordinated with runway lighting intensity settings.

#### PAPI Frangible Support

The frangible mounting structure supporting a PAPI light unit, designed to break away under aircraft impact
load to reduce hazard to the aircraft.

#### PAPI Glide Path

The visual approach slope defined by a PAPI's transition sector, in which a pilot on the correct path sees a
set balance of red and white units (typically two of each), with a shift toward all-white indicating high and
all-red indicating low.

#### PAPI Indication

The visual signal presented to a pilot by a PAPI installation, formed by the combination of red and white
lights across its light units, indicating whether the aircraft is above, on, or below the glide path.

#### PAPI Light Unit

One of the individual light boxes in a PAPI (typically four) or APAPI (typically two) installation, each
containing a light source and optical system that produces the red/white split used for glide-path indication.
See also: PAPI Unit.

#### PAPI Operation in LVP

Operation of PAPI within the approved approach configuration during low visibility, including status, aiming
and serviceability controls.

#### PAPI Optical System

The lens and light-source arrangement within a PAPI light unit that produces its precisely defined red-to-
white color transition at the designed approach angle.

#### PAPI Photometric Check

A measurement of a PAPI light unit's beam intensity and, critically, the elevation angle at which its
red/white color transition occurs, verifying it matches the promulgated approach angle.

#### PAPI Power Supply

The electrical supply, typically fed from a dedicated series or constant-voltage circuit, that powers a PAPI
installation's light units and control equipment.

#### PAPI Transition Sector

The narrow vertical angular band, centered on the designed approach angle, within which a PAPI light unit's
indication changes from white to red.

#### PAPI Unit PAPI Light Unit

One optical light unit within a PAPI assembly that produces the required white/red indication according to its
vertical aiming setting. See also: PAPI Light Unit.

#### PAPI Unit Alignment

The precise leveling and angular setting of a PAPI light unit, in elevation to set the correct transition
angle and in azimuth to align with the extended runway centerline.

#### PAPI Unit Elevation

The vertical angle setting of an individual PAPI light unit, staggered slightly between the units so their
combined indication produces the correct glide-path signal.

#### PAPI Unit Spacing

The lateral interval between adjacent PAPI light units in the wing bar. ICAO Annex 14 sets it at about 9 m
(tolerance 1 m), with the units equally spaced.

#### Parallel Taxiway

A taxiway arranged substantially parallel to a runway to provide a route for aircraft movement between runway
access points and other parts of the movement area.

#### Peak Intensity Peak Luminous Intensity

The single highest luminous intensity value recorded during a photometric scan, marking the point of maximum
concentrated output within the beam.

#### Permit to Work

A formal document authorising specific work to proceed, confirming that hazards have been identified and
controls put in place.

#### Phase Sequence Phase Sequence Test

The order in which the phases of a three-phase electrical supply reach their respective phase positions,
relevant to correct equipment rotation and connection.

#### Photometer

Instrument that measures a photometric quantity using a calibrated detector and associated signal-processing
system.

#### Photometric Acceptance Band

Defined range within which a measured photometric result is considered acceptable.

#### Photometric Acquisition Rate

Frequency at which the photometric system records measurement samples.

#### Photometric Alignment Reference

Physical or survey reference used to establish the instrument/fixture orientation and measurement geometry.

#### Photometric Angular Resolution

Smallest angular increment between photometric measurement directions in a scan or distribution.

#### Photometric Calibration Factor

Factor used to convert an instrument response into the applicable photometric quantity based on calibration.

#### Photometric Control Chart

Graphical statistical tool used to monitor a measurement or process over time against control limits.

#### Photometric Dark Current

Detector output measured without the intended optical signal and used to correct the instrument baseline.

#### Photometric Data Completeness

Degree to which all required measurement points, metadata and records have been captured without gaps.

#### Photometric Data Integrity

Assurance that photometric data remain accurate, complete, traceable and unaltered through acquisition,
processing and reporting.

#### Photometric Detector Height

Vertical position of the photometric detector relative to the defined measurement datum.

#### Photometric Distribution

The pattern of luminous intensity a fixture produces across a range of angles, typically presented as an
isocandela diagram or table of values.

#### Photometric Drift

Gradual change in instrument response or calibration factor with time, temperature, aging or use.

#### Photometric Environmental Log

A record of field conditions during photometric measurement, such as ambient temperature, weather, background
light level, pavement or lens contamination, and instrument alignment, used to contextualize results.

#### Photometric Export File

Electronic file containing raw or processed photometric results transferred from the measurement system for
analysis or reporting.

#### Photometric Field Record

Field document capturing the installed fixture/sign identity, measurement conditions, observations and
photometric results.

#### Photometric Gain Check

Verification that detector/system response remains within the specified sensitivity or gain condition.

#### Photometric Grid Photometric Measurement Grid

The array of measurement points, spaced at defined angular or linear intervals, used to map a fixture's
photometric distribution during testing.

#### Photometric Instrument Setup

Defined physical and software configuration of the photometric instrument before data acquisition.

#### Photometric Linearity

Degree to which instrument response remains proportional to the applied photometric signal over the specified
range.

#### Photometric Maintenance

Upkeep activities such as cleaning, lamp or LED replacement and alignment correction, performed specifically
to keep a fixture's measured light output within its required photometric limits.

#### Photometric Measurement Distance

Defined distance between the photometric detector and the light source or measurement plane.

#### Photometric Measurement Log

Record linking each photometric measurement to date, asset, instrument, operator, conditions and result.

#### Photometric Pass/Fail Rule

Decision rule defining how measurement results, including uncertainty where applicable, are compared with
acceptance limits.

#### Photometric Processed Data

Measurement data after defined corrections, calculations, filtering, interpolation or conversion have been
applied.

#### Photometric Quality Control

Planned checks used to detect drift, abnormal measurements or process variation before results are released.

#### Photometric Raw Data

Original unprocessed detector readings and associated measurement information captured during a photometric
test.

#### Photometric Reference Lamp

Calibrated lamp used as a photometric reference for checking or calibrating measurement equipment.

#### Photometric Reference Standard

Calibrated reference used to compare or establish measurement performance with traceability to a recognized
standard.

#### Photometric Scan Rate

Rate at which the photometric system moves through or samples measurement directions during acquisition.

#### Photometric Stability

Ability of the photometric measurement system to maintain consistent response over a defined period under
controlled conditions.

#### Photometric Test

A measurement of a fixture's luminous intensity, beam shape and/or colour, performed to verify its output
meets the applicable specification.

#### Photometric Test Report

A document recording the results of photometric measurements taken on a fixture or system, compared against
the applicable acceptance criteria.

#### Photometric Tolerance

Permitted deviation of a measured or controlled quantity from its specified target or limit.

#### Photometric Uncertainty Budget

Structured evaluation listing the significant uncertainty contributions to a photometric measurement and their
combination.

#### Photometric Zero Offset

Instrument reading offset from the true zero condition before the intended photometric signal is applied.

#### Photometry

Measurement of quantities referring to optical radiation as evaluated according to a defined spectral
luminous-efficiency function.

#### PLC Programmable Logic Controller

Programmable Logic Controller used to execute control logic, process inputs/outputs and interface with field
equipment in an automated control system.

#### Plug and Receptacle

The mating connector pair, typically L-823 style, used to join a fixture's pigtail cable to the circuit cable
in a below-ground connection.

#### Power Analyzer

An instrument used to measure electrical parameters such as voltage, current, power, power factor, energy and
waveform characteristics.

#### Power Factor

The ratio of real power to apparent power for an AC electrical load, representing the phase/displacement and
waveform relationship relevant to system loading.

#### Power Loss

The difference between the power a CCR or circuit draws and the useful power delivered to the lamps, arising
from transformer, conductor and regulator losses, and used in circuit efficiency and energy calculations.

#### Power Quality

Characteristics of the electrical supply, including voltage, frequency, waveform distortion and transients,
that affect AGL equipment operation.

#### Power Supply Derating

Power supply derating is the reduction of the maximum allowable output or load capability of a power supply
under specified temperature, installation, duty-cycle or other operating conditions so that thermal,
electrical and reliability limits are not exceeded.

#### PPE Personal Protective Equipment

Equipment worn by personnel, such as high-visibility clothing, insulated gloves or safety footwear, to reduce
exposure to identified hazards.

#### Pre-Commissioning Test

A test performed before operational commissioning to verify installation integrity, basic
electrical/functional condition and readiness for final commissioning.

#### Preventive Maintenance

Maintenance carried out at planned intervals, regardless of current condition, to reduce the likelihood of
failure.

#### Primary Cable Primary Series Circuit Cable

The cable carrying constant current from the CCR to the primary winding of each series-circuit isolating
transformer.

#### Primary Connector

An FAA L-823 (or equivalent) watertight connector kit joining series-circuit primary cable to an isolation
transformer's primary winding, rated up to about 5 kV with a low maximum contact voltage drop.

#### Prism

A precision-moulded glass or acrylic optical component that refracts light to shape a fixture's beam, commonly
used in inset fixtures.

#### Prism Contamination

Dirt, moisture or corrosion affecting the internal prism of an inset or elevated fixture, which distorts or
reduces the light exiting the fixture.

#### Product Datasheet

A manufacturer-issued document describing a product's technical specifications, ratings and performance
characteristics.

#### Proficiency Test

External comparison in which a laboratory or measurement provider demonstrates performance against an assigned
or reference value.

#### Protective Device

Any device, such as a fuse, circuit breaker, RCD or surge arrestor, installed to automatically detect and
interrupt a fault condition on an AGL circuit.

#### Pushback Area

The apron area behind a parked aircraft used for pushback operations, kept clear of obstructions.

### Q

#### Quality Assurance

The planned activities carried out to provide confidence that quality requirements will be met, focused on
process rather than inspecting finished output.

#### Quality Control

The activities used to verify that a specific product or piece of work meets its requirements, typically
through inspection and testing of the output itself.

#### Quality Management System

The documented framework of policies, procedures and records an organisation uses to plan, control and improve
the quality of its work.

### R

#### Random Error

Component of measurement error that varies unpredictably between repeated measurements.

#### Rapid Exit Taxiway

A taxiway designed and located to allow an aircraft landing on the runway to leave the runway at a higher
speed than would normally be possible at a conventional taxiway exit.

#### Ratio Test Transformer Ratio Test

A test used to verify the transformation ratio of a transformer by comparing the measured primary-to-secondary
relationship with the specified ratio.

#### RCL Runway Centerline Lights

Runway Centreline Lights (RCL) provide longitudinal visual guidance along the runway centreline for the
applicable runway operation.

#### Reactance (X)

The imaginary component of electrical impedance, denoted X, arising from inductance or capacitance in series
lighting circuits and affecting current flow alongside resistance.

#### Redundancy for CAT III

Provision of alternate equipment, circuits, power paths or control functions intended to maintain required
lighting capability after a single failure where the approved design requires it.

#### Reference Axis

The fixed direction, established during design or commissioning, against which a fixture's actual aiming angle
is measured and compared.

#### Reference Lamp

A lamp or light source with known, certified output characteristics, used to calibrate photometric test
equipment or verify test setup accuracy.

#### Reference Point Aerodrome Reference Point

The designated geographical coordinates identifying an aerodrome's location, published for navigation
purposes.

#### Reflector

A component, typically a shaped mirrored surface, that redirects light from a source into the desired beam
pattern.

#### REIL Runway End Identifier Lights

Runway End Identifier Lights (REIL) provide rapid identification of the runway threshold by means of
synchronized high-intensity flashing lights positioned near the runway threshold. See also: Runway End
Identification Lights.

#### REL Runway Entrance Lights

Abbreviation for Runway Entrance Lights, the red in-pavement lights of the FAA Runway Status Lights (RWSL)
system. See <a href="#term-runway-entrance-lights">Runway Entrance Lights</a>.

#### REL Activation Logic

Software/control rules that determine when Runway Entrance Lights illuminate or extinguish from surveillance-
derived runway-status information.

#### Relay

An electrically operated switching device used to control or isolate circuits through a defined coil/control
and contact arrangement.

#### Reliability Run

Controlled operating period used to demonstrate stable AGL performance under representative conditions before
final acceptance.

#### Remote Monitoring

Acquisition and display of equipment or system status at a location remote from the field equipment.

#### Remote Terminal Unit

A Remote Terminal Unit (RTU) is a field control and data-acquisition device that interfaces field inputs and
outputs with a supervisory or control system and communicates operational data and commands over an approved
communication network.

#### Repeatability Measurement Repeatability

Repeatability is the closeness of agreement between repeated measurement results obtained under the same
measurement conditions over a short period using the same method, instrument and operator where applicable.

#### Repeatability Study

Study of measurement agreement when the same method, instrument, operator and conditions are used over
repeated measurements.

#### Reproducibility Measurement Reproducibility

The degree to which repeated measurements of the same quantity, taken under changed conditions such as a
different operator, instrument or time, agree with one another.

#### Reproducibility Study

Study of measurement agreement under changed conditions such as operators, instruments, locations or
laboratories.

#### Residual Current

The current imbalance between line and neutral conductors, monitored by a residual current device to detect
earth leakage and disconnect the circuit if it exceeds a safe threshold.

#### Retest

Repeat test performed after correction, repair or clarification to demonstrate that the affected requirement
is now satisfied.

#### Revision Control

The tracking of successive versions of a drawing or document, identified by revision letters or numbers, so
changes can be traced and the current version identified.

#### RFI Request for Information

A formal query raised during design or construction to clarify a drawing, specification or requirement, along
with the recorded response.

#### Risk Assessment

A structured process of identifying hazards, evaluating the likelihood and severity of harm, and determining
controls needed to reduce risk to an acceptable level.

#### Risk Register

A document listing identified project or operational risks, their likelihood, impact and the controls or
mitigations assigned to each.

#### Root Cause Analysis

A structured investigation method used to identify the underlying cause of a nonconformance or failure, rather
than stopping at its immediate symptom.

#### Route Conformance Monitoring

Function that compares actual surface movement against the assigned or expected route and detects deviations.

#### Routine Inspection

A scheduled, recurring inspection carried out at a fixed interval to confirm equipment remains in serviceable
condition.

#### Routine Test

A test performed as standard practice on every unit or at every scheduled interval, as opposed to a special
test carried out for a specific investigation.

#### Routing Guidance

Function that determines and communicates an approved taxi route between movement-area points.

#### Runway Centerline

The centre line of a runway, typically marked and, on precision runways, lit to guide an aircraft along the
runway during landing, takeoff and roll-out.

#### Runway Centerline Light Alignment

The correct beam orientation of a runway centerline light fixture, aimed parallel to the runway centerline so
it presents its designed intensity to an approaching or landing aircraft; verified during commissioning and
periodic inspection.

#### Runway Centerline Light Color Transition

The change in runway centerline light color from white, to alternating red and white over the final 900 m of
runway, to solid red over the final 300 m, providing the pilot a visual cue to remaining runway length.

#### Runway Centerline Light Spacing

The longitudinal interval between runway centreline lights: approximately 15 m on runways intended for
operations in the lowest visibilities, and up to about 30 m otherwise, per ICAO Annex 14 and equivalent
national criteria.

#### Runway Centerline Lighting in LVP

Use of runway centreline lights to provide longitudinal runway guidance during low-visibility operations.

#### Runway Closure

The temporary or permanent withdrawal of a runway from operational use, requiring notification and, where
lighting is affected, appropriate switching or marking.

#### Runway Designation Sign

Sign displaying the runway designation associated with a runway holding or other aerodrome visual-aid
location.

#### Runway Designator

A runway designator is the alphanumeric identifier assigned to a runway based primarily on its magnetic
azimuth, expressed to the nearest 10 degrees, with additional identifiers used for parallel runways.

#### Runway Edge

The lateral boundary of the runway surface, typically marked and lit with runway edge lights.

#### Runway Edge Light Fixture Alignment

The correct aiming and leveling of a runway edge light fixture, ensuring its beam pattern is oriented as
specified relative to the runway centerline and pavement surface.

#### Runway Edge Light Photometric Check

A field or bench measurement of a runway edge light fixture's luminous intensity, verifying it meets the
minimum candela output required by its photometric classification.

#### Runway Edge Light Spacing

The longitudinal interval between runway edge light fixtures, typically not exceeding 60 m, positioned in
parallel rows along the full length of the runway.

#### Runway End

The physical extremity of the usable runway pavement. It may coincide with the threshold or be displaced from
it, and it is marked at night by runway end lights (red, showing toward the runway).

#### Runway End Identification Lights

A pair of synchronized flashing white lights installed laterally at the runway threshold to give pilots rapid,
positive identification of the runway end, particularly where the runway lacks other approach aids. See also:
REIL.

#### Runway End Light Alignment

The correct positioning and aiming of the red runway end lights so they face along the runway and are visible
to an aircraft on its landing roll or take-off run, as designed.

#### Runway Entrance Lights

Flush-mounted, in-pavement, unidirectional red lights (REL) arranged at runway/taxiway intersections to
indicate that entering or crossing the runway is unsafe. In the FAA Runway Status Lights (RWSL) system, the
REL subsystem uses surveillance inputs and activation logic to illuminate the lights at equipped
intersections.

#### Runway Exit Sign

A sign near a runway exit identifying the taxiway designation of the exit ahead, helping a landing aircraft
anticipate and take the correct turn-off.

#### Runway Guard Light

Yellow lights that flash alternately at a taxiway/runway intersection to increase the conspicuity of the
runway holding position: either a pair on each side of the taxiway (Configuration A) or a row of in-pavement
lights across the taxiway (Configuration B). See also: Taxiway Holding Position Light.

#### Runway Guard Light in LVP

Use of runway guard lights to increase conspicuity of a runway holding position during reduced visibility.

#### Runway Holding Position

Runway Holding Position is a designated position on a taxiway or other movement route where an aircraft or
vehicle is required to hold before entering or crossing a runway or another protected area.

#### Runway Incursion

Runway Incursion is an occurrence involving the incorrect presence of an aircraft, vehicle or person on the
protected area of a surface designated for the landing and takeoff of aircraft.

#### Runway Incursion Hotspot

A location on the aerodrome identified, from historical data or layout analysis, as having a higher-than-
average risk of runway incursion.

#### Runway Light Base Can

The below-grade housing into which a runway light fixture and its frangible coupling are mounted, providing a
sealed, structurally anchored point for the cable and isolation transformer.

#### Runway Light Base Elevation

The vertical positioning of a runway light's base can and fixture relative to the pavement surface, set so the
fixture presents its correct beam height without creating a foreign object hazard.

#### Runway Light Beam Orientation

The direction and angle at which a runway light fixture's optical beam is aimed, set during installation to
meet the photometric coverage required for approaching or taxiing aircraft.

#### Runway Light Circuit Segmentation

The division of a runway lighting circuit into separately switchable or controllable sections, for example by
runway third or light type, to allow selective control, maintenance isolation, or partial-runway operation.

#### Runway Light Connector Lead

The factory pigtail cable on a runway light fixture that terminates in an L-823-style plug, used to connect
the fixture to its isolation transformer's secondary lead.

#### Runway Light Frangible Mount

A coupling supporting a runway light fixture that is designed to break away at a predetermined low load if
struck by an aircraft, reducing hazard to the aircraft while the fixture separates cleanly from its base.

#### Runway Light Intensity Step

The brightness level, selected from the CCR's available steps, at which a runway lighting circuit is currently
operating.

#### Runway Light Lens

The optical component of a runway light fixture that shapes and directs the light source's output into the
required beam pattern and color.

#### Runway Light Maintenance Interval

The scheduled period between inspections, cleaning or photometric checks of runway light fixtures, set by the
aerodrome's maintenance program to sustain required output and reliability.

#### Runway Light Optical Axis

The centerline of a runway light fixture's beam, around which its intensity distribution is measured and to
which its aiming is referenced.

#### Runway Light Photometric Degradation

The gradual reduction in a runway light fixture's luminous output over time, due to lamp or LED aging, lens
fouling, or optical component wear.

#### Runway Light Prism

A refractive optical element, used in some fixture designs, particularly older incandescent fixtures, that
redirects and shapes the light source's output into the required beam.

#### Runway Light Secondary Lead

The cable from an isolation transformer's secondary winding to the runway light fixture, carrying the supply
for that fixture's lamp or LED driver, isolated from the primary series circuit.

#### Runway Light Series Circuit Loading

The cumulative electrical load, from the number and type of fixtures and their isolation transformers
connected to a single constant-current series circuit, kept within the CCR's rated capacity.

#### Runway Light Service Life

The expected operational lifespan of a runway light fixture or its lamp/LED source before replacement is
required, typically stated by the manufacturer under specified operating conditions.

#### Runway Shoulder

A prepared surface adjoining the runway edge, provided to support occasional excursions by aircraft and to
resist erosion.

#### Runway Status Lights

Fully automated runway-safety lighting system that uses surveillance-derived traffic information and control
logic to activate red in-pavement Runway Entrance Lights and Takeoff Hold Lights when runway entry, crossing
or takeoff is unsafe.

#### Runway Strip

A defined area including the runway and any stopway, provided to reduce risk of damage to aircraft running off
the runway and to protect aircraft flying over it during takeoff or landing.

#### Runway Threshold

The beginning of the portion of runway usable for landing, typically marked with threshold markings and
lighting.

#### Runway Threshold Identification

The set of lighting and marking used to positively identify the beginning of the usable runway to a pilot,
principally the green threshold lights and threshold pavement markings.

#### Runway Threshold Light Alignment

The correct aiming of the green threshold lights across the runway end, ensuring their beam is oriented to be
visible to an aircraft on final approach.

#### Runway Threshold Wing Bar

A row of additional green lights on each side of the runway at the threshold, extending outward at right
angles to the runway edge lights (ICAO: at least five lights over at least 10 m), to make the threshold more
conspicuous, particularly on precision approach runways.

#### Runway Touchdown Zone Light

One of the white lights, normally in barrettes of at least three lights, installed in symmetrical pairs on
either side of the runway centreline in the touchdown zone of a precision approach runway to give distance and
alignment guidance.

#### Runway Turn Pad

A defined area on a runway, adjacent to the end, provided to allow an aircraft to make a 180-degree turn.

#### Runway Visual Range

Runway Visual Range (RVR) is the meteorological/operational measure of the horizontal distance over which a
pilot on the runway centreline can see runway markings or lights used for approach and runway operations.

#### RVR Operating Condition

Defined runway visual range condition used to determine which low-visibility operating procedures and lighting
configurations apply.

#### RVR Sensor Interface

Data/control interface through which an RVR measurement system supplies visibility information to an airport
operational or control system.

#### RWSL Runway Status Lights

Runway Status Lights (RWSL) is a fully automated runway-safety lighting system that uses surveillance-derived
traffic information and control logic to activate red in-pavement Runway Entrance Lights and Takeoff Hold
Lights when runway entry, crossing or takeoff is unsafe.

#### RWSL Controller

Control processor that receives surveillance information, executes RWSL logic and commands REL/THL field
lighting.

#### RWSL Event Log

A time-stamped record of Runway Status Light system activity, including REL/THL light commands, target
detections, mode changes, alarms and faults, used for operational review and troubleshooting.

### S

#### Safety Cone

A portable cone used to mark hazards, work areas or restricted zones on the airside.

#### Salt Spray Test

An accelerated corrosion test in which a component is exposed to a salt fog environment to assess its
resistance to corrosion, relevant for coastal or humid-climate installations.

#### Sampling Plan

A defined method for selecting a subset of items from a batch for inspection or testing, used when testing
every item is impractical.

#### SAT Site Acceptance Test

The abbreviation for Site Acceptance Test, commonly used in contract documents and test procedures. See also:
Site Acceptance Test.

#### SCADA Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition

Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition system used to supervise, monitor, alarm and record distributed
equipment and process information.

#### SCADA Alarm

An alert generated within the supervisory control and data acquisition layer of an ALCMS when a monitored AGL
parameter, such as current, voltage or fault status, falls outside its defined limit.

#### Schematic Diagram

A simplified drawing showing the electrical connections and logic of a circuit or system without representing
physical layout.

#### Secondary AGL Cable

Secondary AGL Cable is the cable connecting the secondary winding of an isolating transformer to the
associated AGL light fixture or load. See also: Secondary Cable.

#### Secondary Cable Secondary Fixture Cable

The short length of cable connecting an isolating transformer's secondary winding to the fixture itself. See
also: Secondary AGL Cable.

#### Secondary Connector

An FAA L-823 (or equivalent) quick-disconnect plug-and-socket joining an isolation transformer's secondary
lead to a fixture's plug lead, rated for submersible outdoor service with a low maximum contact voltage drop.

#### Selective Coordination

Protection arrangement in which the protective device nearest a fault operates before upstream devices, where
the design requires selectivity.

#### Selector Switch

A manually operated switch used to select among defined control modes, sources, intensity steps or operating
states.

#### Series Circuit

An AGL series circuit is a closed-loop lighting power circuit in which individual light loads are connected in
series and supplied from a constant-current regulator.

#### Series Circuit Continuity

The unbroken electrical path through every lamp and isolation transformer wired in series on an AGL circuit;
the CCR relies on this continuity to maintain its regulated current, and a break registers as an open-circuit
fault.

#### Series Circuit Current

The single current value common to every fixture connected in a series AGL circuit, set by the CCR and
unaffected by the number of fixtures.

#### Series Circuit Isolation

Electrical separation within the AGL series-circuit architecture that limits direct electrical connection
between circuit sections or equipment as required by the design.

#### Series Circuit Power Factor

The ratio of real to apparent power drawn by a series airfield lighting circuit, governed mainly by the
reactive (magnetizing) current of the isolation transformers and the CCR's own regulating transformer.

#### Series Circuit Resistance

The total electrical resistance of a series AGL circuit, comprising cable, connector and transformer
resistance, measured to detect degradation or faults.

#### Shallow Base

A base can with reduced burial depth, used where ground conditions or ducting depth limit installation depth.

#### Shop Drawing

A detailed fabrication or installation drawing prepared by a contractor or supplier, submitted for approval
before manufacture or construction.

#### Short-Circuit Level

Available short-circuit current or fault level at a defined point in the electrical system.

#### Sign Access Panel

Removable panel providing access to specified internal electrical or optical components.

#### Sign Base

Structural support/base connecting the sign assembly to its foundation or mounting system.

#### Sign Brightness

Controlled visual output level of an illuminated sign, normally adjusted to maintain adequate conspicuity for
operating conditions.

#### Sign Cable Entry

Sealed point where the sign power/control cable enters the housing or base.

#### Sign Chromaticity

Quantitative specification of the sign's emitted or reflected color using an applicable chromaticity system.

#### Sign Circuit Isolation

Electrical separation of the sign from its supply/circuit for safe maintenance or fault isolation.

#### Sign Cleaning

Removal of dirt, dust, deposits or other contamination from sign optical surfaces to restore intended
visibility and photometric performance.

#### Sign Connector

Electrical connector used to connect the sign to its supply or internal wiring while maintaining the required
electrical and environmental performance.

#### Sign Contrast

Difference in luminance or visual appearance between the sign legend and its background that supports
legibility.

#### Sign Door

Access door or removable panel providing maintenance access to internal sign components.

#### Sign Drainage

Provision for removing accumulated water from the sign housing or base assembly.

#### Sign External Illumination

Illumination applied to the sign from an external light source rather than an internal optical system.

#### Sign Face

Front visual surface of an airfield sign carrying the legend, color and optical elements visible to the
intended observer.

#### Sign Foundation

Civil/structural foundation transferring sign loads to the ground while maintaining required position and
stability.

#### Sign Framing

Structural members that support the sign panel and maintain dimensional rigidity.

#### Sign Frangible Support

Support designed to meet the applicable frangibility requirement for an aerodrome visual-aid sign
installation.

#### Sign Functional Test

Test confirming correct sign legend illumination, brightness control, electrical operation and relevant
monitoring functions.

#### Sign Housing

Enclosure that protects the sign optical, electrical and structural components from environmental exposure.

#### Sign Internal Illumination

Illumination produced within the sign housing to light the legend or sign face.

#### Sign LED Module

LED light source/module used to provide the required internal illumination of an illuminated sign.

#### Sign Legend

Letters, numbers, symbols or combinations displayed on the sign face to convey the required aerodrome
information.

#### Sign Legend Height

Specified character height of the sign legend, selected to provide required readability from the intended
viewing distance.

#### Sign Legend Stroke

Specified width of the strokes forming letters, numerals or symbols in the sign legend.

#### Sign LGP

Light-guide plate used in an edge-lit sign to distribute LED light across the sign face.

#### Sign Maintenance

Planned and corrective activities used to preserve sign structure, optics, illumination, electrical
connections and legibility.

#### Sign Module Replacement

Controlled replacement of a failed or degraded illuminated sign module while maintaining the approved optical
and electrical configuration.

#### Sign Panel

Structural/visual panel forming the main body of an airfield sign and supporting the legend and optical
system.

#### Sign Sealing

Sealing arrangement that limits water and contaminant ingress into the sign housing and electrical
compartments.

#### Sign Transformer

Isolation transformer or other specified power component used to supply an illuminated airfield sign circuit.

#### Sign Uniformity

Degree to which the required illuminated sign area maintains consistent luminance without unacceptable
bright/dark regions.

#### Signal Light

An aerodrome visual aid capable of transmitting defined light signals to aircraft when the applicable
operational system requires them.

#### Single Line Diagram

A simplified drawing representing a three-phase electrical system using a single line, showing major
equipment, protective devices and circuit connections.

#### Site Acceptance Test

A controlled test performed after site installation to verify the installed equipment/system against the
approved site acceptance criteria. See also: SAT.

#### SMGCS Surface Movement Guidance and Control System

Surface Movement Guidance and Control System (SMGCS) is the set of procedures, facilities, equipment and
operational arrangements used to support the safe movement of aircraft and vehicles on the aerodrome surface,
particularly under reduced-visibility or complex operating conditions.

#### SMGCS Route Surface Movement Guidance Route

A defined route, part of a Surface Movement Guidance and Control System, established for aircraft or vehicle
movement during low-visibility conditions.

#### SMR Surface Movement Radar

Surface radar used to detect and track aircraft and vehicles on or near the movement area.

#### Solid Angle

A three-dimensional angular measure, expressed in steradians, describing the extent of a beam or field of view
from a point source, used in luminous flux and intensity calculations.

#### Special Test

A test carried out outside the routine schedule, typically to investigate a specific fault, verify a repair,
or satisfy a particular contractual requirement.

#### Spectral Power Distribution

Distribution of optical power of a light source as a function of wavelength.

#### Stand Lead-In Line

A marking, sometimes accompanied by lighting, guiding an aircraft into its parking stand.

#### Stand Lead-Out Line

A marking guiding an aircraft out of its parking stand toward the taxiway system.

#### Stop Bar Clearance

The air traffic control authorization required before an aircraft or vehicle may cross an illuminated stop
bar; the stop bar lighting itself is a visual indication and does not substitute for the controller's
instruction.

#### Stop Bar Control

The switching function, typically via CCR or ALCMS, that illuminates or extinguishes a stop bar to indicate
whether an aircraft or vehicle is cleared to cross a runway-holding position.

#### Stop Bar Interlocking

A control logic that prevents a stop bar and the taxiway centreline lights beyond it from being illuminated at
the same time, so a crossing is never shown as both stopped and cleared.

#### Stop Bar Light

A red, controlled lighting element installed at a holding position to indicate that movement beyond the stop
bar is not permitted when the stop bar is illuminated.

#### Stop Bar Operation in LVP

Controlled use of stop bars during low visibility to provide positive visual control of movement across
protected taxiway/runway holding positions.

#### Stop Bar Status in A-SMGCS

Status information indicating whether a stop bar is illuminated, extinguished, unavailable or otherwise
reported by the lighting-control interface.

#### Submittal Technical Submittal

A document, drawing or sample provided by a contractor to the engineer or client for review and approval
before proceeding with the related work.

#### Surface Movement

The movement of aircraft and vehicles on the ground area of an aerodrome, monitored and controlled to maintain
safety.

#### Surface Movement Control

Control function that authorizes, sequences or restricts aircraft and vehicle movement on the aerodrome
surface.

#### Surface Movement Guidance

Information, visual aids, systems or procedures that guide aircraft and vehicles along approved movement-area
routes.

#### Surface Movement Sensor

Sensor system providing aircraft/vehicle position or movement information for surface surveillance.

#### Surge Arrester

A device that limits transient overvoltage and diverts surge current to a suitable discharge path to protect
connected electrical equipment.

#### Surge Protection

Devices installed to limit transient overvoltages, such as those from lightning or switching, from damaging
AGL equipment.

#### Surge Protective Device SPD

A Surge Protective Device (SPD) is a protective device that limits transient overvoltage and diverts or clamps
surge current away from connected electrical equipment to reduce damage caused by lightning-induced or
switching transients. Also commonly called a surge protection device.

#### Surveillance Function

A-SMGCS function that determines the position and movement of aircraft and vehicles using the adopted
surveillance sources.

#### Systematic Error

Component of measurement error that remains constant or changes predictably under repeated conditions.

### T

#### Takeoff Hold Lights

In-pavement, unidirectional red lights arranged in longitudinal rows near the runway centreline that indicate
to a departing aircraft that takeoff is unsafe because conflicting traffic occupies or is about to occupy the
runway.

#### Taxi Route Display

Display of the approved or assigned taxi route for use by an operator or controller.

#### Taxiway Centerline

The centre line of a taxiway, along which taxiway centreline lights or markings are positioned to guide
aircraft.

#### Taxiway Centerline Guidance

The visual path formed by taxiway centreline lights that a pilot follows to keep the aircraft on the taxiway
centreline during taxi.

#### Taxiway Centerline Guidance in A-SMGCS

Integration of taxiway centreline lighting or related guidance with the surface-movement guidance function.

#### Taxiway Centerline Light

An in-pavement or otherwise approved taxiway lighting element used to provide longitudinal centreline guidance
along a taxi route.

#### Taxiway Centerline Light Alignment

The correct physical positioning and levelling of a centreline fixture so its beam is oriented along the
taxiway centreline as designed.

#### Taxiway Centerline Light Color

The specified colour of taxiway centreline lights: green, except along a runway exit taxiway, where ICAO calls
for alternating green and yellow from the runway centreline out to the edge of the ILS/MLS critical/sensitive
area (or the inner transitional surface, whichever is farther), then green.

#### Taxiway Centerline Light Spacing

The maximum distance permitted between successive taxiway centreline fixtures, set by the applicable standard
to maintain continuous visual guidance.

#### Taxiway Centerline Lighting in LVP

Use of taxiway centreline lights to provide continuous or controlled routing guidance when surface visibility
limits ordinary visual navigation.

#### Taxiway Clearance Bar

A row of yellow lights installed across a taxiway at an intersection to indicate the holding position for
aircraft awaiting clearance.

#### Taxiway Closure

The temporary or permanent withdrawal of a taxiway from operational use.

#### Taxiway Curve Lighting

Reduced-spacing taxiway centreline or edge lighting installed through a curve to give pilots earlier and
clearer indication of the turn.

#### Taxiway Designation Sign

A yellow-on-black location sign displaying a taxiway's alphanumeric designator, mounted at intersections to
confirm which taxiway an aircraft is currently on.

#### Taxiway Designator

The alphanumeric identifier assigned to a taxiway, used in markings, signage and radio communication.

#### Taxiway Edge

The lateral boundary of a taxiway's usable surface, marked and often delineated with taxiway edge lights.

#### Taxiway Edge Delineation

The marking of the physical edges of a taxiway using edge lights or reflective markers so pilots and vehicle
operators can identify the usable pavement width.

#### Taxiway Edge Light

A light fixture used to define the lateral limits of a taxiway and provide visual guidance for aircraft ground
movement.

#### Taxiway Edge Light Alignment

The correct physical positioning of taxiway edge fixtures relative to the pavement edge, per the design
layout.

#### Taxiway Edge Light Color

The specified colour, typically blue, that a taxiway edge fixture must emit.

#### Taxiway Edge Light Spacing

The maximum distance permitted between successive taxiway edge fixtures.

#### Taxiway Guidance in LVP

Integrated visual and procedural guidance used to keep aircraft/vehicles on approved taxi routes during low
visibility.

#### Taxiway Holding Position

A designated position intended to protect a runway, obstacle limitation surface, or ILS critical or sensitive
area, at which taxiing aircraft and vehicles must stop unless authorised.

#### Taxiway Holding Position Light

A yellow light installed at a runway holding position to show pilots and vehicle drivers where they must stop.
The usual form is the runway guard light. See also: Runway Guard Light.

#### Taxiway Intersection

The point where two or more taxiways, or a taxiway and runway, meet.

#### Taxiway Intersection Lighting

Additional or modified lighting installed at a taxiway intersection to clearly indicate the junction and guide
the correct turn.

#### Taxiway Lead-Off Lighting

Lighting that guides an aircraft from the runway onto a connecting taxiway after landing.

#### Taxiway Lead-On Lighting

Lighting that guides an aircraft from a taxiway onto the runway before takeoff.

#### Taxiway Light Base

The below-ground housing, deep or shallow base, into which a taxiway fixture is mounted and through which its
cable is connected.

#### Taxiway Light Fixture Elevation

The height a taxiway light fixture protrudes above the pavement surface, controlled to remain within
tolerances that avoid aircraft or vehicle strike risk.

#### Taxiway Light Prism Condition

The physical state, clean, cracked or discoloured, of the internal prism of a taxiway inset fixture, assessed
during inspection.

#### Taxiway Light Transformer

The isolation transformer connected to an individual taxiway fixture in a series circuit. It passes the
regulated series current to the fixture's secondary circuit while keeping the fixture electrically isolated,
so a failed lamp does not open the whole series loop.

#### Taxiway Lighting Circuit

A series or parallel electrical circuit dedicated to powering a defined group of taxiway lighting fixtures.

#### Taxiway Lighting Commissioning

The testing and verification process performed before a newly installed or modified taxiway lighting circuit
is brought into operational service.

#### Taxiway Lighting Failure

The loss of function of one or more taxiway lighting fixtures or a circuit, requiring reporting and corrective
action.

#### Taxiway Lighting Inspection

A scheduled visual or functional check of taxiway lighting fixtures and circuits to confirm serviceability.

#### Taxiway Lighting Intensity

The luminous intensity setting, or brightness step, applied to a taxiway lighting circuit, adjustable via the
CCR to suit visibility conditions.

#### Taxiway Lighting Maintenance

Routine and corrective work performed to keep taxiway lighting fixtures and circuits within their required
performance limits.

#### Taxiway Routing Status

Current state of a taxi route, including active, blocked, unavailable or otherwise constrained segments.

#### Taxiway Shoulder

A prepared surface adjoining the taxiway edge, provided to resist erosion and support occasional aircraft
excursions.

#### Taxiway Stop Bar

A set of unidirectional red lights installed across a taxiway at a runway-holding position to indicate that
crossing is not authorised.

#### Taxiway Straight Section

A length of taxiway centreline or edge lighting installed on a straight run, where spacing follows the
standard interval rather than the reduced curve spacing.

#### TDZL Touchdown Zone Lights

Touchdown Zone Lights providing visual reference to the runway touchdown zone during landing.

#### Technical Data Sheet

A document specifying the technical parameters, tolerances and test values applicable to a particular
material, component or installation.

#### Technical Query

A question raised by site or design personnel seeking clarification on a technical point, tracked until
formally answered and closed.

#### Temperature Rise Test

A test measuring the temperature increase of a component such as a transformer or CCR under rated load, to
confirm it stays within its thermal design limits.

#### Temperature Test

A controlled measurement or test used to verify equipment temperature or temperature-related performance under
the defined condition.

#### Test Certificate

A signed document recording the results of a specific test, confirming pass/fail status, used as formal
evidence for acceptance or handover.

#### Test Data Sheet

Controlled form for recording measured values, test conditions, instrument identification and acceptance
results.

#### Test Deviation

Documented departure from the approved test method or acceptance requirement, including technical
justification and approval where permitted.

#### Test Exemption

Formally approved exclusion from a specified test requirement when the governing procedure allows such an
exemption.

#### Test Instrument Register

Controlled list of instruments used for testing, including identification, range, calibration status and
ownership.

#### Test Method Statement

Approved document describing how a specific AGL test will be performed, including equipment, sequence, safety
controls and acceptance criteria.

#### Test Procedure

Controlled sequence of steps for performing a defined AGL inspection or measurement consistently.

#### Test Report

A document recording the procedure, results and pass/fail outcome of a test performed on AGL equipment or a
circuit.

#### Test Witness

A person, often the client's representative or the certifying authority, present to observe and confirm a test
was performed correctly and its results are valid.

#### Thermal Derating

The planned reduction in a component's rated output or current-carrying capacity as ambient or operating
temperature rises, applied to avoid overheating.

#### THL Takeoff Hold Lights

Takeoff Hold Lights used within the FAA Runway Status Lights system to provide a red warning to an aircraft
when takeoff is unsafe or should not be initiated.

#### THL System

Takeoff Hold Lights subsystem of RWSL that uses traffic information and control logic to indicate an unsafe
takeoff condition.

#### Threshold Crossing Height

The height of the glide path above the runway threshold. For visual slope indicators such as PAPI it is set so
the aircraft's wheels clear the threshold by an adequate margin (minimum eye height over the threshold).

#### Time Domain Reflectometry

Time Domain Reflectometry (TDR) is a cable diagnostic and fault-location technique that transmits a controlled
electrical pulse or signal into a cable and analyzes reflected energy caused by impedance discontinuities to
estimate the location and nature of a fault.

#### Toolbox Talk

A short, informal briefing given to a work team before starting a task, covering the specific hazards and
controls relevant to that day's work.

#### Torque Test Torque Verification Test

A verification of applied fastener torque using a suitable calibrated torque tool against the specified
installation torque.

#### Touchdown Zone

The portion of a runway, beyond the threshold, where landing aeroplanes are intended first to contact the
runway (ICAO). FAA practice treats the first 3,000 ft (about 900 m) from the threshold as the touchdown zone.
On precision approach runways it is marked by touchdown zone markings and lit by touchdown zone lights.

#### Touchdown Zone Light Spacing

The longitudinal and lateral arrangement of touchdown zone light barrettes: pairs symmetric about the runway
centreline, spaced 30 m or 60 m apart longitudinally, extending up to 900 m from the threshold (less on short
runways), per ICAO Annex 14 and equivalent FAA criteria.

#### Traceability Measurement Traceability

Property of a measurement result that can be related to a stated reference through an unbroken documented
chain of calibrations, each contributing to measurement uncertainty.

#### Transformer Acceptance Criteria

Defined limits and conditions used to determine whether a transformer is acceptable for the intended
application.

#### Transformer Ambient Temperature

Temperature of the surrounding environment used when evaluating transformer thermal performance and rating.

#### Transformer Batch Test

Test applied to a defined production batch according to the applicable quality-control or specification
requirements.

#### Transformer Connector Polarity

Defined relationship of connector contacts/leads that must be maintained for correct circuit connection.

#### Transformer Copper Loss

Winding I²R loss produced by current flowing through transformer winding resistance.

#### Transformer Core

The laminated magnetic material, typically silicon steel, around which a series isolation transformer's
windings are wound, providing the flux path that couples current between primary and secondary.

#### Transformer Core Loss

Power loss in the transformer magnetic core caused primarily by hysteresis and eddy-current effects.

#### Transformer Dielectric Strength

Ability of the transformer insulation system to withstand a specified electrical stress without breakdown.

#### Transformer Encapsulation

Surrounding a component or winding assembly with an insulating material to provide electrical and
environmental protection.

#### Transformer Enclosure

Physical housing or construction protecting the transformer from mechanical and environmental exposure.

#### Transformer Frequency

Rated AC supply frequency for which the transformer is designed to operate within its specified performance.

#### Transformer Impulse Withstand

Ability of the transformer insulation system to withstand specified transient impulse voltage.

#### Transformer Insulation

The dielectric materials and encapsulation, such as cast epoxy or a synthetic rubber compound, that separate a
series isolation transformer's windings from each other, from the core, and from earth, rated for the circuit
voltage and for buried or wet-location service.

#### Transformer Insulation Class

Thermal/electrical insulation classification of the transformer winding system according to the applicable
specification.

#### Transformer Lead Identification

Marking used to distinguish transformer leads and maintain correct circuit connection.

#### Transformer Lead Length

Specified physical length of the transformer connection lead between the transformer body and
termination/connector.

#### Transformer Leakage Reactance

The reactance representing magnetic flux that links only one winding of a transformer rather than both, which
limits fault current and contributes to voltage drop under load.

#### Transformer Load Voltage

Secondary voltage measured while the transformer supplies its specified connected load.

#### Transformer Mechanical Integrity

Condition of the transformer body, leads, seals, terminals and construction against physical damage or
loosening.

#### Transformer Moisture Resistance

Ability of the transformer construction and insulation system to resist performance degradation from moisture
exposure.

#### Transformer No-Load Voltage

Secondary voltage measured with the specified primary applied and no external secondary load connected.

#### Transformer Overload

Operation beyond the transformer's specified current or VA capability.

#### Transformer Potting

Process of filling an electrical assembly with insulating compound to improve environmental protection and
mechanical support.

#### Transformer Power Factor

The ratio of real to apparent power at a series isolation transformer's primary, determined mainly by its
magnetizing (reactive) current.

#### Transformer Primary

The winding of a series isolation transformer that is connected directly into the constant-current series
circuit and carries the CCR's regulated current.

#### Transformer Primary Voltage

The voltage across a series isolation transformer's primary winding while it carries the circuit current.
Because the primary is fed with constant current (for example 6.6 A), this voltage is not a fixed rating; it
depends on the connected load. The transformer is rated by primary current and VA.

#### Transformer Rated Current

Maximum or nominal current for which the transformer is designed under its specified operating conditions.

#### Transformer Rated VA

Apparent-power rating of the transformer based on its specified current and voltage/load conditions.

#### Transformer Rating

A series isolation transformer's specified primary current, secondary VA capacity and voltage class, selected
to match the CCR output and the connected lamp per AC 150/5345-47.

#### Transformer Regulation

Change in secondary voltage between defined no-load and load conditions, expressed according to the applicable
transformer definition.

#### Transformer Replacement

The removal and replacement of a failed or out-of-tolerance isolating transformer in a series circuit.

#### Transformer Routine Test

Production test performed on each transformer or defined production unit to verify specified characteristics.

#### Transformer Secondary

Transformer Secondary is the winding or output side of an isolating transformer that supplies the connected
AGL fixture or secondary circuit while remaining electrically isolated from the primary series-circuit side.

#### Transformer Secondary Load

Electrical load connected to the transformer secondary, normally the AGL fixture or designated load.

#### Transformer Secondary Voltage

Voltage appearing at the transformer secondary under the defined load and operating condition.

#### Transformer Serial Number

Unique identifier assigned to an individual transformer for traceability.

#### Transformer Short-Circuit Withstand

Ability of the transformer to withstand specified short-circuit stresses without unacceptable damage.

#### Transformer Total Loss

The sum of a transformer's no-load (core/iron) loss and load (copper/I²R) loss under its defined operating
condition, representing total power dissipated as heat.

#### Transformer Turns Ratio

Ratio of primary to secondary winding turns, which sets the relationship between primary and secondary current
and voltage. Many series isolation transformers are 1:1 (6.6 A / 6.6 A); others, such as 20 A / 6.6 A types,
step the current down.

#### Transformer Type Test

Design-verification test performed on a representative transformer type to demonstrate compliance with
specified requirements.

#### Transformer Voltage Drop

Difference between a defined transformer/input voltage and the corresponding loaded output voltage.

#### Transformer Winding

A coil of insulated conductor, primary or secondary, wound around a series isolation transformer's core to
transfer power between the constant-current circuit and the lamp by mutual induction while maintaining
electrical isolation.

#### Transformer Winding Resistance

Electrical resistance of a transformer winding, used for loss, temperature and condition assessment.

#### Transient Overvoltage

Short-duration overvoltage caused by switching, lightning or other transient events.

#### Trend Data

Historical measurement or performance data plotted over time to identify gradual changes, such as declining
fixture intensity or rising cable resistance.

#### True Bearing

A direction measured relative to true, geographic north, as distinct from magnetic heading, used in some
navigation and survey contexts.

#### Type A Uncertainty

Measurement uncertainty evaluated by statistical analysis of repeated observations.

#### Type B Uncertainty

Measurement uncertainty evaluated from sources other than repeated statistical observations, such as
calibration certificates, specifications or prior data.

#### Type Test

A test performed once on a representative sample of a product design, to demonstrate the design itself meets a
standard, as distinct from testing every individual unit produced.

### U

#### Uniformity Photometric Uniformity

A measure of how evenly light intensity is distributed across a runway, taxiway or fixture's beam, usually
expressed as a ratio between minimum and maximum or minimum and average values.

#### UV Resistance Ultraviolet Resistance

A material's ability to withstand degradation such as cracking, discoloration or loss of strength from
prolonged ultraviolet exposure, relevant to outdoor AGL cable jackets, lenses and housings.

### V

#### VASI Visual Approach Slope Indicator

Visual Approach Slope Indicator providing visual glide-path information to an approaching aircraft.

#### VASIS Visual Approach Slope Indicator System

Visual Approach Slope Indicator System providing visual glide-path guidance through light indications viewed
from the approach.

#### Vehicle Access Control

The system of permits, escorts and physical controls governing which vehicles may enter the airside movement
area and under what conditions.

#### Vehicle Tracking

Continuous or periodic determination of a vehicle's identity and movement position on the aerodrome surface.

#### Vibration Test

A test in which a component is subjected to controlled vibration to verify it withstands the mechanical
stresses of transport, jet blast or ground operation without failure.

#### Viewing Angle

The angle, relative to a fixture's optical axis, from which an observer sees the light, used to define the
angular range over which a signal must remain visible.

#### Visual Docking Guidance System

A system that provides visual guidance and stopping information to assist an aircraft in reaching its
designated parking position.

#### Visual Guidance

The general term for information conveyed to pilots and vehicle drivers through lights, markings and signs to
support safe ground movement and approach and landing.

#### Visual Inspection

A systematic examination of physical condition, identification, installation, cleanliness, damage, alignment
and other observable characteristics.

#### Voltage Calculation

Voltage calculation is the determination of expected electrical voltage, voltage drop or circuit voltage from
the source voltage, load, conductor characteristics, resistance or impedance and the applicable circuit
configuration.

#### Voltage Disturbance

Temporary or transient deviation of supply voltage from its nominal condition.

#### Voltage Drop

The reduction in voltage along a conductor or circuit caused by its impedance and the current flowing through
it.

#### Voltage Measurement

The recording of actual voltage present at a defined point in an AGL circuit, taken to verify it matches
design or rated values.

#### Voltage Sag

A short-duration reduction in RMS supply voltage. Its effect on AGL equipment depends on the duration,
magnitude, source and equipment characteristics and should be evaluated against the applicable power-quality
requirements.

#### Voltage Swell

A short-duration increase in RMS supply voltage. Its effect on AGL equipment depends on the duration,
magnitude, source and equipment characteristics and should be evaluated against the applicable power-quality
requirements.

### W

#### Warning Light

A light, of a distinct colour or flash pattern, used to indicate a hazard, fault or restricted condition
rather than to provide navigational guidance.

#### Warning Tape

Buried identification tape placed above an underground cable/duct route to warn future excavation personnel.

#### Waterproof Connector

A connector, typically an L-823 style, designed and sealed to prevent water ingress at below-ground or exposed
cable connections.

#### White-on-Red Sign

Airfield sign presentation using a white legend on a red background, associated with mandatory-instruction
sign applications where specified.

#### Wind Direction Indicator

A visual device that indicates wind direction and provides a practical surface reference for pilots during
aerodrome operations.

#### Wiring Diagram

A drawing showing the physical wiring connections between components, including terminal numbers and cable
references, used for installation and fault-finding.

#### Witness Point

A stage in an Inspection Test Plan at which a specified party may observe the work or test but is not required
to, and work may proceed if they choose not to attend.

#### Work Permit

The document, once issued and signed, that authorises named personnel to carry out defined work under
specified conditions and time limits.

#### Working at Height

Any work carried out where a person could fall a distance liable to cause injury, subject to specific controls
such as fall protection or safe access equipment.

### X

#### Xenon Flash Tube

A gas-discharge lamp filled with xenon gas used in strobe-type warning and obstruction lights to produce a
brief, intense flash of light.

### Y

#### Yellow-on-Black Sign

Airfield sign with a yellow legend on a black background, used for location signs such as the taxiway
designation, so the pilot knows which surface the aircraft is on. Direction and destination signs use the
reverse arrangement (black on yellow).

### Z

#### Zero Check Instrument Zero Check

A calibration step in which a test instrument is confirmed to read zero with no input signal present,
performed before measurements to catch offset errors.

## Airfield Lighting Terminology & Glossary Notes

### Airfield lighting terminology

Airfield lighting terminology is the shared vocabulary of the field: the names of lights, circuits, equipment,
tests and standards. Using the same terms in specifications, drawings and fault reports avoids confusion
between designers, contractors and maintenance staff.

### Airfield lighting glossary

This airfield lighting glossary lists terms, abbreviations and short definitions across electrical systems,
fixtures, photometry, testing, maintenance and standards. Use the search box and the category filters above to
find a term, then follow the related pages for the full engineering explanation.

### Runway touchdown zone lights

Runway touchdown zone lights are the rows of white lights in the touchdown zone of a precision approach
runway, helping pilots judge the touchdown point and keep the aircraft aligned in low visibility. Their
arrangement and use follow the applicable standard and the runway category.

### Approach lighting spacing

Approach lighting spacing is the distance between lights or light bars along the approach lighting system. It
is fixed by the system type and the standard, and it affects the pilot's visual cues and the length of cable
needed on each circuit.

### AGL maintenance records

AGL maintenance records are the logs of inspections, tests, faults, repairs and replacements for the lighting
system. Good records show trends, support defect analysis and prove that the maintenance programme was carried
out.

# AGL Engineering Calculators

Practical calculation tools for Airfield Ground Lighting design, electrical systems, equipment selection, and
field engineering — organised by category and technically validated before publishing.
