## Common AGL Compliance Mistakes

#### Using ICAO as the Only Standard

The project may additionally specify DGCA, BIS, IEC, FAA and airport-specific requirements.

#### Assuming FAA Doesn’t Apply in India

FAA requirements can appear in Indian tenders where specifically referenced.

#### Treating All Airports the Same

Airport category, operational requirements and existing systems can differ significantly.

#### Checking Only the Product

A fixture may comply individually but still need CCR, transformer, cable and connector compatibility.

#### Ignoring Installation Requirements

Correct equipment doesn’t guarantee performance if installation or alignment is incorrect.

#### Ignoring Testing Requirements

A product certificate alone may not satisfy project acceptance requirements.

#### Using an Old Certificate

The tender may specify particular labs, test methods or certificate validity.

### AGL Photometry India | Airfield Lighting Photometric Testing

Canonical URL: https://rahulsharmaagl.in/agl-photometry-india.html

**Page summary:** AGL photometry in India for runway, taxiway, approach lighting and PAPI: in-field testing of colour, coverage, chromaticity, aiming and test reports.

# AGL PHOTOMETRY INDIA

Airfield Ground Lighting photometric testing and measurement for runway, taxiway and approach lighting and
PAPI — in-field testing of colour, coverage, configuration, chromaticity and aiming, with detailed AGL test
reports.

A light being ON does not prove it is performing correctly. Photometry verifies the optical performance of
airport visual aids in the field.

## What Is AGL Photometry?

Airfield Ground Lighting (AGL) photometry is the measurement and evaluation of the optical performance of
aerodrome lighting on runways, taxiways and approaches, and of visual approach guidance systems such as PAPI.

A lighting system may be electrically operational and still fail to provide the required optical performance.
A lamp can illuminate, an LED fitting can turn on and a CCR can supply the correct current, yet the actual
beam intensity, aiming, colour, coverage or configuration may be outside the applicable requirements. That is
why AGL photometric testing matters for commissioning, periodic inspection, maintenance, troubleshooting and
performance verification.

In India, AAI tender documents show that in-field photometric testing is actively used for AGL facilities.
Recent AAI specifications call for testing of runway, approach, threshold, PAPI and other AGL fittings, with
measurements covering colour, coverage, configuration and chromaticity. [1] ICAO's aerodrome visual-aids
documentation also addresses the characteristics and performance of approach, runway and taxiway lighting. [2]

The purpose is not simply to confirm that a fitting is ON . It is to determine whether the fitting produces
the correct optical output in the intended direction, and whether the installed system performs consistently
across the airfield.

Airport lighting is a safety-critical visual system; pilots depend on runway, taxiway, approach and PAPI cues,
especially at night and in reduced visibility. This is particularly important for LED AGL : long service life
does not prevent optical performance being affected by contamination, damaged optics, incorrect aiming,
mechanical movement, ageing, lens deterioration, internal component failure or installation errors.

## AGL Photometry and the 4Cs: Colour, Coverage, Configuration, Chromaticity

AAI specifications for AGL in-field photometric testing have used the framework of the 4Cs. [1] These are not
a simple lamp-function test.

#### Colour

The visible colour must be correct for the fitting's function. Incorrect colour can come from incorrect
optical components, damaged lenses, LED degradation, contamination, incorrect installation, wrong replacement
components or electrical/electronic failures.

#### Coverage

Whether emitted light gives the intended angular and spatial distribution. Poor coverage can result from
incorrect aiming, fixture displacement, damaged optics, incorrect mounting, pavement settlement, mechanical
movement or internal optical deterioration.

#### Configuration

Whether the installation is arranged correctly within the overall visual aid system — for example incorrect
fixture spacing, a missing fitting, incorrect orientation, wrong fixture type, incorrect light sequence or a
displaced or misinstalled unit.

#### Chromaticity

An objective way of evaluating colour characteristics rather than relying only on visual judgement. The
measurement method and limits should come from the governing specification, not an arbitrary generic value.

## AGL Photometry Services in India

An India-focused photometry programme may cover the complete aerodrome lighting system, depending on the
airport and project specification.

AGL system | Typical photometric evaluation

Runway edge lights | Intensity, aiming, colour, configuration and coverage

Runway threshold lights | Intensity, optical direction, colour and alignment

Runway end lights | Intensity, colour and aiming

Runway centreline lights | Intensity, colour, configuration and circuit performance

Touchdown zone lights | Intensity, alignment and optical output

Approach lights | Intensity, configuration, colour and aiming

Taxiway edge lights | Intensity, colour, alignment and coverage

Taxiway centreline lights | Intensity, colour and alignment

Stop bars | Intensity, colour and directional performance

Runway guard lights | Optical output and operational condition

PAPI | Intensity, colour, beam transition and aiming

Elevated AGL fittings | Intensity, aiming, colour and physical alignment

Inset AGL fittings | Intensity, optical performance and installation condition

The exact test matrix should always be based on the applicable ICAO provisions, Indian regulatory
requirements, airport-specific specifications, equipment documentation and approved project criteria.

## AGL Photometry Equipment: Vehicle-Mounted and Hand-Held Testing

AAI specifications have called for both vehicle-mounted mobile testing equipment and hand-held devices for in-
field AGL photometry at Indian airports. [3]

AAI specifications for hand-portable equipment also describe measurement of photometric diagrams, mean
intensity, aiming angles and other parameters for AGL and PAPI systems. [4]

### Photometric Testing Equipment Airport

Photometric testing equipment for an airport is chosen by the testing scope: vehicle-mounted systems for large
runway and taxiway surveys, and hand-held equipment for PAPI, individual fittings and spot checks. Either type
should provide calibrated photometric sensors, angular and aiming-angle measurement, colour / chromaticity
measurement, data acquisition with reporting software, and calibration documentation. Confirm suitability for
the systems to be tested, including PAPI, before mobilising.

#### Vehicle-mounted testing

Testing every fitting with a manually positioned instrument is slow on large airports. A vehicle-mounted
system measures systematically while travelling along a runway or taxiway. Useful for runway edge and
centreline surveys, approach lighting, threshold and end lights, taxiway surveys, acceptance testing, periodic
maintenance testing and trend monitoring. AAI has tendered in-field AGL photometric testing using vehicle-
mounted devices. [3]

#### Hand-held testing

Useful where a vehicle system is impractical or an individual fitting needs detailed investigation: PAPI
measurements, defective-fitting verification, isolated runway or taxiway lights, post-maintenance
verification, field alignment checks, troubleshooting, spot measurements and laboratory or workshop
evaluation. Portable systems complement, rather than necessarily replace, a vehicle-based survey.

## Runway, Taxiway, Approach Lighting and PAPI Photometry

### Runway lighting

Edge lights: verify output and orientation (low or inconsistent intensity, incorrect aiming, tilted elevated
fixtures, damaged inset fittings, dirty optics, wrong colour, dead or weak units). Threshold and end lights:
re-check after maintenance, resurfacing, fixture replacement, civil works or rehabilitation. Centreline
lights: identify weak fittings, defective LEDs, wrong colour, optical degradation, damaged inset units and
circuit inconsistencies. Touchdown zone: reveals deterioration not obvious in a night visual inspection.

### Taxiway lighting

Edge and centreline lights, stop bars, runway guard lights, holding-position and special guidance lighting.
Attention to colour, beam direction, fixture orientation, damaged or sunken fittings, contamination, intensity
variation and incorrect replacement fixtures. A taxiway fitting may be electrically functional but optically
misaligned; photometry provides objective evidence.

### Approach Lighting Photometric Testing

Arrays of visual aids give alignment and distance cues. Assessment covers intensity, colour, configuration,
aiming, spacing-related installation condition, elevated support alignment, inset light performance and
defective or missing fittings. AAI specifications explicitly include approach lights among fittings subject to
in-field photometric testing. [1]

### PAPI

Depends on both intensity and the correct relationship between white and red sectors. Testing covers luminous
intensity, colour, beam transition, unit aiming, horizontal alignment, elevation angle, optical consistency
between units and system configuration. A unit can illuminate normally while incorrectly aimed, so visual
inspection alone is not enough. Use suitable equipment and the applicable aerodrome specification and
authority-approved criteria.

## AGL Photometric Testing Procedure

A professional field photometry programme follows a controlled sequence.

#### 1. Document review

AGL layout drawings, runway and taxiway configuration, fitting inventory, fixture type, circuit
identification, project specifications, previous photometric reports, maintenance records, PAPI documentation
and applicable criteria — establishing what is supposed to be measured.

#### 2. Airfield inspection

Look for damaged, missing or displaced fittings, dirty lenses, broken housings, incorrect orientation, damaged
cables, standing water, damaged mountings and signs of pavement movement, so installation problems are not
mistaken for measurement anomalies.

#### 3. Calibration verification

Current calibration or verification documentation appropriate to the project. A photometric report is only
meaningful when the measurement system itself is controlled.

#### 4. Equipment setup

Configure per the manufacturer's procedure and applicable methodology. Vehicle: vehicle → measurement frame →
sensor → data acquisition → analysis software. Portable: operator → portable photometer → fixture →
measurement → report.

#### 5. Circuit preparation

Energize the circuit at the appropriate operating condition. Where several brightness stages exist, the test
plan must say which are required — on CCR-fed series circuits, measured performance can depend on the
operating current level.

#### 6. Measurement

Record the applicable parameters: intensity, angular distribution, aiming angle, colour, chromaticity,
photometric curve, fixture position, unit identification and pass/fail status.

#### 7. Data analysis

Process raw data against the applicable requirements and classify results as Pass , Marginal / investigation
required or Fail , linked to project criteria rather than a generic industry number.

#### 8. Defect identification

Locate the problem, for example: Runway 09 → edge light no. 47 → low intensity; Taxiway A → centreline unit 18
→ incorrect aiming; PAPI 27 → unit 3 → abnormal beam transition. More useful than an overall pass percentage.

#### 9. Corrective maintenance

Cleaning, aiming correction, fixture, optical-component or LED-module replacement, cable/connector repair,
transformer replacement, mechanical realignment, housing repair, replacement of damaged fittings and
correction of installation configuration.

#### 10. Retesting

Retest corrected fittings where required to confirm the action restored the required optical performance.

## AGL Photometry Report and Deliverables

A professional report should provide enough information for traceability and engineering decisions.

#### Project information

- Airport, runway/taxiway, location

- Date and relevant environmental information

- Test personnel and equipment

#### Equipment information

- Photometer make/model and serial number

- Calibration information

- Software version

- Vehicle or measurement-frame details

#### AGL asset information

- Fitting identification and type

- Runway/taxiway location, circuit, unit number

- Fixture technology and position

#### Measurement results

- Measured photometric values

- Colour / chromaticity

- Aiming and coverage / distribution

- Pass/fail classification and defect comments

#### Corrective action

- Defect identified

- Recommended and performed action

- Retest result

#### Final summary

- Total fittings tested and passed

- Fittings requiring correction and retested

- Unresolved observations

AAI tender specifications have also called for formal submission of photometric test reports and corrective
measures following field testing. [7]

## Defect Categories and Common Problems Found

A useful programme does not simply report "low light" — it investigates the cause, together with electrical
testing, physical inspection and maintenance records.

Observation | Possible cause

Low intensity | LED degradation, lamp failure, optical deterioration, incorrect current

Wrong colour | Optical/component issue, damaged filter, incorrect fitting

Incorrect aiming | Mechanical movement, poor installation, maintenance error

Narrow coverage | Incorrect orientation or optical problem

Uneven intensity | Fixture degradation or circuit variation

PAPI imbalance | Incorrect aiming, optical problem or unit condition

Inconsistent readings | Measurement setup or equipment issue

Missing fitting | Installation / configuration deficiency

Inset fitting weak | Lens damage, contamination, internal failure

Elevated fitting misaligned | Frangible support or mounting movement

#### Dirty optical surfaces

Dust, oil, rubber deposits and contamination reduce performance.

#### Incorrect aiming

Sufficient intensity directed outside the intended angular region.

#### Damaged lenses

Cracks, scratches, discolouration or contamination.

#### Fixture movement

Impact, loose mounting or other airfield works.

#### Inset fitting problems

Lens damage, water ingress, pavement contamination, deterioration.

#### Incorrect replacements

A visually similar but optically different assembly.

#### PAPI misalignment

Very small aiming errors affect the approach-path indication.

#### Ageing / electronic degradation

An LED system can operate while optical performance falls.

## Photometry vs Electrical Testing

The two are different disciplines that should be considered together; a complete AGL maintenance programme
uses both.

Electrical testing | Photometric testing

Checks circuit continuity | Checks optical performance

Measures insulation condition | Measures light output

Checks transformer condition | Checks beam characteristics

Evaluates CCR / circuit operation | Evaluates intensity and distribution

Identifies electrical faults | Identifies optical / aiming faults

Electrical measurement | Optical measurement

A fitting with low measured intensity could have a healthy transformer, correct circuit continuity and
acceptable insulation resistance — and still have a defective optical assembly.

Visual inspection finds lights that are off, obviously damaged, wrong-coloured, missing or visibly misaligned,
but cannot reliably quantify optical performance. Photometry gives measurement → evidence → comparison →
defect identification → corrective action → retest , which is far more valuable for engineering acceptance and
asset management.

## Photometry in Commissioning, Existing Airports, Compliance, LED and CAT II/III

#### Commissioning

Sequence: installation → electrical testing → functional testing → energization → photometric testing →
corrections → retest → final acceptance → documentation. At new runways, extensions, taxiway construction,
rehabilitation, LED conversion, approach modifications, PAPI relocation, CAT II/III improvements and major
upgrades, it identifies installation defects before handover.

#### Existing airports

Existing systems may mix legacy lamps, LED fittings, mixed fixture types, older transformers, new and old
circuits and replacement fixtures from different manufacturers. Photometry establishes actual field condition.
AAI has awarded and tendered dedicated photometric work at operational airports, including testing of all AGL
at Hyderabad Airport, Begumpet, and other airport-specific photometric surveys. [5]

#### DGCA compliance

An AAI 2026 tender for Ranchi Airport sought in-field photometric testing of AGL using vehicle-mounted and
hand-held equipment as part of compliance with DGCA observations. [3] Photometry is not only a design or
commissioning activity — it can be an operational compliance and corrective-maintenance activity. Acceptance
criteria must come from the applicable DGCA requirements, ICAO provisions, airport specifications and approved
documents.

#### LED airport lighting

LED removes many lamp-related problems but not optical ageing, lens contamination, damaged optics, thermal
degradation, electronic faults, incorrect replacement assemblies, alignment errors or incorrect installation.
Periodic photometry works as a performance-monitoring tool: initial test → annual test → trend comparison →
reduced performance → corrective maintenance. Historical data becomes part of asset management.

#### Preventive maintenance

Photometric data supports condition-based maintenance: spot gradual intensity reduction, repeated failures at
one location, systematic aiming problems, colour deterioration, recurring circuit abnormalities and fixture
types with higher failure rates — directing resources to assets that need attention.

#### CAT II / III operations

A performance programme for low-visibility operations may include regular visual inspections, functional
checks, photometric testing, fixture condition monitoring, PAPI verification, circuit and CCR checks,
corrective maintenance and documented retesting. Frequency and acceptance requirements come from the
operational approval, regulations, airport procedures and approved maintenance programme.

## AGL Photometry for Airport Projects

Photometric testing can support several stages of an airport project.

#### Design verification

Verify installed equipment performs as intended in the field.

#### Construction QA/QC

Identify installation-related optical errors.

#### Pre-commissioning

Before final acceptance and operational handover.

#### Commissioning

Part of complete AGL system performance evaluation.

#### Periodic inspection

Monitor ongoing lighting performance.

#### Maintenance

Identify defective or deteriorated fittings.

#### Rehabilitation

Before and after major AGL replacement programmes.

#### Regulatory / inspection response

Objective data for corrective-action programmes.

## The Indian AGL Photometry Market and How to Select a Provider

AGL photometry is an established airport engineering service in India. Current AAI procurement records include
dedicated AGL photometric field testing at Madurai Airport in 2026, and other AAI documents specify vehicle-
mounted and hand-held systems. [6] AAI technical documents also specify field testing of approach, runway
edge, runway end, threshold and PAPI fittings, with reporting and corrective measures. [7]

This creates demand for providers who combine photometric equipment + AGL engineering knowledge + field
testing + data analysis + corrective guidance + retesting .

#### Suitable equipment

Measurement equipment appropriate for the AGL systems being tested.

#### Calibration and traceability

#### Runway and taxiway experience

Methodology changes with fitting type and installation.

Aiming, beam transition and optical performance expertise.

#### Vehicle-mounted testing

#### Hand-held testing

For detailed investigation and individual fixture verification.

Technically useful, traceable to individual fittings and suitable for corrective action.

Difference between ICAO provisions, DGCA requirements, AAI specifications, project specifications,

## ICAO and Indian Requirements for AGL Photometry

Photometry should always be performed against the correct governing requirements .

ICAO Annex 14 Volume I is a core international reference for aerodrome design and operations; the ICAO Store
lists the 9th Edition (July 2022) with Amendment 18 dated 4 August 2025 and subsequent corrigenda issued in
2026. [8] ICAO's Aerodrome Design Manual Part 4, Visual Aids , addresses visual-aid characteristics including
approach, runway and taxiway lighting; the store lists it as the 5th Edition, 2021. [2]

For Indian projects, the applicable DGCA requirements, AAI technical specifications, airport procedures and
contract documents must also be considered. AAI field-testing specifications illustrate how ICAO/DGCA
requirements are incorporated into actual Indian airport work packages. [1]

Acceptance criteria vary with the project and operational category, so this page deliberately does not publish
universal numerical pass/fail values. Always take them from the exact applicable standard or project
specification.

Photometric testing is most useful when it goes beyond collecting measurements and produces actionable
engineering information.

Precision AGL Solutions offers India-focused AGL photometry covering field measurement, runway and taxiway
lighting evaluation, PAPI testing, colour and chromaticity assessment, aiming verification, defect
identification, reporting and retesting, subject to the applicable airport project requirements.

Final engineering perspective. AGL photometry is the link between an installed airport lighting system and its
actual optical performance in the field. The electrical system may be healthy and the light may be ON, yet an
optical problem can remain. Modern AGL quality control combines electrical testing + functional testing +
physical inspection + photometry + corrective maintenance + retesting — verifying the performance,
consistency, maintainability and operational readiness of airport visual aids. [6]

### AGL Installation Checklist & Quality Control in India

Canonical URL: https://rahulsharmaagl.in/agl-installation-india.html

**Page summary:** AGL installation services for Indian airports: installation checklist, quality control, primary and secondary circuit work and equipment installation.

# AGL INSTALLATION IN INDIA

AGL installation requires coordination between lighting equipment, electrical infrastructure, civil works and
airfield operational requirements.

Our installation support covers primary and secondary circuit work, lighting equipment installation, and the
quality checks that lead to commissioning.

## AGL Installation Services

AGL installation requires coordination between lighting equipment, electrical infrastructure, civil works and
airfield operational requirements.

#### Primary Circuit

Primary cable routing, primary connector installation, series-circuit connections, isolating transformer
installation.

#### Secondary Circuit

Secondary connector assembly, fixture connection, cable termination, equipment identification.

#### Lighting Equipment

Elevated fixtures, inset fixtures, runway lights, taxiway lights, approach lighting, sign systems.

## What Does AGL Installation Include?

An AGL installation is not limited to fixing lights on the runway or taxiway — it includes the complete
relationship between civil infrastructure, cable network, connectors, transformers, fixtures, CCR, control and
testing.

## AGL Installation Requires Multi-Discipline Coordination

AGL installation interfaces with several airport disciplines, and the installation sequence should be
coordinated with the complete airport project programme.

#### Electrical Works

- CCRs

- Primary cables

- Transformers & connectors

- Control & monitoring systems

#### Civil Works

- Pavement & foundations

- Ducts & manholes

- Cable routes

- Inset fixture cut-outs, equipment bases

#### Lighting Works

- Runway & taxiway fixtures

- Approach lights

- Signs

- Visual guidance equipment

#### Airside Operations

- Work restrictions & access control

- Operational areas & maintenance windows

- Testing & commissioning windows

- Return to service

## AGL Installation Process

A typical installation workflow, though the actual sequence can vary depending on the project.

## Pre-Installation Planning & Site Survey

The installation team should work from the latest approved documents. Any discrepancy between the approved
design and actual site condition should be addressed through the project process before installation.

#### AGL Layout

- Fixture locations

- Transformer locations

- Cable routes

- Sign & equipment locations

#### Civil Conditions

- Pavement condition

- Foundations, ducts, manholes

- Cut-outs & mounting arrangements

#### Electrical Conditions

- Existing cable & connectors

- Existing transformers & CCRs

- Existing control infrastructure

#### Operational Conditions

- Airside access

- Work areas

- Operational restrictions & coordination

## Primary Circuit Installation

The primary circuit is a major part of the AGL electrical infrastructure. Primary cable routing, primary
connector installation, series-circuit connections and isolating transformer installation are part of the
installation scope.

## Primary Cable Routing, Connectors & Transformer Installation

#### Primary Cable Routing

- Approved route & equipment locations

- Duct / trench arrangement

- Cable & circuit identification

- Protection during installation

#### Primary Connector Installation

- Correct connector type & cable

- Correct assembly & connection

- Physical condition & sealing

- Identification

#### Isolating Transformer Installation

- Correct rating & location

- Correct cable & connector arrangement

- Mechanical protection

- Equipment identification

## Secondary Circuit Installation

The secondary circuit connects the isolating transformer to the lighting fixture. Incorrect connector
selection or assembly can affect individual fixture operation.

## Elevated & Inset AGL Fixture Installation

#### Elevated Fixture Installation

- Correct location, mounting & orientation

- Correct elevation & alignment

- Cable connection

- Equipment identification

#### Inset Fixture Installation

## Runway, Taxiway, Approach & Sign Installation

#### Runway AGL Installation

Edge, threshold, runway end, centreline, touchdown zone and approach lighting — layout verification, civil
readiness, fixture and transformer installation, alignment, testing and commissioning.

#### Taxiway AGL Installation

Edge, centreline, stop bars, runway guard lights and holding-position lighting, coordinated with taxiway
geometry, pavement markings, runway interfaces and control systems.

#### Approach Lighting Installation

Requires careful coordination since fixtures extend outside the runway environment — structures, electrical
connections, cable routes, foundations, alignment and control.

#### Airfield Sign Installation

Positioning, foundation/mounting, electrical connection, cable termination, identification and functional
verification, coordinated with pavement layout and movement areas.

## Fixture Positioning, Orientation & Alignment

A fixture installed at the wrong position can affect the intended lighting pattern even if the fixture itself
is technically compliant. Alignment should be checked after installation and again after any work that could
disturb the fixture.

## Cable & Connector Inspection, Equipment Identification

Equipment identification provides traceability between Drawing → Circuit → Equipment → Physical Location.

#### Cable

- Correct cable type

- Physical condition

- Identification, routing & termination

#### Connector

- Correct type & assembly

- Physical condition

- Connection integrity & sealing

#### Equipment Identification

- Circuits & transformers

- Cables, connectors & fixtures

- Signs & equipment locations

## Electrical Testing After Installation

The exact test method, test voltage and acceptance criteria should be established from the applicable project
specification and test procedure.

#### Continuity Testing

Identifies open circuit, incorrect connection, connection failure or circuit discontinuity, following the
applicable project requirements.

#### Insulation Resistance Testing

Assesses electrical insulation condition of primary circuit, cables, equipment and connections; instrument,
voltage, duration and criteria come from the project procedure.

#### Functional Verification

Fixture, circuit, CCR, current-step, control, monitoring, fault indication, sign and stop bar operation,
confirming intended operation.

#### Photometric Verification

Light intensity, beam direction/alignment, colour/chromaticity — helps identify orientation, alignment,
optical damage or location issues.

## AGL Installation Quality Control

A structured quality-control process used throughout installation.

#### Before Installation

- Equipment approved & materials inspected

- Site condition verified

- Civil works ready

#### During Installation

- Correct location & orientation

- Correct transformer, cable & connector

- Connections inspected

- Equipment identified

#### Before Testing

- Installation complete

- Circuit connections & cable condition checked

- Fixture alignment checked

- Documentation updated

#### Before Commissioning

- Electrical & functional tests completed

- Control & monitoring checked

- Photometry completed where required

- Defects closed

## Civil Interfaces, Rehabilitation & LED Retrofit Installation

Civil and AGL teams should coordinate pavement, foundation and underground interfaces before installation
begins. Runway rehabilitation requires extensive removal and reinstatement work, and LED retrofit installation
requires a compatibility review before physical work begins.

## AGL Installation in Operational Areas

Airport work can take place around operational movement areas. The specific procedures are airport- and
project-dependent and should follow the applicable airport operational requirements.

## Installation Defects & Troubleshooting

These issues demonstrate why AGL installation quality is as important as product quality. A system problem
should be investigated through the complete chain, helping identify whether the issue originated during
installation or within an upstream component.

#### Positioning & Orientation

Fixture installed at incorrect location, or facing the wrong direction.

#### Alignment & Connection

Beam direction incorrectly set, or poor electrical connection.

#### Transformer & Cable

Incorrect rating or installation; cable damage, incorrect termination or poor insulation.

#### Connector & Civil Interface

Incorrect assembly or incompatible connector; incorrect fixture mounting or pavement interface.

## Installation Testing Sequence

A practical sequence; the exact steps may be modified according to the project test procedure.

## AGL Installation Standards

BIS documentation identifies IS 12309 Part 1 as the Indian code of practice for installation of aerodrome
lighting fittings, and IS 12309 Part 2 for maintenance. The current applicable edition and exact project
requirements should always be verified before installation.

### AGL Maintenance Contract | Airfield Lighting Maintenance

Canonical URL: https://rahulsharmaagl.in/agl-maintenance-india.html

**Page summary:** AGL maintenance contract and annual maintenance for Indian airports: inspection, testing, fault diagnosis and CAT II/III serviceability.

# AGL MAINTENANCE SERVICES IN INDIA

AGL maintenance is essential for maintaining availability and supporting airport operations across India.

For low-visibility operations, serviceability of critical AGL facilities becomes particularly important, with
specific inspection requirements for LVP and CAT II/III operations.

## Airport AGL Maintenance & Technical Support

AGL maintenance involves much more than replacing a defective light. An AGL system contains interconnected
electrical, lighting and control components, so a fault in one part of the chain can affect a single fixture
or an entire circuit. Maintenance should therefore consider the complete system rather than only the visible
fixture.

AGL chain: CCR → Primary Cable → Primary Connector → Isolating Transformer → Secondary Connector → Light
Fixture.

## What AGL Maintenance Maintains

AGL maintenance is the planned inspection, testing, servicing, repair and replacement of airport lighting
equipment and associated infrastructure. The objective is to maintain:

The exact maintenance programme depends on airport configuration, operational category, installed equipment,
airport procedures, applicable regulations, manufacturer requirements, project specifications and operational
requirements.

## AGL Maintenance Activities

Typical AGL maintenance activities identified in the India AGL source material as part of airport AGL
maintenance and technical support:

## AGL Maintenance Types

A practical maintenance programme can be divided into several categories. The actual strategy should follow
the airport's established procedures.

### Preventive Maintenance

Planned activities performed before a failure occurs.

- Scheduled inspection

- Cleaning

- Connector & transformer inspection

- Cable & CCR checks

- Alignment & photometric checks

### Corrective Maintenance

Work carried out after a defect or failure is identified.

- Failed fixture / lamp / LED replacement

- Transformer & connector replacement

- Cable repair

- CCR & control-system fault correction

### Airport Lighting Breakdown Maintenance

Immediate investigation and restoration following an unexpected failure.

- Fault report & circuit ID

- Fault isolation & testing

- Defective component ID

- Repair / replace & return to service

### Airport Lighting Emergency Maintenance

Urgent work on a failure that affects operations, such as lost lights on an active runway, taxiway or approach
circuit.

- Follows the breakdown workflow

- Coordinated with airport operations and ATC

- Temporary measures until the system is restored

### Condition-Based Maintenance

Planned around indicators of equipment condition.

- Repeated failures

- Reduced lighting performance

- Insulation / connector / transformer deterioration

- Equipment alarms & physical damage

## Visual Inspection

Visual inspection is one of the first steps in AGL maintenance — regular inspection of fixtures, connectors,
transformers and cables.

#### Fixture

- Physical / mechanical damage

- Lens / optical condition

- Contamination & water ingress

- Incorrect orientation

- Loose mounting

#### Transformer

- Physical condition

- Connection condition

- Environmental condition

- Signs of damage

#### Connector

- Physical condition

- Connection & sealing

- Damage

- Contamination

#### Cable

- Visible damage

- Exposed sections

- Joint condition

- Termination condition

## Elevated & Inset Light Maintenance

Lighting fixtures should be checked for damage, optical condition, water ingress, contamination, mechanical
security, orientation, alignment, electrical connection and illumination. Elevated and inset fixtures carry
additional considerations.

#### General Fixture Inspection

- Physical damage & optical window

- Water ingress / dirt

- Mechanical security & alignment

- Electrical connection & illumination

#### Elevated Light Maintenance

- Fixture body & mounting

- Frangible arrangement where applicable

- Orientation & alignment

- Cable connection & optical components

#### Inset Light Maintenance

- Pavement interface & water ingress

- Optical window & mechanical condition

- Cable & transformer connection

- Final position & alignment after reinstallation

## Connector & Isolating Transformer Inspection

Connectors and isolating transformers are critical points in the series-circuit system, and both should form
part of systematic maintenance.

#### Connector Inspection

A defective connector can result in:

- Intermittent operation

- High-resistance connection

- Open circuit

- Fixture failure / circuit problems

#### Isolating Transformer Inspection

Checks may include:

- Physical & connection condition

- Insulation & environmental condition

- Signs of water ingress

- Rating verification & primary/secondary connection

Where a fixture repeatedly fails, the transformer should also be considered during fault investigation.

## Primary Series-Circuit & Cable Testing

#### Series-Circuit Maintenance

The primary AGL series circuit connects the CCR to multiple lighting units.

- Circuit & connector checks

- Cable & transformer testing

- Insulation & continuity testing

- Fault location & performance verification

#### Cable Testing

Potential cable-related problems:

- Open / short circuit

- Insulation deterioration

- Joint / termination failure

- Physical & water-related damage

A systematic approach helps determine whether a lighting failure is local to one fixture or associated with
the wider circuit. Exact test procedures and acceptance criteria should follow the applicable airport
maintenance and testing requirements.

## CCR & Control / Monitoring Maintenance

The Constant Current Regulator is a major part of the AGL electrical system. A CCR problem can affect every
fixture within the connected circuit.

Maintenance should also confirm that the system correctly reports and controls the equipment, not only that
fixtures illuminate:

## AGL Fault Diagnosis

Fault diagnosis should follow a structured process, tracing an individual fixture back through the complete
AGL chain:

This approach helps identify whether the failure is:

## Troubleshooting Example — One Light Not Operating

Tracing the fault through the complete chain avoids replacing a fixture when the actual fault is upstream:

Step | Action

1 | Inspect the fixture

2 | Check the secondary connector

3 | Check the isolating transformer

4 | Check the primary connector

5 | Check the primary cable and circuit

6 | Verify CCR output

7 | Check control / monitoring indications

8 | Identify the defective component

9 | Repair or replace

10 | Perform functional verification

## Multiple & Intermittent Faults

#### Multiple Light Failures

Investigation should begin at the common parts of the system: CCR, primary series circuit, cable, common
connector, control system, power supply.

- Are the failed fixtures on the same circuit or common equipment?

#### Intermittent Faults

More difficult to identify since equipment may operate normally during a basic inspection.

- Loose connection / connector condition

- Cable joint & transformer connection

- Insulation deterioration

- CCR behaviour & control-system communication

## Component Replacement & Compatibility

Maintenance may require replacement of fixtures, lamps, LED components, isolating transformers, connectors,
L-823 plugs/receptacles, cable joint components, sign components and GLF spares — based on compatibility with
the existing system.

Before replacing a component, review compatibility against the existing system. A component should not be
selected only because its basic dimensions appear similar.

## LED vs Conventional Lamp Maintenance

#### LED Fixture Maintenance

- Fixture body & optical system

- LED module & driver / electronics

- Connector, sealing & alignment

- Light output

For an LED replacement project, the existing CCR, transformer, cable, connector and control system should also
be evaluated.

#### Conventional Lamp Maintenance

- Lamp replacement

- Fixture & optical inspection

- Connector & transformer inspection

- Functional testing

Lamp replacement should follow the applicable fixture and manufacturer requirements.

## AGL Maintenance Standards & Support Scope

AGL maintenance requirements in India can involve ICAO, DGCA, AAI / airport maintenance procedures, airport-
specific technical specifications, BIS / Indian Standards, manufacturer instructions and project-specific
maintenance requirements. BIS documentation identifies IS 12309 Part 2 for maintenance of aerodrome lighting
fittings — current applicable requirements should always be verified before carrying out maintenance
activities.

#### Runways

#### Taxiways

#### Electrical

CCR, transformers, cables, connectors

### FAA Airport Lighting Maintenance

FAA maintenance guidance, such as AC 150/5340-26C on maintenance of airport visual aid facilities, may be
referred to where FAA-type equipment is used or the project specification calls for it. At Indian airports the
governing procedures are normally ICAO, DGCA, AAI and BIS based, so confirm which document applies and its
current edition. See ICAO vs FAA .

### Airport Lighting Maintenance Technician

An airport lighting maintenance technician needs a working knowledge of series circuits, CCR operation,
isolating transformers, connectors, test instruments and the airport's maintenance procedures. Safe working
matters, because a series circuit can still carry current when the lights look off. Training builds these
skills; see the AGL Academy .

A failed light may be caused by a component located several steps upstream — a defective connector,
transformer, cable, CCR or control fault, not the fixture itself. AGL maintenance should therefore combine
inspection, electrical testing, fault diagnosis, equipment knowledge and functional verification as a single
system activity.

## AGL Maintenance Contracts in India

### Airfield lighting maintenance company

An airfield lighting maintenance company provides trained staff, test equipment and spares to keep the AGL
system serviceable. It should know the airport's circuits, CCRs and control system and work to the airport's
procedures.

### AGL maintenance contract

An AGL maintenance contract defines the inspections, tests, response times, spares, reporting and
responsibilities for the airfield lighting system. A clear scope and measurable service levels make
performance easy to review.

### Airfield lighting annual maintenance contract

An airfield lighting annual maintenance contract covers planned maintenance and fault attendance over a year.
It normally lists the schedule of inspections, what is included and excluded, and how records are handed to
the airport.

## AGL Equipment & Component Supply in India

The Indian AGL supply chain includes manufacturers, component suppliers, system integrators, distributors and

## How We Can Support Your Project

## Who Makes Up the Indian AGL Supply Chain

Unlike conventional outdoor lighting, AGL equipment must operate as part of an integrated airfield lighting
system: CCR → Primary Cable → Primary Connector → Isolating Transformer → Secondary Connector → Light Fixture.
Equipment selection should consider the individual product and its compatibility with the complete system.

#### AGL Equipment Manufacturers

- Isolating transformers, CCRs

- Airfield & LED fixtures

- Signs, connectors, cable accessories

#### Component Suppliers

- Primary / secondary connector kits

- L-823 plugs & receptacles

- Cable joint kits, lamps, GLF spares

#### System Integrators

- CCR systems & series circuits

- Control & monitoring, ALCMS interfaces

- Installation, testing, commissioning

#### AGL Contractors

- Cable laying, transformer & fixture installation

- Connector termination

- Testing, commissioning, maintenance, retrofit

#### Distributors & Stockists

- Product availability & local inventory

- Replacement parts, emergency requirements

- OEM coordination, project procurement

## AGL Product Categories in India

#### Isolating Transformers

Interface the series primary circuit with individual lighting fixtures.

#### Primary Connector Kits

Connect the primary series cable to the isolating transformer.

#### Secondary Connector Kits

Connect the isolating transformer to the airfield lighting fixture.

#### L-823 Plugs & Receptacles

Airport series-circuit connections for transformers, fixtures & replacements.

Runway, taxiway, approach lights and signs — evaluated as a system.

Lamps, connectors, transformer/fixture components, LED modules, seals.

#### AGL Electrical Components

CCRs, transformers, cables, connectors, control & monitoring interfaces.

### Airport Lighting Equipment List

A typical airport lighting equipment list for AGL supply covers isolating transformers, primary and secondary
connector kits, L-823 plugs and receptacles, airfield lamps, LED airfield lighting, airfield sign boards,
cable accessories, GLF spares, and AGL electrical components such as CCRs, cables and control & monitoring
interfaces. The final list should come from the approved BOQ, drawings and technical specification, and each
item should be checked for compatibility with the complete series circuit. See Airfield Lighting Components .

- Applicable standards, type & routine testing

- Connector configuration & fixture compatibility

- Mechanical connection

- Waterproofing / sealing requirements

## Selecting the Right L-823 Components

L-823 connectors are commonly associated with airport series-circuit connections — transformer, fixture and
secondary connections, replacement assemblies and maintenance requirements.

A connector should not be selected solely because it carries an L-823 designation. The exact required type and
configuration should be established from the project documentation.

## Lamps, LED Retrofit & Airfield Signs

#### Airfield Lamps

Replacement, spare and fixture-specific lamps for existing lamp-based systems. Compatibility with the existing
fixture and electrical system should be confirmed before replacement.

#### LED Airfield Lighting

A system-compatibility exercise, not a like-for-like swap. Evaluate before replacing existing fixtures:

- CCR & series-circuit compatibility

- Transformer, cable & connector arrangement

- Control & monitoring interface

- Fixture photometric performance

#### Airfield Sign Boards

Mandatory instruction, location, direction and runway/taxiway designation signs, illuminated and LED sign
systems. Type, legend, colour, illumination and installation are determined from the applicable airport and
project requirements.

## Keeping the Series Circuit Reliable

#### Cable Accessories

Cable joint kits, termination accessories, primary/secondary connectors and cable protection — particularly
important because the AGL series circuit depends on reliable electrical and environmental connections.

#### GLF Spares

Lamps, connectors, transformer and fixture components, LED modules, drivers, optical components, hardware,
seals and gaskets. The actual spare list should be developed from the installed equipment and airport
maintenance requirements.

### Airport Lighting Power Supply

Airport lighting power supply on an airfield is delivered through the series circuit: CCR, primary cable,
primary connector, isolating transformer, secondary connector and light fixture. The CCR, transformers, cables
and connectors must therefore be selected as one system, with the series-circuit rating, connector arrangement
and control & monitoring interface verified before any item is replaced or added. For the wider electrical
architecture, see AGL Electrical Architecture & Redundancy .

## A Related System, Not Independent Products

A supplier should understand the relationship between these components rather than treating them as
independent electrical products.

## Airfield Lighting Manufacturers & Airport Lighting Manufacturers in India

### Airfield Lighting Manufacturers

Airfield lighting manufacturers design and build fixtures, regulators, transformers and cables to published
standards. Ask each for type-test reports and approvals accepted by your aerodrome operator, not just a
catalogue.

### Airport Lighting Manufacturers

Airport lighting manufacturers differ in range: some cover the full series circuit and control, others only
fixtures or cable. Check which products they make themselves and which they resell.

### Airfield Lighting Manufacturer

An airfield lighting manufacturer should be able to show factory quality control, certified test results and
spare parts support for the full life of the installation.

### Airfield Ground Lighting Manufacturer

An airfield ground lighting manufacturer is judged on compliance with the specified standard, such as ICAO
Annex 14 photometry or FAA fixture specifications, and on how long it supports each product.

### Airport Lighting Manufacturer

When choosing an airport lighting manufacturer, compare certified performance, delivery time, warranty terms
and after-sales support in India, along with price.

### Runway Edge Lights Manufacturer

A runway edge lights manufacturer should provide photometric test reports and certification to the specified
standard, along with maintenance and spare lamp or LED module information.

### Constant Current Regulator Manufacturer

A constant current regulator manufacturer should be able to show compliance with the relevant standard, such
as IEC 61822 or FAA CCR requirements, plus service support and spare parts.

### Airfield Lighting Isolation Transformer Manufacturer

An airfield lighting isolation transformer manufacturer should show type-test results for insulation, open-
circuit behaviour and temperature rise, and give clear selection guidance.

### Airfield Lighting Cable Manufacturer

An airfield lighting cable manufacturer should provide material and test data, such as insulation resistance
and voltage withstand results, and traceability for each batch.

### Airfield Lighting Control System Manufacturer

An airfield lighting control system manufacturer should show standards compliance, redundancy options,
supported CCR interfaces and a clear plan for software support.

### ALCMS Manufacturer

An ALCMS manufacturer should be able to show how its control and monitoring software and hardware interface
with the CCRs in use, what redundancy and alarm functions are provided, and how updates, spares and training
are supported over the life of the system. See the ALCMS page for how the system works.

## AGL Equipment Suppliers, Distributors & Vendor List in India

### AGL Equipment Suppliers

AGL equipment suppliers include manufacturers' own sales channels, authorised distributors and traders.
Confirm authorisation in writing, since it affects warranty and genuine spares.

### AGL Equipment Supplier India

An AGL equipment supplier in India should be clear on import or local manufacture, lead time, customs and
delivery, and who handles warranty claims and site support.

### AGL Equipment Distributor

An AGL equipment distributor holds stock and resells products from one or more manufacturers. Check that it is
authorised for the brand and that spares and documentation are available.

### Airfield Lighting Supplier

An airfield lighting supplier should supply to a clear technical specification and provide datasheets,
certificates and installation guidance, so the material submitted matches what is delivered.

### Airport Lighting Supplier

Airport lighting supplier selection should look at technical competence and track record on comparable
airfields, not only the quoted price.

### Airfield Lighting System Supplier India

An airfield lighting system supplier in India can provide the full series circuit, from regulators and cable
to fixtures and control, or only part of it. Confirm that the parts are compatible as a system.

### Airport Lighting Products India

Airport lighting products available in India include CCRs, isolating transformers, L-823 connectors, cables,
light fixtures, lamps and signs. List each item against the BOQ and its specification.

### Airfield Lighting Vendor List

An airfield lighting vendor list is a project's pre-approved set of manufacturers and suppliers. Build it from
technical approval and past performance, and review it for each tender.

### Best Airfield Lighting System

The best airfield lighting system is the one that meets the runway category and standards, is compatible as a
whole, and can be maintained locally. It is a technical decision, not a brand ranking.

## Runway, Taxiway, Approach, CCR, Transformer, Cable & Connector Suppliers

### Approach Lighting Supplier

An approach lighting supplier must provide frangible structures and fixtures that meet the specified approach
system, along with mounting hardware, cables and installation details.

### Runway Lighting Supplier

A runway lighting supplier should provide edge, threshold, end and centreline fixtures in the correct colours
and beam patterns, with matching bases, transformers and connectors.

### Taxiway Lighting Supplier

A taxiway lighting supplier should provide edge and centreline fixtures with the right colours, and, where
needed, stop bars and guidance signs designed to work with the circuit.

### Runway Edge Lights Supplier

A runway edge lights supplier should confirm the fixture type (elevated or inset), colour, intensity class and
frangibility, and supply matching transformers and connectors.

### Constant Current Regulator Supplier

A constant current regulator supplier should confirm output rating, number of brightness steps, standard
compliance and control interface, and match the CCR size to the circuit load.

### Airfield Lighting Transformer Supplier

An airfield lighting transformer supplier should provide series isolating transformers matched to lamp wattage
and current, with correct insulation rating and connectors.

### Airfield Lighting Isolation Transformer Supplier

An airfield lighting isolation transformer supplier should state the rating, lead type and compliance with
standards such as IEC 61823 or the FAA specification, so it suits the fixtures and series circuit.

### AGL Cable Supplier

An AGL cable supplier should provide single-core series cable with the specified voltage rating, insulation
and sheath, supplied on drums with test certificates.

### Airfield Lighting Cable Supplier

An airfield lighting cable supplier should offer the cable type, rating and certification the project
specifies, plus joint kits and accessories that suit it.

### L-823 Connector Supplier

An L-823 connector supplier should supply plugs and receptacles that match the cable and transformer lead,
with approvals and moulding or assembly instructions, since poor connectors are a common fault source.

### Airfield Lighting Control System Supplier

An airfield lighting control system supplier should provide the ALCMS hardware, software and interfaces, with
FAT and SAT support. See the ALCMS page for how the system works.

### ALCMS Supplier

An ALCMS supplier should provide a design suited to the airport's size and procedures, with documentation,
training and long-term support for software and hardware.

## AGL Spare Parts & Airfield Lighting Retrofit Products

### AGL Spare Parts Supplier

An AGL spare parts supplier should be able to deliver lamps, lenses, gaskets, connectors and transformers
quickly, so repairs are not delayed and the airfield stays within serviceability limits.

### Airfield Lighting Spare Parts India

Airfield lighting spare parts in India should be stocked or available at short notice. Ask about lead time,
minimum order, obsolescence policy and genuine-part guarantees.

### Airfield Lighting Retrofit Products

Airfield lighting retrofit products, such as LED conversion kits or replacement fixtures, must be compatible
with the existing series circuit, transformers and control, so check load, current and photometry first.

## AGL Supplier Technical Checklist

Before placing an order or approving an AGL supplier, verify each group:

#### Product

- Correct equipment type, rating & application

- Correct dimensions

- Correct connector arrangement

#### Compliance

- Project specification reviewed

- Applicable standards identified

- Compliance statement & type-test documents available

- Routine & acceptance testing requirements identified

#### Compatibility

- CCR, transformer & cable compatibility

- Connector compatibility

- Control / monitoring compatibility

- Mechanical compatibility

#### Documentation

- TDS, catalogue, GAD, GTP

- Test certificates

- Installation instructions & O&M documentation

#### Project Support

- Technical clarification & BOQ support

- Submittal & installation support

- Testing & commissioning support

- Spare support

## No Single Supplier Category Fits Every Project

There is no single supplier category that is automatically suitable for every airport project. The right
supplier depends on project scope, equipment requirement, airport specification, operational category,
existing AGL system, applicable standards, required testing, delivery requirements, installation scope and
maintenance requirements .

A supplier should therefore be evaluated against the actual project requirement , not only against product
availability or price. A practical starting point is: BOQ + Technical Specification + Existing System Details
+ Required Equipment — from which the required product, rating, standard, compatibility, testing and
documentation can be established.

## AGL Manufacturing Standards

Standard | Scope

identifying the relevant document, applicability, product configuration and supporting evidence.

### AGL Training Courses in India | Online, Fees & Certification

## What Is Airfield Ground Lighting Training?

Specialised education on airport lighting and its electrical infrastructure: functions, engineering
principles, installation, testing and maintenance. Whether you call it an airfield lighting course, an airport
lighting course or an airfield ground lighting course, the programme may include lessons, drawings,
calculations, case studies, assignments, simulated faults and equipment demonstrations.

### Airfield lighting systems

Runway edge, centreline, threshold and end lights; taxiway lighting; approach and touchdown zone lighting;
runway guard lights, stop bars, PAPI and signs.

### Electrical infrastructure

CCR operation, constant-current series circuits, isolating transformers, cables, connectors, insulation
testing, earthing and counterpoise, surge and lightning protection, and electrical safety.

### Engineering design

Layouts, circuit arrangements, cable selection, voltage-drop calculations, equipment schedules, specifications
and quantity estimation.

### Photometry and testing

Luminous intensity, beam alignment, chromaticity, measurement principles, test equipment, calibration
considerations and reporting.

### Maintenance and fault diagnosis

Systematic inspection, defect identification, circuit fault investigation, alarm interpretation and
maintenance records.

### Standards and documentation

ICAO provisions, FAA advisory circulars, DGCA requirements and airport specifications, with compliance
matrices, test reports and handover files.

## AGL Training Courses Offered by Precision AGL Academy

Programmes organised by level of technical knowledge, as listed on the Academy's main course page.

### Master Diploma in Airfield Ground Lighting Engineering

Covers aviation fundamentals and lighting systems through electrical infrastructure, design, testing,
maintenance and project documentation. Suited to learners who want broad AGL engineering knowledge rather than

compliance matrices and equipment submissions. For engineers, consultants and project professionals.

arrangement.

connector faults, defect reports and return-to-service considerations.

## Online vs Practical and Classroom Training

The right option depends on your objectives and the hands-on experience you need.

### AGL Online Course & Airfield Lighting Course Online India

Best for theory and principles: system fundamentals, components, ICAO/FAA references, design calculations,
photometry methodology, maintenance theory and BOQ documentation. Flexible for working professionals.

### Practical AGL training

Component identification, CCR and transformer demonstrations, cable and connector familiarisation, test
instruments, simulated faults and photometric equipment. Work on energised or operational equipment must
follow authorised procedures and safety controls. Series circuits carry dangerous current and voltage: never
open, disconnect or touch a live circuit; isolate, lock out, earth and test before work.

### Classroom and on-site training

Useful for organisations training engineering, maintenance or project teams. Evaluate trainer, syllabus,
facilities, location, duration, practical activities and assessment.

### Airfield Lighting Study Notes | AGL for Students & Engineers

Canonical URL: https://rahulsharmaagl.in/agl-study-notes.html

**Page summary:** 21 airfield lighting study notes: runway, taxiway and approach lighting, PAPI, CCRs, transformers, L-823, photometry, CAT I-III, LVP, ICAO Annex 14 and FAA ACs.

## INTRODUCTION TO AIRFIELD GROUND LIGHTING (AGL)

Airfield Ground Lighting, commonly called AGL , is the network of lighting and visual guidance systems used on
an aerodrome to help pilots identify, approach, land on, taxi along and operate around the airfield. It
becomes especially important during darkness, restricted visibility and instrument operations.

It is not simply a collection of lights. An AGL installation combines lighting equipment + electrical circuits
+ control systems + installation + testing + maintenance + operational requirements .

### Why is AGL required?

Without appropriate visual guidance, runway and taxiway geometry is harder to identify, particularly at night
or in reduced visibility. AGL helps pilots identify:

- Runway edges

- Runway threshold

- Runway end

- Runway centreline

- Touchdown zone

- Taxiway routes

- Holding positions

- Runway entrances

- Approach alignment

- Vertical approach guidance

### Main AGL areas

### Runway

- Edge, threshold, end lights

- Centreline, touchdown zone

- Runway end identifier lights

- Rapid exit taxiway indicator lights, where provided

### Taxiway

- Edge and centreline lights

- Lead-on and lead-off lights

- Stop bars

- Runway guard lights

### Approach area

- Approach Lighting Systems

- PAPI, APAPI

- Other visual guidance systems

### Airfield signs

- Location and direction

- Mandatory instructions

- Runway and taxiway identification

### Simple AGL concept diagram

```
APPROACH AREA ↓ Approach lighting → PAPI / APAPI ↓ ┌─────────────────────────────┐ │ RUNWAY │ │ Edge lights Centreline │ │ TDZ lighting │ └─────────────────────────────┘ ↓ TAXIWAY (edge / centreline / stop bar) ↓ APRON → AIRCRAFT STAND
```

### AGL as a complete system

A common beginner mistake is studying every light in isolation. Understand the whole chain:

If one part fails, the visible symptom may appear somewhere else. That is why AGL people need both component
knowledge and system knowledge . FAA specifications include dedicated requirements for constant-current
regulators, L-823 connectors, isolating transformers and airport lighting cable, showing how these form
distinct parts of the system.

- AGL = Airfield Ground Lighting

- It provides visual guidance for aerodrome operations

- It includes runway, taxiway, approach and other visual guidance applications

- It is both a lighting system and an electrical infrastructure system

- Understand the complete system, not only the fixture

## RUNWAY LIGHTING SYSTEMS

Runway lighting provides visual guidance during take-off and landing. Study each light by connecting Location
→ Colour → Function → Operational meaning .

### 1. Runway edge lights

Define the lateral limits of the runway. FAA guidance classifies them by intensity: HIRL (High), MIRL
(Medium), LIRL (Low). They are normally white, with yellow replacing white on the last 2,000 ft or half the
runway length, whichever is less, on instrument runways. ICAO Annex 14 uses yellow on the last 600 m or one-
third of the runway length , whichever is less; check the applicable AIP.

### 2. Threshold lights

Identify the beginning of the landing portion of the runway. In FAA configurations they are green when viewed
from the approach side.

### 3. Runway end lights

Identify the end of the usable runway. FAA bidirectional fixtures show red when viewed from the runway and
green when viewed from the approach side. Red = runway end; Green = threshold.

### 4. Runway centreline lights

Provide accurate alignment, especially on precision approach runways and in reduced visibility. FAA AIM
describes 50 ft spacing. The FAA colour sequence seen from the landing threshold is White → Alternating
White/Red → Red :

Distance remaining | Centreline colour

More than 3,000 ft | White

Last 3,000 to 1,000 ft | Alternating white/red

Last 1,000 ft | Red

### 5. Touchdown zone lights (TDZL)

Identify the touchdown zone on applicable precision approach runways. FAA describes rows of transverse light
bars, symmetrically placed about the centreline, steady-burning white.

### 6. REIL

Runway End Identifier Lights : two synchronised flashing lights placed laterally near the threshold for rapid,
positive identification of the approach end of a runway.

### 7. RETIL

Rapid Exit Taxiway Indicator Lights give distance-to-go information to the nearest rapid exit taxiway and
improve situational awareness during landing and rollout. ICAO-based provisions describe fixed, unidirectional
yellow lights in a 3-2-1 pattern . Check the aerodrome AIP for the runways that have RETILs. REIL identifies
the runway end; RETIL indicates distance toward a rapid exit.

### Quick revision table

System | Main function | Typical colour

Runway edge | Defines runway edges | White / caution-zone colour

Threshold | Identifies threshold | Green

Runway end | Identifies runway end | Red (viewed from runway)

Centreline | Alignment / distance-to-go cue | White / red sequence

TDZ | Identifies touchdown zone | White

REIL | Rapid runway-end identification | Flashing

RETIL | Distance to rapid exit | Yellow

- Threshold = Green · Runway End = Red

- REIL = Runway End Identifier Lights · RETIL = Rapid Exit Taxiway Indicator Lights

- TDZL = Touchdown Zone Lights

- FAA centreline sequence = White → Red/White → Red

## TAXIWAY LIGHTING SYSTEMS

Taxiways guide aircraft between runways, aprons, terminals, maintenance areas and other locations. Colours and
configurations communicate location and movement guidance.

Lighting system | Colour | Basic meaning

Taxiway edge | Blue | Defines taxiway edge

Taxiway centreline | Green | Taxiway guidance

Lead-on / lead-off | Green and yellow | Runway-environment transition

Stop bar | Red | Stopping position

Runway guard lights | Flashing yellow | Runway holding position

FAA guidance confirms blue edge, green centreline and alternating green/yellow lead-on and lead-off lighting
in applicable configurations, and describes runway guard lights as flashing yellow.

### 1–2. Edge and centreline

Edge lights outline the taxiway ( Blue ). Centreline lights guide along the route ( Green ).

### 3. Lead-off lights

Guide aircraft exiting a runway onto a taxiway. FAA describes alternating green and yellow, beginning with
green, from the runway centreline toward the holding position/critical-area boundary. Leaving runway → Lead-
Off.

### 4. Lead-on lights

Guide aircraft entering the runway from a taxiway, using the same alternating green/yellow pattern as lead-off
lights, in bidirectional fixtures where provided. In ICAO practice, lead-on lights are green and work with the
stop bar: lit when the stop bar is off. Going toward runway → Lead-On.

### 5–6. Stop bars and runway guard lights

Stop bars are red and mark a stopping position. Runway guard lights are flashing yellow, in elevated or in-
pavement arrangements, and identify a runway holding position. Don't confuse Stop Bar → Red with Runway Guard
→ Flashing Yellow . A lit stop bar must not be crossed. ATC switches it off when it clears the aircraft or
vehicle to proceed; contingency procedures apply only if it cannot be switched off.

### 7. Runway entrance lights (REL)

Part of the FAA Runway Status Lights system: red in-pavement fixtures along the taxiway centreline near a
holding position. When activated they indicate runway traffic or an aircraft on final approach within the
activation area. Runway Guard = flashing yellow; REL = red. They are different systems.

- Blue = Taxiway Edge · Green = Taxiway Centreline

- Red = Stop Bar · Flashing Yellow = Runway Guard

- Green/Yellow = Lead-On / Lead-Off

- Red REL = Runway Entrance Lights in FAA RWSL

## APPROACH LIGHTING SYSTEMS & PRECISION APPROACH AIDS

Approach lighting helps pilots transition from instrument conditions to visual references for landing. It is
installed in the approach area beyond the threshold. FAA describes ALS as providing information on runway
alignment, height perception, roll guidance and horizontal references.

- Runway alignment

- Longitudinal perspective

- Approach path reference

- Threshold identification

- Lateral reference

- Instrument-to-visual transition

### Main FAA approach lighting terms

### ALSF-1

Approach Lighting System with Sequenced Flashing Lights, Category I configuration; high intensity.

### ALSF-2

High-intensity system supporting Category II/III instrument approaches.

### SSALR

Simplified Short Approach Lighting System with Runway Alignment Indicator Lights. Medium intensity, associated
with Category I approaches; also a mode of ALSF-2/SSALR where applicable.

### MALSR

Medium Intensity Approach Lighting System with Runway Alignment Indicator Lights, along the extended
centreline; steady-burning bars plus sequenced flashers.

ICAO / India: Annex 14 describes simple approach lighting (centreline about 420 m with a crossbar at 300 m)
and precision approach lighting CAT I (centreline 900 m, crossbar at 300 m) and CAT II/III (900 m, extra
crossbar at 150 m and red side rows over the inner 270 m). FAA also uses MALS, MALSF, SALS and ODALS. Always
confirm against the applicable AIP.

### PAPI: Precision Approach Path Indicator

Visual approach slope guidance. FAA describes two or four lights in a single row, normally to the left of the
runway. Common four-light interpretation:

Pilot sees | Meaning

4 white | Too high

3 white + 1 red | Slightly high

2 white + 2 red | On slope

1 white + 3 red | Slightly low

4 red | Too low

More white = high. More red = low. 2 white + 2 red = on path.

### VASI: Visual Approach Slope Indicator

Common two-bar interpretation: White/White = above path; Red/White = on path; Red/Red = below path. Three-bar
VASI can give two visual glide paths.

Feature | PAPI | VASI

Full form | Precision Approach Path Indicator | Visual Approach Slope Indicator

Common arrangement | 4 lights | 2 bars

Function | Vertical approach guidance | Vertical approach guidance

Typical on-path | 2 white + 2 red | Red/White

Concept | Colour balance | Colour relationship

- Common 4-light PAPI on path = 2 White + 2 Red

- More White = Above Path · More Red = Below Path

- ALSF-2 = high-intensity, FAA CAT II/III applications

- MALSR = medium intensity with runway alignment indicator lights

## AIRFIELD ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS FOR AGL

The fixture is only one part of an AGL system. Behind every light is an electrical system delivering
controlled power. The series circuit is one of the most important concepts for electrical and airport
engineering students.

```
POWER SUPPLY → CCR → PRIMARY CABLE → PRIMARY CONNECTOR → ISOLATING TRANSFORMER → SECONDARY CONNECTOR → AGL LIGHT
```

### 1. Constant Current Regulator (CCR)

Supplies controlled current to the series circuit, provides intensity levels in applicable systems and
interfaces with airport lighting control. FAA lists AC 150/5345-10H for CCRs and regulator monitors. Why a
CCR? Because series-circuit lighting is designed to operate with controlled constant current. Typical FAA
values (check the specification): 6.6 A maximum; 3-step 4.8 / 5.5 / 6.6 A; 5-step 2.8 / 3.4 / 4.1 / 5.2 / 6.6
A.

### 2. Series circuit

```
CCR out ─► [TX 1] ─► [TX 2] ─► [TX 3] ─► … ─► [TX N] ─┐ ▲ │ │ │ │ │ │ Light 1 Light 2 Light 3 Light N │ │ │ └───── return to CCR: the loop is continuous ─────┘
```

The circuit is one continuous loop: the same current leaves the CCR, passes through every isolating
transformer primary and returns to the CCR.

### 3. Isolating transformer

Provides electrical isolation between the primary series circuit and the fixture, transfers power to the
secondary side, and lets individual fixtures connect to the series circuit. FAA AC 150/5345-47C covers series-
to-series isolation transformers.

### 4–5. Primary cable and connector

The primary cable is part of the high-voltage series circuit; FAA AC 150/5345-7F specifies L-824 underground
cable. Primary connectors join cable lengths and connect the cable to the transformer primary; in FAA systems
they are normally L-823. A poor connection can look like a circuit or fixture fault.

### 6–7. L-823 and secondary connection

L-823 connectors are used for underground power cables, isolation transformer leads and fixture leads (FAA AC
150/5345-26E), covering both primary and secondary connectors. The transformer secondary supplies the fixture
through the secondary connection. L-823 = airport lighting cable connector.

### AGL fault-finding logic

Don't immediately replace the light. Ask, in order:

- Is the CCR operating correctly?

- Is the series circuit energised?

- Is the primary circuit continuous?

- Are the connectors satisfactory?

- Is the isolating transformer healthy?

- Is the secondary connection satisfactory?

- Is the light fixture working?

### One runway light not operating

- Fixture fault

- Secondary connector problem

- Transformer fault

- Primary connector problem

- Local cable issue

Don't assume the lamp or LED is at fault.

### Several lights not operating

- CCR output

- Primary circuit and cable continuity

- Connector condition

- Multiple component failures

The more fixtures affected, the more you should investigate the common part. If the whole circuit is out,
suspect an open primary loop or a CCR trip.

### Revision table

Component | Main function

CCR | Controls series-circuit current

Primary cable | Carries primary series-circuit current

Primary connector | Connects primary circuit components

Isolating transformer | Isolation; transfers power to fixture

Secondary connector | Connects transformer secondary to fixture

Light fixture | Produces visual light output

L-823 | Standard airport lighting connector spec (FAA)

- CCR = Constant Current Regulator; AGL commonly uses series circuits

- Transformer = isolation between primary series circuit and fixture

- L-823 = connector spec · L-824 = underground cable spec (FAA)

- Understand the complete circuit before troubleshooting

## Airport Lighting Careers in India

What the work involves, who employs AGL professionals, and how the pieces of an airfield lighting project fit

#### Airport Lighting Companies India and Airfield Lighting Companies India

The terms airport lighting companies India and airfield lighting companies India both describe the
organisations that work on airfield ground lighting: equipment suppliers, installation and maintenance
contractors, consultancies and airport operators' own engineering teams. Each hires differently, so check
whether a role is field work, testing or documentation before you apply. Precision AGL Solutions is a
consultancy and testing practice, and the roles listed above are the ones we are building for.

#### Airport Lighting Consultant India and Airport Lighting Contractor India

An airport lighting consultant India practice advises on design, specification, testing and compliance. An
airport lighting contractor India employs the installation, cabling and commissioning crews who build the
system on site. Consultancy roles lean towards testing, documentation and compliance, while contractor roles
lean towards field installation and site supervision. Knowing which side you prefer helps you choose the right
role with us.

#### Airport Lighting Specification India

An airport lighting specification India project document sets out what must be supplied, installed, tested and
accepted: fixtures, CCRs, cables, connectors and test requirements. Technical staff need to read it and check
site work against it. Our projects involve ICAO Annex 14 and FAA AC 150 compliant work, and each project's own
specification states which requirements apply.

#### CCR Airport Lighting India, Cable and Connector Skills

On CCR airport lighting India projects, the constant current regulator feeds the series lighting circuit, so
technicians need to understand CCR output, circuit behaviour and testing. Airport lighting cable India work
covers laying, identifying, terminating and testing the cabling. Airport lighting connector India work covers
making and checking connectors and their sealing. A poor termination or connector can affect a whole circuit,
so these skills matter.

#### Airport Lighting Tender India, Project India and Commissioning India

An airport lighting tender India process is how an airport or its main contractor invites bids for lighting
work, and people who can read tender documents and technical schedules are useful on both the bidding and
delivery sides. An airport lighting project India then moves through design, installation, testing and airport
lighting commissioning India, where each circuit and the system as a whole are tested and documented before
acceptance.

#### AGL Engineer Jobs India and AGL Technician Jobs India

AGL engineer jobs India centre on testing, photometry, supervision, design support and compliance
documentation. AGL technician jobs India centre on installation, alignment, cabling and maintenance on site.
Airport lighting training India is mostly learned on live sites with mentorship, backed by study of
photometry, CCR systems, isolating transformers and ICAO/FAA compliance; the Precision AGL Academy on this
site is a place to study.

# CAREER & CERTIFICATION GUIDANCE IN AIRFIELD GROUND LIGHTING

Airfield Ground Lighting is a specialised field within airport electrical and airside infrastructure. It
combines electrical engineering, airport operations, visual guidance, lighting technology, safety, testing,
maintenance and aviation standards. This guide shows the career paths, skills, training options and
preparation steps to build expertise in it.

## WHO CAN BUILD A CAREER IN AGL?

AGL is not limited to one educational background. A strong foundation in electrical systems helps, but
practical AGL knowledge comes from understanding how the complete airfield lighting system works.
