## HOW TO PREPARE FOR AN AGL INTERVIEW

Do not prepare only by memorising definitions. Be ready to explain how a system works, identify a fault,
interpret a test result or describe how you would approach an airport project.

### Troubleshooting: “One runway light is not working. What will you do?”

Don’t answer “replace the light.” Show engineering thinking:

- Confirm the symptom

- Identify the circuit

- Check whether other fixtures are affected

- Check transformer and connector connections

- Take electrical measurements safely

- Trace the fault systematically

- Identify the failed component

- Rectify the cause

- Test the circuit again

- Document the result

### Structure every answer

- Definition : what it is

- Function : what it does

- Application : where it is used

- Technical principle : how it works

- Practical example : a field case

- Safety / standards : where relevant

### Scenario drills

- Complete circuit unavailable: CCR → cable → connectors → transformers → fixtures

- One fixture out: fixture, secondary connection, transformer, local wiring

- Several fixtures out: series circuit, primary cable, connector, CCR, common issue

- Lights work but photometry fails: alignment, condition, contamination, lamp/LED, geometry, measurement conditions, operating current

### Our Approach | Precision AGL Solutions

Canonical URL: https://rahulsharmaagl.in/our-approach.html

**Page summary:** How Precision AGL Solutions works — a systems approach connecting AGL engineering, testing, documentation and knowledge into one continuous lifecycle.

# A Systems Approach to Airfield Ground Lighting

Airfield Ground Lighting is not a collection of independent products. Precision AGL Solutions combines
technical understanding, structured procedures, testing, documentation, knowledge development and continuous
improvement into one connected approach.

## Understand the Complete System Before Solving the Individual Problem

A runway light depends on its circuit. A circuit depends on its CCR, cables and isolating transformers. A PAPI
depends on correct siting, alignment and verification. A testing result depends on the right procedure and
accurate measurement. A maintenance decision depends on inspection, failure history and documentation.

## From Components to Complete Systems

We do not look at an AGL component in isolation — we look at how it fits into the complete airport lighting
system. The same systems thinking applies to how we structure documentation and knowledge.

This is the foundation behind our connected AGL resource ecosystem.

## Understand → Assess → Engineer → Verify → Deliver

#### Understand

- Project objective

- Airport environment

- Existing infrastructure

- Technical requirements

- Operational requirements

#### Assess

- System & equipment review

- Site inspection

- Drawing & documentation review

- Testing & photometric measurement

- Compliance review & fault investigation

#### Engineer

- System architecture & AGL layouts

- Equipment selection & circuit planning

- Cable & transformer considerations

- CCR & PAPI / visual aid requirements

- Testing methodology & maintenance strategy

#### Verify

- Inspection & measurement

- Electrical testing & photometry

- Functional verification

- Documentation review

- Compliance checks

#### Deliver

- Technical & inspection reports

- Photometry reports & test records

- Compliance documentation

- SOPs & checklists

- Training material & technical support

Design tells us what should happen. Testing tells us what is happening.

## We Do Not Let Knowledge Stay in One Document

A solution to one problem can become reusable knowledge — reflected throughout the AGL Knowledge Hub.

## The AGL Topic Architecture

Our approach connects resources around individual AGL topics. Take, for example: Isolating Transformer.

This is what we mean by connected AGL knowledge.

## Standards Are a Starting Point, Not the Entire Answer

AGL projects frequently involve multiple technical references. Our approach is to understand the applicable
requirement first and then connect it to the actual engineering application — moving from requirement, to
engineering meaning, to implementation, testing and documentation.

The Standards Companion connects ICAO, FAA, IS and related requirements with practical engineering
interpretation. Explore the Standards Companion →

### ICAO Approach Lighting System

The approach lighting system is a good example of how we treat a standard. ICAO Annex 14 is the starting point
for the approach lighting required for a runway, and the configuration that applies depends on the runway
type, the operational category and the airport's approved design.

We then move from that requirement to its engineering meaning, covering layout, series circuits and CCR
loading, and on to installation, testing and documentation. Always confirm the requirement against the current
edition of Annex 14. Approach Lighting Systems →

### Approach Lighting System Diagram

The same chain applied to approach lighting runs in this order:

- Requirement from the approved approach lighting configuration

- Layout drawing, with elevation, azimuth and aiming of the fixtures

- Series circuit and CCR arrangement

- Installation, then electrical and photometric testing

- Test report and documentation

Each step is covered on the Approach Lighting Systems page.

## Measure. Record. Interpret. Verify.

Testing should not be treated as an isolated activity at the end of a project — our technical framework
connects testing resources with inspection, maintenance, troubleshooting and documentation.

## Symptom → Measurement → Diagnosis → Root Cause → Corrective Action

Troubleshooting should be systematic. This philosophy forms the basis of the AGL Troubleshooting Atlas and AGL
Failure Database.

What is actually happening?

What technical conditions could create that symptom?

What can be tested or measured to narrow the possibilities?

What does the evidence indicate?

What actually created the failure?

Repair, replace, adjust or otherwise address the cause.

Confirm the system has returned to the required condition.

## Engineering Should Be Traceable

A technical activity is incomplete when its result cannot be understood later. We value structured
documentation across every stage of a project.

## Maintain the System, Not Just the Failure

Our approach extends beyond corrective repair, connecting daily inspection and maintenance with longer-term
asset management — and connecting theory with real engineering application.

What is it? → How does it work? → Where is it used? → How is it tested? → How is it maintained? → How is it
troubleshot? → How can it be improved?

Explore Precision AGL Academy →

# THE AGL SPECIALIST

I am an Airfield Ground Lighting (AGL) Specialist and AGL Photometry Specialist with over 6 years of
experience in airport lighting systems, AGL photometry, testing, technical compliance, project execution, and
airport electrical infrastructure. I specialize in understanding AGL systems not only from an equipment and
installation perspective, but through their actual field performance, photometric characteristics, testing
requirements, and standards compliance.

## AGL Engineering

I work across the complete Airfield Ground Lighting engineering cycle — from initial design through to long-
term compliance.

Understanding system architecture, equipment selection, technical specifications, BOQs and project
requirements.

#### AGL Photometry

Photometric testing, beam alignment, intensity verification, chromaticity evaluation, analysis and compliance
reporting.

#### Electrical Testing

Testing and evaluation of AGL equipment, including isolation transformers, series circuits and associated
electrical systems.

Supporting inspection, testing, commissioning and performance verification of airport lighting systems.

#### Standards & Compliance

Working with applicable ICAO, FAA, IS and airport-specific technical requirements for AGL systems.

Understanding failures through symptoms, measurements, system analysis, root-cause identification and
corrective action.

project documentation.

## Understand the Complete System

## Our key achievements

Thirteen resources, each built to stand on its own and to connect with the others.

### AGL SOP Library

Turning experience into repeatable procedures

We created the AGL SOP Library to organize practical procedures for AGL work. It focuses on structured
procedures covering testing, inspection, maintenance and operational activities.

### AGL Inspection Handbook

A structured inspection reference

Inspection is one of the most important parts of maintaining an airport lighting system. The handbook
organizes inspection knowledge into a structured reference, designed to support a systematic approach rather
than relying only on individual experience.

### AGL Maintenance Handbook

From reactive maintenance to structured maintenance

We developed the handbook as a dedicated knowledge layer for maintaining AGL infrastructure throughout its
service life. The goal is to transform maintenance information into a usable engineering reference.

### AGL Testing & Commissioning Manual

Making testing more systematic

Testing and commissioning require clear procedures, defined checks and proper documentation. The manual is a
technical reference for engineers and project teams working through the testing and handover stages of AGL
systems.

### AGL Component Library

A common language for AGL components

One of our core achievements. Instead of treating AGL equipment as a list of product names, the library
explains each component in terms of the wider system. It covers fixtures, CCRs, transformers, connectors and
other AGL components.

### AGL Standards Companion

Translating standards into engineering understanding

Standards can be difficult to use when they are viewed only as documents. The Companion connects them with
practical engineering meaning, so engineers can understand not only what a requirement says, but how it
relates to actual AGL work.

### AGL Troubleshooting Atlas

Problem, investigation, root cause, corrective action

We organized fault diagnosis around real engineering thinking. Instead of simply listing faults, the framework
follows a structured sequence, creating a practical bridge between technical knowledge and field problem-
solving.

### AGL Failure Database

Turning failures into engineering knowledge

Failures should not disappear after the immediate problem is solved. The database creates a structured layer
for recording and studying them, so individual problems become reusable engineering knowledge.

### AGL Engineering Forms & Templates

Converting engineering work into reusable documents

Good engineering also depends on good documentation. This system reduces repeated work and creates greater
consistency in technical documentation.

### AGL Glossary

A shared technical vocabulary

AGL contains hundreds of technical terms, abbreviations and specialist expressions. A common vocabulary makes
technical communication easier for students, engineers, technicians and aviation professionals.

### AGL Knowledge Quiz Center

From reading knowledge to testing knowledge

We wanted learning to go beyond passive reading. The Quiz Center introduces structured assessment across AGL
topics, helping users test their understanding and identify knowledge gaps.

### AGL Asset Lifecycle Guide

Looking beyond installation

An AGL system does not end when commissioning is complete. The guide extends the ecosystem beyond
installation, and the Knowledge Hub describes it as the strategic asset-management layer.

### AGL Innovation Hub

Building the next layer of AGL engineering

The Innovation Hub looks beyond today's systems. It creates a structured space for studying how technology may
influence the future of AGL engineering.

# One Connected Ecosystem for Airfield Ground Lighting

Precision AGL Ecosystem is a connected platform bringing together AGL engineering, technical knowledge,
learning, standards, tools, testing, operations, troubleshooting and continuous improvement. It is designed
around one simple principle: AGL knowledge should not exist as disconnected information.

AGL Knowledge Should Not Exist as Disconnected Information

A component should connect to its application. A system should connect to its standard. A standard should
connect to testing. Testing should connect to inspection. Inspection should connect to maintenance.
Maintenance should connect to troubleshooting. And every experience should contribute to better engineering
practice.

## Structured to Connect Every Area of AGL

Precision AGL is structured to connect the different areas required to understand, engineer, operate and
improve Airfield Ground Lighting systems.

### AGL Solutions

Technical solutions and professional engineering support for Airfield Ground Lighting and airport visual aids.

### AGL Knowledge Hub

A structured knowledge platform designed to make AGL information accessible, practical, connected and easier
to use — from fundamentals to testing, maintenance, troubleshooting and innovation.

### AGL Academy

A dedicated learning environment for developing practical knowledge and professional understanding of AGL —
connecting learning with real engineering subjects rather than isolated theory.

### Engineering & Field Practice

Knowledge becomes useful when it can be applied. The objective is a continuous connection between what an
engineer learns, what a technician performs, what a system requires, and what the field reveals.

### Standards & Compliance

Technical decisions need a standards foundation. The ecosystem brings standards-related information together
with engineering subjects for the right context.

### Testing, Inspection & Verification

Reliable AGL operation depends on verification — organizing what should be checked, how it should be checked,
what should be recorded, what the results mean, and what action may be required.

### Operations & Maintenance

An AGL system is not complete when installation ends. The ecosystem extends into operation and asset care.

Learn → Operate → Inspect → Diagnose → Maintain → Improve

### Engineering Tools & Documentation

Good engineering also requires good tools and documentation — making technical work more structured,
repeatable and easier to document.
